imposes a total order

\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}
with maximal chains given by the sequence of roots

\beta_{r}=\gamma(b_{r})=\gamma(\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}[1,r])
. Their explicit expressions in terms of simple roots
\alpha_{i}
and
\alpha_{j}
are as follows for Lie types
\mathsf{A}_{2}
,

\mathsf{B}_{2}
, and
\mathsf{G}_{2}
, respectively.

(2.33)

\displaystyle\mathsf{e}

\displaystyle=1\qquad

\displaystyle\alpha_{j}\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}\alpha_{i}+\alpha_{j}\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}\alpha_{i}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{12.80373pt}\mathsf{e}

\displaystyle=2\qquad

\displaystyle\alpha_{j}\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}\alpha_{i}+\alpha_{j}\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}2\alpha_{i}+\alpha_{j}\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}\alpha_{i}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{12.80373pt}\mathsf{e}

\displaystyle=3\qquad

\displaystyle\alpha_{j}\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}\alpha_{i}+\alpha_{j}\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}3\alpha_{i}+2\alpha_{j}\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}2\alpha_{i}+\alpha_{j}\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}3\alpha_{i}+\alpha_{j}\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}\alpha_{i}

By Corollary
2.9
and the fact that
\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}=\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}^{\dagger}

the total
\prec_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}}
order imposed by the other maximal reduced word
\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}
is exactly the opposite one.

Often questions for general Coxeter systems can be reduced to ones of rank 2 situations. This is illustrated in the following method of extracting from some
s\in\mathscr{W}
a maximal element
r\leq_{L}s
that belongs to such a subsystem. The proof here extends the argument used in the proof of Proposition 1.8 of
[
45
]
to also the non-simply laced Lie types.

Lemma 2.13
.

Suppose
s\in\mathscr{W}
and
1\leq i\leq n
are such that
l(s\cdot s_{i})=l(s)+1\geq 2\,
. Then there exists
j\neq i
,

t\in\mathscr{W}
and
y\in\mathscr{W}^{*}\mkern-4.0mu\raise-0.59998pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}
, such that for
r=\mathscr{r}(y)
we have

s=t\cdot r\;,\quad l(s)=l(t)+l(r)\;,\quad 1\leq l(r)<m\;,\quad t(\alpha_{i}),t(\alpha_{j})\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\;,\quad\mbox{and}\quad\tau(y)=j\,.

Moreover, if
s(\alpha_{i})=\alpha_{k}\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}
, then
r\cdot s_{i}=\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\,
so that
r(\alpha_{i})\in\{\alpha_{i},\alpha_{j}\}\,
and, hence, either
t(\alpha_{i})=\alpha_{k}
or
t(\alpha_{j})=\alpha_{k}
.

Proof.

If
u\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
with
\mathscr{r}(u)=s
we have by the first assumption that
u\cdot w_{i}
is reduced as well. Thus, by Lemma
2.2
, we have

\gamma(u\cdot w_{i})=s(\alpha_{i})\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\,
. Now let
j=\tau(u)
so that
s=s^{\prime}\cdot s_{j}
with
s^{\prime}=\mathscr{r}(u^{\flat})
. Therefore,

\gamma(u)=s^{\prime}(\alpha_{j})=-s^{\prime}(s_{j}(\alpha_{j}))=-s(\alpha_{j})\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
again by Lemma
2.2
, which implies

s(\alpha_{j})\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{-}}
and, hence,
j\neq i
.

Next, let
t\in\mathscr{W}
be an element of minimal length in the coset
\,s\cdot\mathscr{W}\mkern-4.0mu\raise-0.39993pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(ij)$}
. Since

s\cdot s_{j}=\mathscr{r}(u^{\flat})
we have
l(s\cdot s_{j})<l(s)
so that
l(t)<l(s)\,
and
l(r)\geq 1\,
.
Minimality of
t
further implies that
l(t\cdot s_{i})>l(t)
and
l(t\cdot s_{j})>l(t)\,
.
Thus, if
x\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
is a reduced word representing
t
also
x\cdot w_{i}
and
x\cdot w_{j}
are reduced, implying positivity of both
\gamma(x\cdot w_{i})=t(\alpha_{i})\,,\,\gamma(x\cdot w_{j})=t(\alpha_{j})\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\,
.

Since
\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(r)\subset\mathbb{N}_{0}\alpha_{i}+\mathbb{N}_{0}\alpha_{j}
this also implies that
t(\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(r))\subseteq{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
. By Corollary
2.4
we thus obtain that
l(s)=l(t)+l(r)\,
.

Observe further that
r(\alpha_{i})=n_{i}\alpha_{i}+n_{j}\alpha_{j}
with either both
n_{i},n_{j}>0
if
r(\alpha_{i})\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
or both
n_{i},n_{j}<0
if
r(\alpha_{i})\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{-}}
. The latter case is not possible since it would imply
s(\alpha_{i})=n_{i}t(\alpha_{i})+n_{j}t(\alpha_{j})\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{-}}\,
by the previous observation. Now,
r(\alpha_{i})\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
implies that a reduced word representing
r
ends in
w_{j}
and that
l(r)<m\,
.

Finally, the condition
s(\alpha_{i})=\alpha_{k}=n_{i}t(\alpha_{i})+n_{j}t(\alpha_{j})
implies that either
t(\alpha_{i})=\alpha_{k}
, with
(n_{i},n_{j})=(1,0)
and hence
r(\alpha_{i})=\alpha_{i}
, or

t(\alpha_{j})=\alpha_{k}
, with
(n_{i},n_{j})=(0,1)
and hence
r(\alpha_{i})=\alpha_{j}\,
. Given that
l(r)\geq 1
this now entails that
l(r)=m-1
so that
y\cdot w_{i}\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}\mkern-2.5mu\raise-0.59998pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}\,
.
∎

3.
Quantum Groups at Generic Parameter
q

We recall the standard definitions of quantum groups as defined, for example, in
[
37
,
16
]
. Various ground rings are introduced over which subalgebras and variants of the quantum groups can be defined. Throughout this section we fix a simple Lie algebra
\mathfrak{g}
with root system

\mathsf{\Phi}

and Cartan data
A_{ij}
as introduced in the previous section.

3.1.
Quantization Rings, Quantum Numbers, Integral Subrings

In their original definitions, such as in
[
25
]
, quantum groups are obtained as deformations of the universal enveloping algebra of a Lie algebra
\mathfrak{g}
along a formal parameter
\hbar\,
. The natural ground ring in this context is the ring of formal power series
\mathbb{Q}\lBrack\hbar\rBrack\,
, which contains
q=e^{\hbar}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n!}\hbar^{n}\,
. The parameter identification yields a ring embedding
\mathbb{Q}(q)^{1}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{Q}\lBrack\hbar\rBrack
, where
\mathbb{Q}(q)^{1}
denotes the subring of rational functions without poles at
q=1
. It extends to an embedding
\mathbb{Q}(q)\hookrightarrow\mathbb{Q}\lBrack\hbar\rBrack_{\hbar}
, where the localization
\mathbb{Q}\lBrack\hbar\rBrack_{\hbar}
is given by formal Laurent series with finite numbers of negative powers. We continue our discussion with various frequently used quantities and formulae in
\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]
.

For a positive root
\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
in the
\mathscr{W}
-orbit of
\alpha_{i}\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}
, let
d_{\alpha}=d_{i}
and
q_{\alpha}=q_{i}=q^{d_{i}}
. Given
a,b\in\mathbb{N}
, quantum numbers, factorials, and binomials are denoted with respect to this data as

(3.1)

\displaystyle[a]_{\alpha}=\dfrac{q_{\alpha}^{a}-q_{\alpha}^{-a}}{q_{\alpha}-q_{\alpha}^{-1}}\,,

\displaystyle[a]!_{\alpha}=\prod_{j=1}^{a}\dfrac{q^{j}_{\alpha}-q^{-j}_{\alpha}}{q_{\alpha}-q^{-1}_{\alpha}}\,,

and

\displaystyle\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$a+b$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
a\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{\alpha}=\dfrac{[a+b]!_{\alpha}}{[a]!_{\alpha}[b]!_{\alpha}}\,,

all of which are valued in
\mathbb{Z}[q_{\alpha},q^{-1}_{\alpha}]\subseteq\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]\,
. The subscript
\alpha
is suppressed if
q_{\alpha}=q
, meaning
d_{i}=d_{\alpha}=1
. We will frequently also use the abbreviation
[n]_{i}=[n]_{\alpha_{i}}
for simple roots and analogous notation for factorials and binomial coefficients. The binomial recursion below is easily verified and frequently used.

(3.2)

\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n+1$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
t\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{\alpha}=q_{\alpha}^{\pm t}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
t\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{\alpha}+q_{\alpha}^{\mp(n+1-t)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
t-1\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{\alpha}

The
q
-binomial coefficients arise naturally in the
respective binomial formula for
q
-commuting generators. Specifically,
assume the algebra
\mathcal{H}_{q}
over
\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]
is generated by
U
and
V
subject to the relation
VU=q^{2}UV
.
Then the following is easily
proved by induction,

(3.3)

(U+V)^{a}\,=\,\sum_{k=0}^{a}q^{-k(a-k)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$a$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
k\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}U^{k}V^{a-k}\,=\,\sum_{k=0}^{a}q^{k(a-k)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$a$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
k\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}V^{k}U^{a-k}\,.

Adjoining an inverse
V^{-1}
to
\mathcal{H}_{q}
and multiplying (
3.3
) by
V^{-a}
from the right one readily obtains, after the substitution
z=V^{-1}U
, the following variant of Gauss’s formula,

(3.4)

\sum_{k=0}^{a}q^{-k(a+1)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$a$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
k\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}z^{k}\,=\,\prod_{t=1}^{a}(q^{-2t}z+1)\,=\,q^{-\binom{a+1}{2}}\prod_{t=1}^{a}(q^{t}+q^{-t}z)\,.

For convenience in later computations we express ratios of factorials for different root lengths
d_{j}\in\{1,2,3\}
as

(3.5)

\frac{[d_{j}k]!}{[k]!_{j}}\,=\,[d_{j}]^{k}\cdot[k\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mud_{j}]\mkern-1.6mu{\rotatebox[origin]{180.0}{!}}\mkern-1.6mu{\rotatebox[origin]{180.0}{!}}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\frac{[k]!_{j}}{[k]!}\,=\,[d_{j}]^{-k}\cdot\left\{k\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mud_{j}\right\}\,,

where we use the following notation for elements in
\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]
,

(3.6)

[k\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu\mathsf{e}]\mkern-1.6mu{\rotatebox[origin]{180.0}{!}}\mkern-1.6mu{\rotatebox[origin]{180.0}{!}}\,=\,\prod_{s=0}^{k-1}\prod_{t=1}^{\mathsf{e}-1}[s\mathsf{e}+t]\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\left\{k\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu\mathsf{e}\right\}\,=\,\prod_{s=1}^{k}\frac{q^{\mathsf{e}s}-q^{-\mathsf{e}s}}{q^{s}-q^{-s}}\,.

Note that
[k\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu1]\mkern-1.6mu{\rotatebox[origin]{180.0}{!}}\mkern-1.6mu{\rotatebox[origin]{180.0}{!}}=1=\left\{k\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu1\right\}
for all
k\in\mathbb{N}\,
. On occasion, we will also use notation for quantum multinomial coefficients in
\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]
given by

(3.7)

\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$a_{1}+a_{2}+\ldots+a_{r}$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
a_{1}\,,\,a_{2}\,,\,\ldots\,,\,a_{r}\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{\alpha}=\frac{[a_{1}+a_{2}+\ldots+a_{r}]!_{\alpha}}{[a_{1}]!_{\alpha}[a_{2}]!_{\alpha}\ldots[a_{r}]!_{\alpha}}=\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$a_{1}+\ldots+a_{r}$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
a_{r}\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{\alpha}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$a_{1}+\ldots+a_{r-1}$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
a_{r-1}\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{\alpha}\ldots\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$a_{1}+a_{2}$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
a_{2}\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{\alpha}\,.

Concluding, we introduce the following notation for subrings of
\mathbb{Q}(q)\,
, over which various versions of quantum groups can be defined. Clearly, all of these are integral domains and have
\mathbb{Q}(q)
as a common field of fractions. However, as opposed to
\mathbb{Q}(q)\,
, they have well-defined specializations to roots of unity of large enough orders.

(3.8)

\displaystyle\Lambda_{q}

\displaystyle=\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]

\displaystyle\Lambda_{q,n}=\mathbb{Z}\textstyle{\left[q,q^{-1},\frac{1}{[n-1]!}\right]}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{19.91692pt}\Lambda_{q}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}

\displaystyle=\mathbb{Z}\textstyle{\left[{q,q^{-1},\frac{1}{q-q^{-1}}}\right]}

\displaystyle\Lambda_{q,n}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}=\mathbb{Z}\textstyle{\left[q,q^{-1},\frac{1}{q-q^{-1}},\frac{1}{[n-1]!}\right]}

3.2.
Quantum Group Generators and Relations

For Cartan data as above, the quantum universal enveloping algebra
U_{\hbar}(\mathfrak{g})
is defined in
[
25
,
16
]
as the algebra over
\mathbb{Q}\lBrack\hbar\rBrack
topologically generated by elements
E_{i},F_{i},H_{i}
for
1\leq i\leq n
subject to relations

(3.9)

\displaystyle[H_{i},H_{j}]=0\,,

\displaystyle[E_{i},F_{j}]=\delta_{ij}\dfrac{e^{d_{i}\hbar H_{i}}-e^{-d_{i}\hbar H_{i}}}{q_{i}-q_{i}^{-1}}\,,

(3.10)

\displaystyle[H_{i},E_{j}]=A_{ij}E_{j}\,,

\displaystyle[H_{i},F_{j}]=-A_{ij}F_{j}\,,

(3.11)

\displaystyle\sum_{r+s=1-A_{ij}}(-1)^{s}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$1-A_{ij}$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
s\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{i}E_{i}^{r}E_{j}E_{i}^{s}=0\quad(\text{for }i\neq j)\,,

(3.12)

\displaystyle\sum_{r+s=1-A_{ij}}(-1)^{s}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$1-A_{ij}$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
s\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{i}F_{i}^{r}F_{j}F_{i}^{s}=0\quad(\text{for }i\neq j)\,.

Although (
3.9
) and the other relations are well-defined over
\mathbb{Q}\lBrack\hbar\rBrack
we extend the ground ring of
U_{\hbar}(\mathfrak{g})
to
\mathbb{Q}\lBrack\hbar\rBrack_{\hbar}\,
for convenience. If we denote as usual
K_{i}=e^{d_{i}\hbar H_{i}}
the above imply the following relations:

(3.13)

\displaystyle K_{i}K_{j}=K_{j}K_{i}\,,

\displaystyle[E_{i},F_{j}]=\delta_{ij}\dfrac{K_{i}-K_{i}^{-1}}{q_{i}-q_{i}^{-1}}\,,

(3.14)

\displaystyle K_{i}E_{j}K_{i}^{-1}=q_{i}^{A_{ij}}E_{j}=q^{\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{j}\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{j})}{(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{j})}{(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{j})}}E_{j}\,,

\displaystyle K_{i}F_{j}K_{i}^{-1}=q_{i}^{-A_{ij}}F_{j}=q^{-\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{j}\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{j})}{(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{j})}{(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{j})}}F_{j}\,.

Observing
(q_{i}-q_{i}^{-1})=(q-q^{-1})[d_{i}]\,
, we note that all relations (
3.11
-
3.14
) are indeed over
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
where
{\mathsf{e}^{*}}\in\{2,3,4\}
is as in (
2.3
) and we view
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\subset\mathbb{Q}(q)\subset\mathbb{Q}\lBrack\hbar\rBrack_{\hbar}\,
. We thus define
U_{q}(\mathfrak{g})
as the
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
-algebra generated by the elements
\{E_{i},F_{i},K_{i}:1\leq i\leq n\}
and subject to relations (
3.11
-
3.14
). If
\mathfrak{g}
is a general simple Lie algebra or its type is clear from context, we will usually write
U_{q}
instead.

Additionally, we denote by
U_{q}^{+}
the subalgebra generated by only the
E_{i}
,
U_{q}^{-}
the subalgebra generated by only the
F_{i}
, which may be considered as algebras over the subring
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
of
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
. The algebra
U_{q}^{0}
generated by only the
K_{i}
may be considered over
\Lambda_{q}
. Further, we set
U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}=U_{q}^{+}U_{q}^{0}
and
U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}=U_{q}^{-}U_{q}^{0}
the respective subalgebras obtained from two sets of generators, which we also take to be defined over
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\,
by default.

Suppose
\,f\!:\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\rightarrow\Lambda
or
\,f^{\,\,{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}\!:\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\rightarrow\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
is a ring homomorphism where
\Lambda
or
\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
is commutative with unit. We may define quantum algebras over ground rings
\Lambda
or
\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
by respective extensions of scalars of the original algebras, viewed as
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
or
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
modules. Specifically, for any
\,{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\in\{+,-,0,{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\}\,
we denote

(3.15)

U_{q,\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.74861pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}}=f^{\,\,{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}_{!}U_{q}=U_{q}\otimes_{\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.74861pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad U_{q,\Lambda}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}=f_{!}U_{q}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}=U_{q}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\otimes_{\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}}\Lambda\,.

The further abbreviated notation
U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}
and
U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
is used for algebras over
\mathbb{Q}(q)
derived from the inclusions of
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
and
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
in
\mathbb{Q}(q)
. Similarly, for
m\geq{\mathsf{e}^{*}}
we write

U_{q,m}
and
U_{q,m}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
for the inclusions of
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
and
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
in
\Lambda_{q,m}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
and
\Lambda_{q,m}\,
, respectively. That is, the ground rings of
U_{q,m}
and
U_{q,m}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}

contain also elements
\frac{1}{[m-1]!}
.

It is easy to see that the free abelian group algebra
\Lambda_{q}[\{K_{i}^{\pm 1}\}]
embeds in the polynomial algebra
\mathbb{Q}\lBrack\hbar\rBrack_{\hbar}[\{H_{i}\}]
via
K_{i}\mapsto e^{d_{i}\hbar H_{i}}\,
. Using the PBW results below and in
[
65
,
16
]
it further follows that the respective algebra homomorphism
U_{q}\rightarrow U_{\hbar}(\mathfrak{g})
is injective.

An important variant of quantum groups at roots of unity are Lusztig’s divided power algebras
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}
, see
[
47
,
45
,
46
]
. They are defined as the
\Lambda_{q}
-subalgebras of
U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}
generated by elements
E_{i}^{(k)}=\frac{1}{[k]!_{i}}E_{i}^{k}
and
F_{i}^{(k)}=\frac{1}{[k]!_{i}}F_{i}^{k}
as well as certain additional rational expressions in the
K_{i}
generators.

We denote the respective subalgebras by
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{+}
,
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{-}
, and
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{0}\,
. Although they are not discussed explicitly in this paper, we will refer to these algebras in some of the proofs below as we adopt arguments from
[
45
,
46
,
47
]
.

3.3.
Hopf Algebra Structures

Coalgebra structures on
U_{\hbar}(\mathfrak{g})
and
U_{q}
are given by requiring
K_{i}
to be group-like,
H_{i}
to be primitive, and
E_{i}
and
F_{i}
to be
skew-primitives
via the co-relations

(3.16)

\displaystyle\Delta(E_{i})

\displaystyle=E_{i}\otimes K_{i}+1\otimes E_{i}

and

\displaystyle\Delta(F_{i})

\displaystyle=F_{i}\otimes 1+K_{i}^{-1}\otimes F_{i}\,.

In this sense we have that the inclusions of the quantum algebras above, such as
U^{\geq 0}_{q}\hookrightarrow U_{q}\hookrightarrow U_{\hbar}(\mathfrak{g})\,
, are inclusions of Hopf algebras. A counit is given by

\varepsilon(E_{i})=\varepsilon(F_{i})=\varepsilon(H_{i})=0
and
\varepsilon(K_{i})=1
. For later computations we also record here the coproducts for powers of generators, which easily follow from (
3.14
) and (
3.16
).

(3.17)

\displaystyle\Delta(E_{i}^{m})

\displaystyle=\sum_{s=0}^{m}q_{i}^{-s(m-s)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{m}$}\\
\scriptstyle{s}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}_{i}E_{i}^{s}\otimes K_{i}^{s}E_{i}^{m-s}

\displaystyle\Delta(F_{i}^{m})

\displaystyle=\sum_{s=0}^{m}q_{i}^{-s(m-s)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{m}$}\\
\scriptstyle{s}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}_{i}K_{i}^{-s}F_{i}^{m-s}\otimes F_{i}^{s}

The antipode acts on the Cartan generators as
S(K_{i})=K_{i}^{-1}
and
S(H_{i})=-H_{i}
and is given on the other generators as

(3.18)

\displaystyle S(E_{i})

\displaystyle=-E_{i}K_{i}^{-1}=-q_{i}^{2}K_{i}^{-1}E_{i}

and

\displaystyle S(F_{i})

\displaystyle=-K_{i}F_{i}=-q_{i}^{-2}F_{i}K_{i}\,.

Again, it will be useful to also state the antipode of powers of generators.

(3.19)

\displaystyle S(E_{i}^{m})

\displaystyle=(-1)^{m}q_{i}^{-m(m-1)}E_{i}^{m}K_{i}^{-m}

\displaystyle S(F_{i}^{m})

\displaystyle=(-1)^{m}q_{i}^{m(m-1)}K_{i}^{m}F_{i}^{m}\,.

Clearly,
U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
and
U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
form Hopf subalgebras of
U_{q}
, and
U_{q}^{0}=\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}[\{K_{i}^{\pm}\}]
is isomorphic as a Hopf algebra to the group algebra of
\mathbb{Z}^{n}\,
.

Recall
[
69
,
52
,
61
]
that a coalgebra
C
over a field
\mathbb{k}
is called
pointed
if all its (co)simple subcoalgebras are 1-dimensional or, equivalently, if its coradical
C_{0}
coincides with the subcoalgebra
\mathbb{k}[Gr(C)]
of group-like elements. Pointed coalgebras and Hopf algebras have been extensively studied, though most results assume the ground ring to be a field.

Suppose
\mathbb{k}
is a field and
\vartheta:\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\rightarrow\mathbb{k}\,
a ring homomorphism. As noted in (
3.15
), this yields quantum algebras
U_{q,\mathbb{k}}
and
U_{q,\mathbb{k}}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}
over the field
\mathbb{k}
for any
{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\in\{0,{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\}\,
. Besides the case
\mathbb{k}=\mathbb{Q}(q)
given by the obvious inclusions, the following result will also be of interest in the case of a cyclotomic field
\mathbb{k}=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)
.

Proposition 3.1

(
[
53
, Theorem 2.2]
)
.

The Hopf algebras
U_{q,\mathbb{k}}\,
,
U_{q,\mathbb{k}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\,
, and
U_{q,\mathbb{k}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\,
as defined above are pointed. Their common coradical is
U_{q,\mathbb{k}}^{0}\,
.

The proof uses coalgebra filtrations
\{A_{n}\}
of the quantum algebras, where
A_{0}=U_{q,\mathbb{k}}^{0}
. Set
A_{1}=A_{0}\oplus\sum_{i}^{\oplus}E_{i}A_{0}\oplus F_{i}A_{0}\,
for
U_{q,\mathbb{k}}\,

as well as
A_{1}=A_{0}\oplus\sum_{i}^{\oplus}E_{i}A_{0}
for
U_{q,\mathbb{k}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\,
and analogous for
U_{q,\mathbb{k}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\,
. The subspaces are then given as
A_{n}=(A_{1})^{n}\,
, which clearly exhaust the entire algebra. Lemma 5.3.4 in
[
53
]
, for example, now implies that
C_{0}
is contained in and thus equal to

U_{q,\mathbb{k}}^{0}\,
. Pointedness now follows immediately from
C_{0}=U_{q,\mathbb{k}}^{0}\,
, which is then also equal to the total subcoalgebra spanned by group-like elements.

4.
Gradings and Automorphisms on Quantum Groups

Several automorphisms and anti-automorphsisms will play an important role in constructions throughout this paper. They include, besides the antipode, Lusztig’s Artin group actions, involutions, and Che transformations. Additionally, we will refer to two types of gradings in several of our later the proofs. This section will collect basic properties of these automorphisms and gradings as well as establish various useful relations between them.

4.1.
Gradings

Recall that a grading of an algebra
A
by a monoid
G
entails a decomposition
A=\oplus_{g\in G}A_{g}
with
A_{g}\cdot A_{h}\subseteq A_{gh}\,
. We call elements
b\in A_{g}\setminus\{0\}
for some
g\in G

homogeneous
with respect to such a given grading. If
A
is defined in terms of generators and relations, a grading on the free algebra of generators descends to
A
if the relations are homogeneous elements.
Let
G
be a monoid and
S
any set.
In the following discussion, we write
G^{S}
to mean interchangeably additive combinations
\sum_{s\in S}c_{s}s
as well as maps
c:S\rightarrow G\,:\,s\mapsto c_{s}\,
.

A grading in
G=\mathbb{N}_{0}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
with
\mathbb{N}_{0}=\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}
on the algebra
U_{q}^{+}
is given by defining

(U_{q}^{+})_{\mu}
as the subspace spanned by
E_{i_{1}}\ldots E_{i_{m}}
such that
\mu=\sum_{s=1}^{m}\alpha_{i_{s}}\in\mathbb{N}_{0}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\,
. It is clear that the relations in (
3.11
)-(
3.14
) are homogeneous with respect to this grading, which is therefore well-defined on
U_{q}^{+}
. For a homogeneous element
b\in(U_{q}^{+})_{\mu}
we sometimes also write
\mathbb{w}^{+}(b)=\mu
.

An analogous grading in
\mathbb{N}_{0}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
is given on
U_{q}^{-}
by the function

\mathbb{w}^{-}
from the set of homogeneous elements in
U_{q}^{-}
to
\mathbb{N}_{0}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
.
These extend to a
\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
grading on
U_{q}
with
(U_{q})_{\mu}
spanned by
elements
K_{j_{1}}\ldots K_{j_{k}}E^{\epsilon_{1}}_{i_{1}}\ldots E^{\epsilon_{m}}_{i_{m}}
with
\mu=\sum_{s=1}^{m}\epsilon_{s}\alpha_{i_{s}}\,
where
E_{i}^{+}=E_{i}
and
E_{i}^{-}=F_{i}\,
, observing that both sides of the relation for
[E_{i},F_{j}]
are in
(U_{q})_{\alpha_{i}-\alpha_{j}}\,
. For a homogeneous element
a\in(U_{q})_{\mu}
with respect to this weight grading we also write
\mathbb{w}(a)=\mu\,

Thus, if
b\in U_{q}^{+}
and
c\in U_{q}^{-}
are homogeneous elements we have
\mathbb{w}(bc)=\mathbb{w}(cb)=\mathbb{w}^{+}(b)-\mathbb{w}^{-}(c)
, which readily implies, for example

(U_{q}^{+})_{\mu_{1}}\cdot(U_{q}^{-})_{\mu_{2}}\subseteq(U_{q})_{\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}}
.

For an element

\nu=\sum_{i}c_{i}\alpha_{i}\,\in\,\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\,
in the root lattice, we denote a basis element of
U_{q}^{0}
by

(4.1)

K^{\nu}=K_{1}^{c_{1}}\ldots K_{n}^{c_{n}}\;.

Suppose
b\in U_{q}
is homogeneous with
\mu=\mathbb{w}(b)\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
. It is easy to derive the following commutation relation,
where the inner form
\mathchoice{\left(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,\right)}{(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,)}{(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,)}{(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,)}
is naturally extended to a biadditive form on
\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\supset\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\,
,

(4.2)

K^{\nu}b=q^{\mathchoice{\left(\nu|\mathbb{w}(b)\right)}{(\nu|\mathbb{w}(b))}{(\nu|\mathbb{w}(b))}{(\nu|\mathbb{w}(b))}}bK^{\nu}\,.

Additional gradings in
\mathbb{F}_{2}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\,
, where
\mathbb{F}_{2}=\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}=\{0,1\}\,
, are artifacts of the
q\leftrightharpoons q^{-1}
-symmetric definition of quantum numbers and Cartan elements for quantum groups. Two such gradings are defined on generators as follows:

(4.3)

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{+}(E_{i})

\displaystyle=\alpha_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{+}(K_{i})

\displaystyle=\alpha_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{+}(F_{i})=0\,,

(4.4)

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{-}(E_{i})

\displaystyle=0\,,

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{-}(K_{i})

\displaystyle=\alpha_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{-}(F_{i})=\alpha_{i}\,.

As before, it is easy to check that relations (
3.11
)-(
3.14
) are homogeneous with respect to both
\mathbb{o}^{+}
and
\mathbb{o}^{-}
, which are thus well-defined on
U_{q}
. For example,
\mathbb{o}^{+}(E_{i}F_{i})=\mathbb{o}^{+}(F_{i}E_{i})=\mathbb{o}^{+}(K_{i})=\mathbb{o}^{+}(K_{i}^{-1})=\alpha_{i}
over
\mathbb{F}_{2}
in the case of relation (
3.13
). We also note the following interactions of the antipode with these gradings, when evaluated on homogeneous elements:

(4.5)

\displaystyle\mathbb{w}\circ S

\displaystyle=\mathbb{w}\,,

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{+}\circ S

\displaystyle=\mathbb{o}^{-}\,,

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{-}\circ S

\displaystyle=\mathbb{o}^{+}\,.

Although the gradings are related by
\,\mathbb{o}^{+}-\mathbb{o}^{-}=\mathbb{w}\mod 2
, it is useful to denote them separately.
Combining
\mathbb{w}
with either
\mathbb{o}^{+}
or
\mathbb{o}^{-}
yields a grading in
(\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{F}_{2})^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
that provides a refinement of the usual weight decomposition, splitting summands further according to respective multi-parities of Cartan elements in the sense that
\mathbb{o}^{+}(K^{\nu})=\nu\mod 2\,
.

For a discussion of the behavior of the coproduct with respect to these gradings denote by
U
any of the Hopf algebras
U_{q}
,
U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
and
U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
. For
\mu\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
and
\eta\in\mathbb{F}_{2}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
write also
U_{\mu}
and
U^{\eta}
for the graded components for
\mathbb{w}
and
\mathbb{o}^{+}
respectively. The algebra
U\otimes U
thus assumes natural bi-gradings with

(U\otimes U)_{(\mu_{1},\mu_{2})}=U_{\mu_{1}}\otimes U_{\mu_{2}}
and

(U\otimes U)^{(\eta_{1},\eta_{2})}=U^{\eta_{1}}\otimes U^{\eta_{2}}
. A simple verification on generators now yields

(4.6)

\Delta(U_{\mu})\subseteq\sum_{\nu}U_{\mu-\nu}\otimes U_{\nu}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\Delta(U^{\eta})\subseteq U\otimes U^{\eta}\,.

Finally, let
b\in(U_{q}^{+})_{\mu}
and
c\in(U_{q}^{-})_{-\nu}
be
\mathbb{w}
-homogeneous elements with
\mu,\nu\in\mathbb{N}_{0}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
. It follows from an easy inductive verification on generators
E_{i_{1}}\ldots E_{i_{k}}
and
F_{j_{1}}\ldots F_{j_{m}}\,
that
the
(\mu,0)
and
(0,\mu)
graded components of
\Delta(b)
as well as the
(-\nu,0)
and
(0,-\nu)
graded components of

\Delta(c)
have the form

(4.7)

\Delta(b)=b\otimes K^{\mu}+\,\ldots\,+1\otimes b\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\Delta(c)=c\otimes 1+\,\ldots\,+K^{-\nu}\otimes c\,.

4.2.
Che Transformations and Anti-Involutions

A basic family of automorphisms can be obtained by multiplying the step generators by Cartan elements and units subject to certain consistency conditions. The main data characterizing such a

Che
(

Ch
)
transformation
is a

\mathsf{\Phi}

-symmetric map
\mathsfit h\in{\mathbb{S}}(\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}})
as introduced in Section
2.6
.

Additionally, assume a homomorphism
u:\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\rightarrow\Lambda^{\star}
from the root lattice to the multiplicative subgroup of units
\Lambda^{\star}=\{\pm q^{k}:k\in\mathbb{Z}\}
of the ground ring. We define a map
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}
on generators as follows:

(4.8)

\displaystyle\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}(E_{i})

\displaystyle=u(\alpha_{i})K^{\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})}E_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}(F_{i})

\displaystyle=u(\alpha_{i})^{-1}F_{i}K^{-\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})}\,,

\displaystyle\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}(K_{i})

\displaystyle=K_{i}\,.

The next proposition establishes the existence and basic properties of these automorphisms. As before,
U_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
may be
U_{q}
,
U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
, or
U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
defined over the respective minimal ground rings.
The
q
-exponent in the formula in
iii)
is integral by Lemma
2.11
, so that the
q
-term is well-defined by

iv)
of the same lemma.

Proposition 4.1
.

Let
\mathsfit h,\mathsfit k\in{\mathbb{S}}(\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}})
and

u,v\in\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}},\Lambda^{\star})
as above. Then the following hold.

i)

The map
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}
defined in (
4.8
) extends uniquely to an automorphism of
U_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
.

ii)

\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}\circ\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit k}_{v}=\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h+\mathsfit k}_{u\cdot v}\,
, and

\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{0}_{1}
is identity, where
1
is the constant map to
1\in\Lambda^{\star}\,
.

iii)

If
b
is a homogeneous element with grading
\beta=\mathbb{w}(b)

we have

\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}(b)=u(\beta)q^{-\frac{1}{2}(\mathchoice{\left(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta)\right)}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)})}K^{\mathsfit h(\beta)}b\;.

iv)

With
b
as above, the action on gradings is
\mathbb{w}\circ\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}=\mathbb{w}
and
\mathbb{o}^{+}(\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}(b))=\mathbb{o}^{+}(b)+\mathsfit h(\beta)\mod 2\,
.

Proof.

Consider the algebra
L_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
with the same generators as
U_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
but subject only to the relations (
3.14
) in addition to those for
U_{q}^{0}\cong\Lambda[\{K_{i}^{\pm 1}\}]\,
.
L_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
admits the same gradings as
U_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
, and commutation of the
K_{i}
in
L_{q}^{0}\subset L_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
implies that
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}
is well-defined on
L_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
. We next prove that

iii)
holds on
L_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
by induction in the number of
E_{i}
and
F_{i}
generators in an expression for
b\,
. Since
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}
acts trivially on
U_{q}^{0}
we may omit any additional
K_{i}
factors in
b\,
.

For
b=E_{i}
and
\beta=\alpha_{i}
the
q
-exponent is zero because of
(
2.29
) so that the expression is the same as in (
4.8
). For
b=F_{i}
and
\beta=-\alpha_{i}
use

u(-\alpha_{i})=u(\alpha_{i})^{-1}\,
,
\mathsfit h(-\alpha_{i})=-\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})\,
, and

\mathchoice{\left(-\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(-\alpha_{i})\right)}{(-\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(-\alpha_{i}))}{(-\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(-\alpha_{i}))}{(-\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(-\alpha_{i}))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|-\alpha_{i}\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|-\alpha_{i})}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|-\alpha_{i})}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|-\alpha_{i})}=2\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}
again by (
2.29
).

For the induction step, we compute the formula for
E_{i}b
with
\mathbb{w}(E_{i}b)=\alpha_{i}+\beta
assuming the asserted expressions for
E_{i}
and
b
and using the fact that
u
and
\mathsfit h
are homomorphisms,

\displaystyle\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}(E_{i}b)

\displaystyle=\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}(E_{i})\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}(b)

\displaystyle=u(\alpha_{i})u(\beta)q^{-\frac{1}{2}(\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i})}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i})}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i})})}q^{-\frac{1}{2}(\mathchoice{\left(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta)\right)}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)})}K^{\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})}E_{i}K^{\mathsfit h(\beta)}b

\displaystyle=u(\alpha_{i}+\beta)q^{-\frac{1}{2}(\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}+\mathchoice{\left(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta)\right)}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta)})}q^{-\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta)\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta))}}K^{\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})}K^{\mathsfit h(\beta)}E_{i}b

\displaystyle=u(\alpha_{i}+\beta)q^{-\frac{1}{2}(\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}+2\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta)\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta))}+\mathchoice{\left(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta)\right)}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\beta))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta)})}K^{\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}+\beta)}E_{i}b

\displaystyle=u(\alpha_{i}+\beta)q^{-\frac{1}{2}(\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}+\beta|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}+\beta)\right)}{(\alpha_{i}+\beta|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}+\beta))}{(\alpha_{i}+\beta|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}+\beta))}{(\alpha_{i}+\beta|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}+\beta))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}+\beta)})}K^{\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}+\beta)}E_{i}b\,.

In the last step, we invoke the identity

\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta)\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\beta))}=\mathchoice{\left(\beta|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\beta|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}
, which is
equivalent to our assumption that
\mathsfit h
is

\mathsf{\Phi}

-symmetric. The respective computation for
F_{i}b
is analogous, and the extension to
\Lambda
-linear combinations obvious.

Since
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}(b)=g_{\beta}b
for a
\mathbb{w}
-homogeneous elements
b
with

invertible,

\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}
maps the two-sided ideal generated by
b
to itself. Thus,
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}

is well-defined on any quotient of
L_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
obtained by dividing by
\mathbb{w}
-homogeneous relations.
Since all relations in (
3.11
)-(
3.14
) are indeed
\mathbb{w}
-homogeneous, we conclude the statement in Item
i)
. The statement in Item
ii)
is easily checked on the generators, and Item
iv)
is immediate from Item
iii)
.
∎

Given some
\mathsfit h\in{\mathbb{S}}(\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}})
and
\beta\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
, we know
from Lemma
2.11

ii)
that
2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)}\in\mathbb{Z}\,
. We can thus define a character
\varpi_{\mathsfit h}\in\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}},\Lambda^{\star})
by

(4.9)

\varpi_{\mathsfit h}:\,\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\rightarrow\Lambda^{\star}\;:\quad\beta\,\mapsto\,\varpi_{\mathsfit h}(\beta)=q^{2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\beta)}}\,.

Note that
\varpi_{\mathsfit h}\cdot\varpi_{\mathsfit k}=\varpi_{\mathsfit h+k}
. We will also use the abbreviation
\varpi=\varpi_{\mathsfit i\!d}\,
so that
\varpi(\alpha_{i})=q_{i}^{2}\,
.

In
[
46
]
Lusztig introduces two anti-involutions. The Cartan anti-involution
\Omega:U_{q}\rightarrow U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}}}
is defined as the
\mathbb{Z}
-algebra homomorphism with the following actions on algebra generators and the indeterminate of the ground ring.

(4.10)

\displaystyle\Omega(E_{i})=F_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\Omega(F_{i})=E_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\Omega(K_{i})=K_{i}^{-1}\,,

\displaystyle\Omega(q)=q^{-1}\,.

Secondly, let
\mho:U_{q}\rightarrow U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}}
be the involutive
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
-algebra homomorphism defined on generators as follows.

(4.11)

\displaystyle\mho(E_{i})=E_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\mho(F_{i})=F_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\mho(K_{i})=K_{i}^{-1}\,.

Clearly,
\mho
preserves both the
\mathbb{w}
and
\mathbb{o}^{\pm}
gradings, while
\mathbb{w}\circ\Omega=-\mathbb{w}
and
\mathbb{o}^{+}\circ\Omega=\mathbb{o}^{-}\,
. In addition to Lusztig’s involutions, it will be useful to also introduce the conjugation automorphism
\Upsilon:U_{q}\rightarrow U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}}
defined on generators by

(4.12)

\displaystyle\Upsilon(E_{i})=E_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\Upsilon(F_{i})=F_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\Upsilon(K_{i})=K_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\Upsilon(q)=q^{-1}\,.

All three of the above involutions may also be viewed as involutive anti-homomorphisms. It follows easily by inspection on generators that
\Omega
,
\mho
, and
\Upsilon
commute with each other and, thus, implement an action of
(\mathbb{F}_{2})^{3}
on
U_{q}\,
.

For later use, we introduce notation for two composites of these. Firstly,
\Pi=\Upsilon\circ\Omega=\Omega\circ\Upsilon:U_{q}\rightarrow U_{q}
is a
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
-algebra homomorphism given on generators by

(4.13)

\displaystyle\Pi(E_{i})=F_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\Pi(F_{i})=E_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\Pi(K_{i})=K_{i}^{-1}\,.

Secondly, let
\amalg=\Upsilon\circ\mho=\mho\circ\Upsilon:U_{q}\rightarrow U_{q}
, which is a
\mathbb{Z}
-algebra homomorphism with non-trivial action on the ground ring given by

(4.14)

\displaystyle\amalg(E_{i})=E_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\amalg(F_{i})=F_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\amalg(K_{i})=K_{i}^{-1}\,,

\displaystyle\amalg(q)=q^{-1\,}\,.

Clearly, the automorphisms
\mho
,
\Upsilon
, and
\amalg
map each of the subalgebras
U_{q}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}
with
{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\in\{0,+,-,{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\}\,
to itself, while the
\Omega
and
\Pi
map these algebras to their respective opposites.

Additional commutation relations with the antipode and the Che transformations from (
4.8
) are immediate from checks on generators as well. More specifically, for a

\mathsf{\Phi}

-symmetric map
\mathsfit h\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}})
and a character
u\in\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}},\Lambda^{\star})
we obtain the following commutations relations of these involutions with the
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}
transformations, where
\varpi_{\mathsfit h}
is as in (
4.9
).

(4.15)

\displaystyle\Omega\,\circ\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}

\displaystyle=\,\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}\,\circ\,\Omega\hskip 59.75078pt

\displaystyle\hskip 59.75078pt\mho\,\circ\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}

\displaystyle=\,\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{-\mathsfit h}_{u\cdot\varpi_{\mathsfit h}}\,\circ\,\mho

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{14.22636pt}\Pi\,\circ\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}

\displaystyle=\,\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u^{-1}\cdot\varpi^{-1}_{\mathsfit h}}\,\circ\,\Pi

\displaystyle\Upsilon\,\circ\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}

\displaystyle=\,\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u^{-1}\cdot\varpi_{\mathsfit h}^{-1}}\,\circ\,\Upsilon

Furthermore, the antipode can be expressed as the composite

(4.16)

S\,=\,\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{-\mathsfit i\!d}_{\boldsymbol{\iota}\cdot\varpi}\,\circ\,\mho\,=\,\mho\,\circ\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit i\!d}_{\boldsymbol{\iota}}\,,\qquad\mbox{where}\quad\boldsymbol{\iota}(\beta)=(-1)^{0pt(\beta)}=(-1)^{\mathchoice{\left(\breve{\rho}|\beta\right)}{(\breve{\rho}|\beta)}{(\breve{\rho}|\beta)}{(\breve{\rho}|\beta)}}\,,

with
0pt
and
\breve{\rho}
as discussed at the end of Section
2.3
. Commutation relations of the antipode with the other automorphisms can now be derived directly from (
4.16
)
and the commutation relations in (
4.15
). For example,
S
commutes with
\Omega
,
S\circ\mho=\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{-2\mathsfit i\!d}_{\varpi}\circ\mho\circ S\,
, and
S^{2}=\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{0}_{\varpi}\,
.

Finally, note that
\mho
and
\Upsilon
preserve the
\mathbb{w}
and
\mathbb{o}^{\pm}
gradings. For
\Omega
we find

(4.17)

\displaystyle\mathbb{w}\circ\Omega

\displaystyle=-\mathbb{w}\,,

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{+}\circ\Omega

\displaystyle=\mathbb{o}^{-}\,,

and

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{-}\circ\Omega

\displaystyle=\mathbb{o}^{+}\,,

implying the same equations for
\Pi
.

4.3.
Lusztig’s Action of Artin-Tits Monoid

In
[
45
,
46
,
47
]
Lusztig introduces for any Lie type
\mathfrak{g}
algebra automorphisms
T_{i}
on
U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}
as well as on
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}
for
1\leq i\leq n
where
n
is the rank of
\mathfrak{g}
. Importantly, they fulfill the Artin-Tits relations (
2.6
) for the respective Cartan data.

In order to conform with conventions in the
R
-matrix constructions in
[
42
]
we will prefer to work with the inverses
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}=T_{i}^{-1}
of these automorphisms. Their explicit actions on the generators of
U_{q}
are as follows:

(4.18)

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(E_{i})

\displaystyle=-K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(F_{i})

\displaystyle=-E_{i}K_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(K_{j})

\displaystyle=K_{j}K_{i}^{-A_{ij}}\,,

(4.19)

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}^{-1}_{i}(E_{i})

\displaystyle=-F_{i}K_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}^{-1}_{i}(F_{i})

\displaystyle=-K_{i}^{-1}E_{i}\,,

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}^{-1}_{i}(K_{j})

\displaystyle=K_{j}K_{i}^{-A_{ij}}\,,

and for
i\neq j

(4.20)

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(E_{j})=\sum_{r+s=-A_{ij}}\frac{(-1)^{r}q_{i}^{-s}}{[s]!_{i}[r]!_{i}}E_{i}^{s}E_{j}E_{i}^{r}\,,

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(F_{j})=\sum_{r+s=-A_{ij}}\frac{(-1)^{r}q_{i}^{s}}{[r]!_{i}[s]!_{i}}F_{i}^{r}F_{j}F_{i}^{s}\,,

(4.21)

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}^{-1}_{i}(E_{j})=\sum_{r+s=-A_{ij}}\frac{(-1)^{r}q_{i}^{-s}}{[r]!_{i}[s]!_{i}}E_{i}^{r}E_{j}E_{i}^{s}\,,

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}^{-1}_{i}(F_{j})=\sum_{r+s=-A_{ij}}\frac{(-1)^{r}q_{i}^{s}}{[s]!_{i}[r]!_{i}}F_{i}^{s}F_{j}F_{i}^{r}\,.

Lemma 4.2
.

The automorphisms
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
restrict to automorphisms on the algebra
U_{q}
over
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
and fulfill the Artin-Tits relations (
2.6
) for all Lie types.

The proof of the first assertion is immediate, observing that the denominators in the above expressions divide
[-A_{ij}]!_{i}
and hence

[-d_{i}A_{ij}]!
as well as
[\mathsf{e}]!=[{\mathsf{e}^{*}}-1]!
. Thus, the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
automorphisms are well-defined over the ground ring
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
. Moreover, the Artin-Tits relations have been verified for the
T_{i}
automorphisms in
[
45
,
46
,
47
]
and thus also hold for the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}=T_{i}^{-1}
.

An immediate consequence is that we can associate an automorphism to any Weyl group element. For each reduced word
w=w_{i_{1}}\dots w_{i_{k}}\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
, let
\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{i_{1}}\circ\ldots\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{i_{k}}
. By Lemma
2.1
, the composed automorphism only depends on the Weyl group element
s={\mathscr{r}(w)}
represented by
w
, allowing us to write
\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}
. Now, for
s,t\in\mathscr{W}
the construction implies

(4.22)

\mathit{\Gamma}_{st}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{t}\qquad\mbox{if}\quad l(st)=l(s)+l(t)\,.

That is, due to the length additivity condition
s\mapsto\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}
is
not
a representation of
\mathscr{W}\,
. Instead, the above notation should be understood as
the composite of the Matsumoto map

\mathscr{s}:\mathscr{W}\rightarrow\mathscr{A}^{+}\,
from Section
2.2
with the natural monoid homomorphism
\mathit{\Gamma}:\,\mathscr{A}^{+}\rightarrow\mathrm{Aut}(U_{q})\,
defined on the positive Artin-Tits monoid, which extends to an action
\mathit{\Gamma}:\,\mathscr{A}\rightarrow\mathrm{Aut}(U_{q})\,
of the Artin group on
U_{q}
.
Thus, depending on context, we allow subscripts of
\mathit{\Gamma}
to be in
\mathscr{W}
,
\mathscr{W}^{*}
, or

\mathscr{A}
. These notations are related, for example, by
\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{\mathscr{r}(w)}
if
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
or
\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{\mathscr{s}(s)}
if
s\in\mathscr{W}\,
.

Observe that
\Omega
commutes with all
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
and
T_{i}\,
. Also, for the
\mho
involution one
readily infers
\mho\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}\circ\mho=\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{-1}=T_{i}
, or, more generally,

(4.23)

\mho\,\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}\circ\,\mho\,=\,(\mathit{\Gamma}_{s^{-1}})^{-1}\,=\,T_{s}\qquad\forall s\in\mathscr{W}\,.

Here
T_{s}=T_{i_{1}}\circ\ldots\circ T_{i_{k}}
denotes the analogous automorphisms used by Lusztig to define generators associated to general positive roots. The relation in (
4.23
) will thus serve to relate our conventions of choosing generators to those in
[
45
,
46
]
.
The second equality may also be written as
\mathit{\Gamma}_{b}=T_{\iota(b)}
for an element
b\in\mathscr{A}
,
where
\iota\in\mathrm{Aut}(\mathscr{A})
maps each generator of
\mathscr{A}
to its inverse.
The action of the braid automorphisms on the
U_{q}^{0}
basis elements is naturally given by

(4.24)

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(K^{\nu})

\displaystyle=K^{s(\nu)}\,.

Finally, for a homogeneous element
b\in U_{q}
one readily works out the following equivariance relations for the gradings, where the action of
s\in\mathscr{W}
is naturally extended to the root lattice
\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\supset\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\,
as well as
\mathbb{F}_{2}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\,
.

(4.25)

\displaystyle\mathbb{w}(\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(b))

\displaystyle=s(\mathbb{w}(b))

(4.26)

\displaystyle\mathbb{o}^{\pm}(\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(b))

\displaystyle=s(\mathbb{o}^{\pm}(b))

Clearly, (
4.24
), (
4.25
) and (
4.26
) hold also if the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}
are replaced by the original
T_{s}
automorphisms.

4.4.
More
\mathscr{A}^{+}
Commutation Relations

In this section, we provide commutation relations between the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}
automorphisms and the Che transformations
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}
, from which we also obtain respective commutation relations with the antipode. We denote the natural (left) actions of
\mathscr{W}
on elements
\mathsfit h\in{\mathbb{S}}(\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}})
and
u\in\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}},\Lambda^{\star})
by
\mathsfit h^{s}=shs^{-1}
and
s_{*}u=u\circ s^{-1}\,
, respectively. Additionally, define the character
\mathchoice{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-3.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle s}}\in\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}},\Lambda^{\star})
by

(4.27)

\mathchoice{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-3.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle s}}(\beta)=q^{-\mathchoice{\left(\theta_{\mathsfit h}(s)|\beta\right)}{(\theta_{\mathsfit h}(s)|\beta)}{(\theta_{\mathsfit h}(s)|\beta)}{(\theta_{\mathsfit h}(s)|\beta)}}\,,

which is well-defined by Lemma
2.11

vi)
. The following basic relations involving this character are easily derived from statement
viii)
as well as the combination of (
2.27
) and (
4.9
):

(4.28)

\mathchoice{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle t\cdot s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle t\cdot s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle t\cdot s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-3.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle t\cdot s}}=\mathchoice{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h^{s}}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle t$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h^{s}}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle t$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h^{s}}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle t$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h^{s}}\mkern-3.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle t}}\cdot t_{*}(\mathchoice{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-3.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle s}})\,\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad(\mathchoice{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-3.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle s}})^{2}=(s_{*}\varpi_{\mathsfit h})\cdot(\varpi_{\mathsfit h^{s}})^{-1}\,.

Proposition 4.3
.

Suppose
\mathsfit h\in{\mathbb{S}}(\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}})
,
u\in\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}},\Lambda^{\star})
, and
s\in\mathscr{W}
. Using notations and conventions as above we have

(4.29)

\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}\,\circ\,\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}\,\,=\,\,\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h^{s}}_{(s_{*}u)\cdot\mathchoice{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-3.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle s}}}\,\circ\,\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}\;.

Proof.

Since all maps in the relation are automorphisms it suffices to check (
4.29
) for the generators of
U_{q}\,
. Moreover, since the
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}
act trivially on the
K_{i}
’s and since
\Omega
commutes with both
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}
and
\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}
it suffices to check (
4.29
) for only the
E_{i}
generators. Note further that for a homogeneous element
b
with
\mathbb{w}(b)=\beta
we have

\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{0}_{s_{*}u}(\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(b))=(s_{*}u)(s(\beta))\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(b)=u(\beta)\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(b)=\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(u(\beta)b)=\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{0}_{u}(b))
, using
\mathbb{w}(\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(b))=s(\beta)
by (
4.25
), so that (
4.29
) holds for
\mathsfit h=0
. Since
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}=\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit 0}_{u}\circ\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{1}
we may, therefore, assume
u=1
in the following verification.

\displaystyle\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h^{s}}_{\mathchoice{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-3.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle s}}}(\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(E_{i}))

\displaystyle=\mathchoice{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-3.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle s}}(s(\alpha_{i}))q^{-\frac{1}{2}\left({\mathchoice{\left(s(\alpha_{i})|\mathsfit h^{s}(s(\alpha_{i}))\right)}{(s(\alpha_{i})|\mathsfit h^{s}(s(\alpha_{i})))}{(s(\alpha_{i})|\mathsfit h^{s}(s(\alpha_{i})))}{(s(\alpha_{i})|\mathsfit h^{s}(s(\alpha_{i})))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h^{s}}|s(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h^{s}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h^{s}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h^{s}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}}\right)}K^{\mathsfit h^{s}(s(\alpha_{i}))}\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(E_{i})

\displaystyle=q^{-\mathchoice{\left(\theta_{\mathsfit h}(s)|s(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\theta_{\mathsfit h}(s)|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(\theta_{\mathsfit h}(s)|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(\theta_{\mathsfit h}(s)|s(\alpha_{i}))}}q^{-\frac{1}{2}\left({\mathchoice{\left(s(\alpha_{i})|s(\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))\right)}{(s(\alpha_{i})|s(\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})))}{(s(\alpha_{i})|s(\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})))}{(s(\alpha_{i})|s(\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}}\right)}K^{s(\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(E_{i})

\displaystyle=q^{-\left({\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}-\mathchoice{\left(s(\rho_{\mathsfit h})|s(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(s(\rho_{\mathsfit h})|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(s(\rho_{\mathsfit h})|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(s(\rho_{\mathsfit h})|s(\alpha_{i}))}}\right)}q^{-\frac{1}{2}\left({\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(\rho_{s\mathsfit hs^{-1}}|s(\alpha_{i}))}}\right)}\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(K^{\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})})\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(E_{i})

\displaystyle=q^{-\frac{1}{2}\left({\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}-2\mathchoice{\left(s(\rho_{\mathsfit h})|s(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(s(\rho_{\mathsfit h})|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(s(\rho_{\mathsfit h})|s(\alpha_{i}))}{(s(\rho_{\mathsfit h})|s(\alpha_{i}))}}\right)}\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(K^{\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})}E_{i})

\displaystyle=q^{-\frac{1}{2}\left({\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i})\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}{(\alpha_{i}|\mathsfit h(\alpha_{i}))}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i}\right)}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i})}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i})}{(\rho_{\mathsfit h}|\alpha_{i})}}\right)}\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{{\mathsfit h}}_{1}(E_{i}))\qquad=\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}\circ\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{{\mathsfit h}}_{1}(E_{i})

In the first line, we use Proposition
4.1
iii)
for
\beta=\mathbb{w}(\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(E_{i}))=s(\alpha_{i})\,
. In the second line, definitions are inserted, including

. The third line
invokes isometry of
s
and (

). In the fourth line, exponent terms are combined and canceled, and we use that
\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}
is an automorphism. In the last lines
s
-isometry, the definition for
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{{\mathsfit h}}_{1}
, and (
2.29
) are employed.
∎

The action of the Artin-Tits monoid
\mathscr{A}^{+}
on the set of Che transformations given by conjugation thus factors into an action of
\mathscr{W}
on
{\mathbb{S}}(\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}})\times\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}})
. The latter is defined as

s.(\mathsfit h,u)=(\mathsfit h^{s},(s_{*}u)\cdot\mathchoice{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-9.0mu\raisebox{-1.7pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle s$}\mkern 2.7mu}{\vartheta^{\mathsfit h}\mkern-3.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle s}})
using (

). An immediate consequence is that any Che transformation commutes with the action of the

Artin-Tits group on
U_{q}
, defined as the kernel of the map
\mathscr{A}\rightarrow\mathscr{W}\,
.

As an application, we also derive an explicit commutation relation between the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}
maps and the antipode. To this end, let

be the character defined by

(4.30)

\boldsymbol{\kappa}_{s}(\beta)=(-1)^{\mathchoice{\left(\breve{\theta}(s)|\beta\right)}{(\breve{\theta}(s)|\beta)}{(\breve{\theta}(s)|\beta)}{(\breve{\theta}(s)|\beta)}}q^{-\mathchoice{\left(\theta(s)|\beta\right)}{(\theta(s)|\beta)}{(\theta(s)|\beta)}{(\theta(s)|\beta)}}\,,

with

Proposition 4.4
.

For any
s\in\mathscr{W}
we have

Proof.

We first establish that
