\displaystyle\,=\,\sum_{\phi\in S_{\mathsf{e}}(\vec{n})}\,q^{f_{\mathsf{e}}(\phi)}\prod_{t=1}^{\phi(\alpha_{j})}\bigl(q_{j}^{-2t}z+1\bigr){E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle(\phi)$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-9.89171pt}{\hskip-9.89171pt}{\hskip-5.91403pt}{\hskip-4.22432pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-122.94559pt}{\hskip-122.94559pt}{\hskip-73.93651pt}{\hskip-53.43735pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 122.94559pt}

(5.51)

\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{M}z^{k}q_{i}^{k(\mathscr{u}_{i}(\vec{n})-1)}E_{i}^{(M-k)}E_{j}^{(N)}E_{i}^{(k)}

\displaystyle\,=\,\sum_{\phi\in S_{\mathsf{e}}(\vec{n})}\,q^{f_{\mathsf{e}}(\phi)}\prod_{t=1}^{\phi(\alpha_{i})}\bigl(q_{i}^{-2t}z+1\bigr){E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle(\phi)$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-9.89171pt}{\hskip-9.89171pt}{\hskip-5.91403pt}{\hskip-4.22432pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-122.94559pt}{\hskip-122.94559pt}{\hskip-73.93651pt}{\hskip-53.43735pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 122.94559pt}\,.

Proof.

We show here only (
5.50
)
since the proof for (
5.51
) is analogous. Set
w=zq_{j}^{\mathscr{u}_{j}(\vec{n})-1}=zq^{\mathsf{e}(M-N-1)}
. The left side of (
5.50
) can be evaluated as

\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{N}w^{k}E_{j}^{(k)}E_{i}^{(M)}E_{j}^{(N-k)}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}0\leq k\leq N\\
\psi\in S_{\mathsf{e}}(\vec{n}-k\alpha_{j})\end{subarray}}w^{k}q^{f_{\mathsf{e}}(\psi)}E_{j}^{(k)}{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle(\psi)$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-10.37508pt}{\hskip-10.37508pt}{\hskip-6.18626pt}{\hskip-4.41876pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-72.8805pt}{\hskip-52.68301pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 119.56487pt}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}0\leq k\leq N\\
\psi\in S_{\mathsf{e}}(\vec{n}-k\alpha_{j})\end{subarray}}w^{k}q^{f_{\mathsf{e}}(\psi)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\psi(\alpha_{j})+k}$}\\
\scriptstyle{k}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}_{j}{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle(\psi+k\hat{\chi}_{j})$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-32.93004pt}{\hskip-32.93004pt}{\hskip-24.04178pt}{\hskip-20.41248pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-72.8805pt}{\hskip-52.68301pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 119.56487pt}

\displaystyle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}0\leq k\leq\phi(\alpha_{j})\\
\phi\in S_{\mathsf{e}}(\vec{n})\end{subarray}}w^{k}q^{f_{\mathsf{e}}(\phi-k\hat{\chi}_{j})}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\phi(\alpha_{j})}$}\\
\scriptstyle{k}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}_{j}{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle(\phi)$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-9.89171pt}{\hskip-9.89171pt}{\hskip-5.91403pt}{\hskip-4.22432pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-72.8805pt}{\hskip-52.68301pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 119.56487pt}=\sum_{\phi\in S_{\mathsf{e}}(\vec{n})}q^{f_{\mathsf{e}}(\phi)}\left(\sum_{k=0}^{\phi(\alpha_{j})}w^{k}q^{-k\mathsf{e}(\phi(\alpha_{j})+M-N)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\phi(\alpha_{j})}$}\\
\scriptstyle{k}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}_{j}\right){E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle(\phi)$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-9.89171pt}{\hskip-9.89171pt}{\hskip-5.91403pt}{\hskip-4.22432pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-72.8805pt}{\hskip-52.68301pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 119.56487pt}\,.

Here we use (
5.46
) in the first equality with
\vec{n}-k\alpha_{j}=M\alpha_{i}+(N-k)\alpha_{j}\,
. The second step is immediate from the forms (
5.42
) and combining quantum factorials. In the third equality, we substitute
\phi=\psi+k\hat{\chi}_{j}
, summing instead over
\phi\in S_{\mathsf{e}}(\vec{n})
with
\phi(\alpha_{j})\geq k
. The last step invokes
(
5.43
) and rearranges summations. After resubstituting
z
in the last expression, we apply Gauss’s formula from (
3.3
) with
a=\phi(\alpha_{j})
to arrive at the desired expression.
∎

Specializing (
5.50
) to
z=-q_{j}^{2}
and (
5.51
) to
z=-q_{i}^{2}
yields the commutation relations
in Section 5.5 of
[
46
]
. In this case, the product terms will be zero unless
\phi(\alpha_{j})=k_{m}=0
or
\phi(\alpha_{i})=k_{1}=0
, respectively. Assuming further
\mathscr{u}_{j}(\vec{n})=M-N=0
for (
5.50
), it is immediate from (
5.44
) that
k_{1}=\ldots=k_{m-2}=0\,
. Thus, the only exponent function
\phi^{\prime}
that occurs in the summation
is the one that is
N
on
\gamma(a_{m-1})=\alpha_{i}+\alpha_{j}
and zero on all other roots, where
a_{j}
is as in
(
2.32
). Observing also that

f_{\mathsf{e}}(\phi^{\prime})=\mathsf{e}N\,
, the right side of (
5.50
) thus reduces to
q^{\mathsf{e}N}E_{a_{m-1}}^{(N)}\,
.

Analogously, for (
5.51
) the constraint
\mathscr{u}_{i}(\vec{n})=\mathsf{e}N-M=0
implies
k_{3}=\ldots=k_{m}=0
so that
the only remaining exponent function is the one which is
N
on
\gamma(a_{2})=\mathsf{e}\alpha_{i}+\alpha_{j}
and zero on others. The right side of (
5.50
) thus becomes
q^{\mathsf{e}N}E_{a_{2}}^{(N)}\,
. The resulting identities are summarized in the left column of the corollary below.

Corollary 5.8
.

The following identities hold:

(5.52)

E_{a_{m-1}}^{(N)}=\sum_{k=0}^{N}(-1)^{N-k}q_{j}^{-k}E_{j}^{(N-k)}E_{i}^{(N)}E_{j}^{(k)}\,,\qquad\quad E_{(ji)}^{(N)}=\sum_{k=0}^{N}(-1)^{k}q_{j}^{-(N-k)}E_{j}^{(N-k)}E_{i}^{(N)}E_{j}^{(k)}\,,

(5.53)

E_{(ij)}^{(N)}=\sum_{k=0}^{\mathsf{e}N}(-1)^{\mathsf{e}N-k}q^{-k}E_{i}^{(k)}E_{j}^{(N)}E_{i}^{(\mathsf{e}N-k)}\,,\qquad\quad E_{b_{m-1}}^{(N)}=\sum_{k=0}^{\mathsf{e}N}(-1)^{k}q^{-(\mathsf{e}N-k)}E_{i}^{(k)}E_{j}^{(N)}E_{i}^{(\mathsf{e}N-k)}\,.

The identities in the right column are obtained by applying
\mho
and using (
5.16
) as well as the relations

a_{m-1}\dualmap b_{2}=w_{j}w_{i}\,
and
b_{m-1}\dualmap a_{2}=w_{i}w_{j}\,
as in Lemma
2.12
.

As already indicated, (
5.52
) corresponds to the first relation in Section 5.5 of
[
46
]
.
For the change in conventions, note that
\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{ij}=\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{(ji)}=E_{a_{m-1}}
by (
5.19
).
Similarly, the right identity of (
5.53
)
is the translation of the second expression in
[
46
, Section 5.5]
.
For this, the generators
\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{ij}
,
\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{iij}
, and
\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{iiij}
listed in
[
46
]

for
\mathsf{e}=1
,
2
, and
3
, respectively, coincide in all cases with
\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{b_{m-1}}=E_{(ij)}
via
(
5.19
).

We thus have expansions into products of generators for simple roots of divided power generators
E_{w}^{(N)}
for all words, with exception of the words
a_{3}\dualmap b_{4}
and
a_{4}\dualmap b_{3}
in the
\mathsf{G}_{2}
-case. Yet, unlike
(
5.48
), equations (
5.52
) and (
5.53
) cannot be written as expansions of ordinary powers over
\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]\,
.

5.5.
Numberings, Boxes, and Refining Convex Orderings

The integral PBW bases derived in
[
45
,
46
]
for the divided power algebra
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{+}
require orderings on
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
that are compatible with a specific pre-order
\precsim\,
on
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\,
, defined in Section 4.3 of
[
46
]
. As we adapt the proofs there to the situation of regular powers, we review this pre-order next and establish various relations to convex orderings and maximal words.

Lusztig’s construction of
\precsim\,
starts by imposing a
good
numbering on the set

\mathsf{\Delta}

of simple roots. For a given indexing
\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}=\{\alpha_{1},\ldots,\alpha_{n}\}\,
, write
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}[1,j]
for the respective subroot system generated by
\{\alpha_{1},\ldots,\alpha_{j}\}
. Assuming that each
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}[1,j]
is connected, set
L_{j}={\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}[1,j]-\{\rho_{j}\}
, where
\rho_{j}
is the highest root in
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}[1,j]\,
. The numbering is called good if for any root
\beta\in L_{j}
the coefficient of
\alpha_{j}
is at most 1.

The numberings in appendix of
[
13
]
are good with the exception of types
B
and
F
. For the latter two, the reverse numberings given by
i\leftrightharpoons l+1-i
are good. For type A any numbering is good, for
C
also the reverse of
[
13
]
is good, and for type
D
any numbering coinciding with the one in
[
13
]
in the highest index as well as the reverse of the one in
[
13
]
are good.

For a given good numbering, any positive root
\beta
can be uniquely written as
\beta=b_{j}\alpha_{j}+b_{j-1}\alpha_{j-1}+\ldots+b_{1}\alpha_{1}
with
b_{j}>0\,
. Lusztig introduces maps
g:{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\rightarrow\{1,\ldots,n\}
and
c:{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\rightarrow\{1,2\}\,
given by
g(\beta)=j
and
c(\beta)=c_{j}\,
. It is clear from the good numbering construction that
c(\beta)=2
implies that
\beta=\rho_{j}
in
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}[1,j]\,
.
Lusztig further defines
h^{\prime}:{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\rightarrow\mathbb{Q}
by
h^{\prime}(\beta)=c(\beta)^{-1}0pt(\beta)\,
, where
0pt(\beta)=\sum_{i}b_{i}
is the height of the root with respect to

\mathsf{\Delta}

.

The pre-order is now defined by writing
\,\alpha\precsim\beta\,
if
\,g(\alpha)\geq g(\beta)\,
and
\,h^{\prime}(\alpha)\leq h^{\prime}(\beta)\,
. The equivalence classes
R_{m,k}=\{\beta\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}:g(\beta)=m,\,h^{\prime}(\beta)=k\}
are called
boxes
in
[
46
]
. We record the following two observations.

Lemma 5.9
.

Suppose
\alpha,\beta\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
(
\alpha\neq\beta
) belong to the same box. Then none of
\pm\alpha\pm\beta
are roots.

Proof.

Given
m=g(\alpha)=g(\beta)
we have
\alpha,\beta\in M={\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}[1,m]\,
, where
M
itself is a root system with highest root
\rho
, so that it suffices to show
\pm\alpha\pm\beta\not\in M\,
. Assume first
c(\alpha)=c(\beta)=1
. Then
0pt(\alpha-\beta)=0pt(\alpha)-0pt(\beta)=h^{\prime}(\alpha)-h^{\prime}(\beta)=0=0pt(\beta-\alpha)
, which is not possible. For
\gamma=\alpha+\beta
we have

c(\gamma)=2
and
0pt(\gamma)=2k\,
. If
\gamma\in M
the former implies that
\gamma=\rho
and that
M
is of type
\mathsf{E}_{8}
,
\mathsf{F}_{4}
, or
\mathsf{G}_{2}
. In all three cases
0pt(\rho)
is odd (29, 11, or 5), leading to a contradiction. Now,
c(\alpha)=2
implies
\alpha=\rho
and hence
k=h^{\prime}(\alpha)\in\{14.5,5.5,2.5\}
so that there is no other root in the same box.
∎

An immediate corollary is that any two roots in the same box are (strongly) orthogonal. In
[
45
,
46
]
Lusztig goes on to consider total orders refining
\precsim\,
. With good numberings as above, we notice the following.

Lemma 5.10
.

Any total order on
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
refining
\precsim\,
is convex and thus of the form
\preceq_{w}
for some
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}\,
.

Proof.

Let
\alpha,\beta,\gamma=\alpha+\beta\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
and suppose
\alpha\in R_{m,k}
and
\beta\in R_{m^{\prime},k^{\prime}}
.
Set
t=c(\alpha)c(\gamma)^{-1}
and
s=c(\beta)c(\gamma)^{-1}
so that
h^{\prime}(\gamma)=t\cdot k+s\cdot k^{\prime}\,
,
using that
0pt(\gamma)=0pt(\alpha)+0pt(\beta)
. Write also
\mu\not\sim\nu
to indicate two roots are not in the same box.

Suppose now
<
is a total order refining
\precsim
and assume
\alpha<\beta
. Since
\gamma\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
, Lemma
5.9
implies
\alpha\not\sim\beta
. Hence, either we have
m>m^{\prime}
or we have
m=m^{\prime}
and
k<k^{\prime}\,
. The former case implies
g(\gamma)=m
, which means
\gamma\precsim\beta
and
\beta\not\sim\gamma
and, hence,
\gamma<\beta\,
. Moreover, with
c(\gamma)=c(\alpha)\,
, we find
t=1
so that

h^{\prime}(\gamma)=k+s\cdot k^{\prime}>k\,
. Hence,
\gamma\succsim\alpha
and
\gamma\not\sim\alpha
so that
\alpha<\gamma\,
.

In the second case we have
g(\alpha)=g(\beta)=g(\gamma)
and
c(\gamma)=c(\alpha)+c(\beta)
so that
s=(1-t)
. Thus
h^{\prime}(\gamma)=t\cdot k+(1-t)\cdot k^{\prime}
and
k<h^{\prime}(\gamma)<k^{\prime}\,
since
0<t<1
. We, therefore, obtain
\alpha<\gamma<\beta
in this case as well and, hence, convexity of the total ordering. As shown in
[
60
]
this implies that
<
needs to be of the form
\preceq_{w}
as desired.
∎

Note, for Lie types
A
,
B
, and
G
each box contains no more than one element. Thus, there is only one
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
for which the total order
\preceq_{w}
refines
\precsim\,
. Specifically, the chosen good numbering for
\mathsf{A}_{n}
is realized by the maximal word
w_{\mathsf{A}_{n}}=a_{1}a_{2}\ldots a_{n}
, where
a_{k}=w_{n}w_{n-1}\ldots w_{k}\,
. Also, for
\mathsf{B}_{n}
we have
w_{\mathsf{B}_{n}}=b_{n}\ldots b_{1}
, where
b_{k}=w_{k}w_{k-1}\ldots w_{2}w_{1}w_{2}\ldots w_{k-1}w_{k}
, and for
\mathsf{G}_{2}
that
w_{\mathsf{G}_{2}}=(w_{2}w_{1})^{3}\,
.

For
\mathsf{C}_{n}
with the Bourbaki numbering one longest word choice refining
\precsim\,

is given as a product
w=u\cdot v
. Here
u=\alpha_{0}\beta_{0}\alpha_{1}\beta_{1}\ldots\beta_{1}\alpha_{1}\beta_{0}\alpha_{0}
is a palindromic expression in
\alpha_{j}=w_{n}w_{n-2}\ldots w_{n-2j}
and
\beta_{j}=w_{n-1}w_{n-3}\ldots w_{n-2j-1}
centered around the longest
\alpha_{k}
or
\beta_{k}
, and
v
is a longest word for
A_{n-1}
. The reduced word

w_{4}w_{3}w_{2}w_{3}w_{1}w_{4}w_{2}w_{3}w_{4}w_{2}w_{3}w_{1}w_{2}w_{3}w_{4}w_{3}w_{2}w_{3}w_{1}w_{2}w_{3}w_{1}w_{2}w_{1}

is compatible with the pre-order for
\mathsf{F}_{4}
using the reverse numbering of that in
[
13
]
. The words for the simply laced
D
and
E
Lie types are similarly worked out with additional choices within boxes.

5.6.
PBW Bases for Box Orderings

The sole focus of this section is the adaption of the proofs in
[
45
,
46
]
to yields a PBW theorem for regular power
generators instead of divided power generators. The main
change from the original proof is that the involved
commutation and recursion relations for generators are valid only over

\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
rather than
\Lambda_{q}
as in
[
45
,
46
]
.
The second difference is merely concerning conventions,
namely the alternate choice of generators
E_{w}
defined
via the automorphisms
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
in Section
5.1
rather than the
\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{w}
used in
[
45
,
46
]
. Thanks to the relation in (
5.29
)
it is not difficult to move between
these two settings using the
\mho
involution,
while also replacing the root ordering for
z
by
the one for
z^{\dagger}
.
The form (
5.25
) for
the action of the
\Upsilon
involutions
implies, further,
that bases with generators multiplied in opposing directions have the same spans.

Although the inductive argument for a PBW theorem itself is unchanged from
[
45
,
46
]
, we outline the main steps
again in the proof below. We also adapt the formulae to fit our conventions, even as the mentioned
automorphisms and symmetries would afford us the flexibility to retain those in
[
45
,
46
]
. We freely use the notation for monomial sets and spans introduced at the end of Section
5.3
, with a focus on the minimal
ground ring
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\,
and the maximal exponent set
\mathsf{S}=\mathcal{E}({s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}})\,
.

Proposition 5.11
.

Suppose
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
is such that
\preceq_{w}
refines
\precsim\,
. Then
U_{q}^{+}
is free a
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-module with basis given by either the generators in

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
or those in

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w
as defined in (
5.35
).
The analogous statement holds for
U_{q}^{-}
and the sets

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle-\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
and

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle-\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w
.

Proof.

Recall that, by Proposition
5.1
, the
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-module

{\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
, generated by elements in

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
, is contained in
U_{q}^{+}
.
Since the elements in

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
form a basis of
U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}
over the field
\mathbb{Q}(q)
, see Corollary 40.2.2 in
[
47
]
, we also know that they form a basis of

{\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
as a
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-module and that
U_{q}^{+}/{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
is at most a torsion module.
Since
1\in{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
is a cyclic vector for the left or right regular action of
U_{q}^{+}
on itself,
either
U_{q}\cdot{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\subseteq{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
or
{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\cdot U_{q}\subseteq{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}

would imply
U_{q}={\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\,
.
Thus, it remains to show that
{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\cdot E_{i}\subseteq{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\,
for all
i\,
or
E_{i}\cdot{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\subseteq{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\,
for all
i\,
.

The inductive proof in the simply laced case can be obtained by modifying the arguments in Section 2 of
[
45
]
. Specifically, instead of the spaces in 2.10 we consider analogous spaces defined with regular rather than divided powers. For example,
X_{m,k}
is replaced by
X_{m,k}^{*}\,
, defined as the
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-algebra of
U_{q}^{+}
generated by
E_{w[\alpha]}
(as in (
2.15
)) with
\alpha\in R_{m,k}
as well as
E_{j}
with
j<m\,
. Similarly,
Y^{*}_{m,k}
is the free
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-submodule generated by

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle u\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
where
u\leq_{R}w
is the maximal word with
\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(u)\cap R^{+}_{m,k}=\emptyset\,
.
Statement (b) of Lemma 2.11 in

[
45
]

is then changed to
Y^{*}_{m,k}\cdot X_{m,k}^{*}\subseteq Y^{*}_{m^{\prime},k^{\prime}}\cdot X_{m^{\prime},k^{\prime}}^{*}\,
if
R^{+}_{m^{\prime},k^{\prime}}
is the next smaller box in the
\precsim

order after
R^{+}_{m,k}
with integer
k^{\prime}\,
.

In the adjustment of the proof, we first redefine the generators
\xi_{t}
as ordinary powers
E^{N_{t}}_{\alpha_{t}}
. The notions of distinguished and non-distinguished generators as well as
bad or good pairs are adapted to ordinary powers in the same manner.
The commutation argument invokes equations (d2)-(d5) in
\lx@sectionsign 2.3
of
[
45
]
that are imposed on the algebra
V^{+}
defined there. The isomorphism
V^{+}\cong{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{+}
in Section 4.7 implies that these relations also hold in
U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{+}
for the divided powers of the
\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{\alpha}
generators. Analogous equations can be readily derived from these for ordinary powers of the
E_{\alpha}
generators, as defined in (
5.1
) and (
5.3
). For example, for
\alpha
and
\alpha^{\prime}
fulfilling (e1) or (e2), equation (d3) in
[
45
]
specializes for
N=M=1
to
\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{\alpha^{\prime}}\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{\alpha}=q\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{\alpha+\alpha^{\prime}}+q\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{\alpha}\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{\alpha^{\prime}}
. Applying
\mho
with
\mho(\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{\alpha})=E_{\alpha}
we obtain
E_{\alpha^{\prime}}E_{\alpha}=(-1)E_{\alpha+\alpha^{\prime}}+q^{-1}E_{\alpha}E_{\alpha^{\prime}}
. Analogs for (d2), (d4), and (d5) are also obtained by application of
\mho
and multiplication of factorials. The desired analog of (d3) is then obtained from these relations by the same induction,

E_{\alpha^{\prime}}^{N}E_{\alpha}^{M}=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(N,M)}(-1)^{j}q^{-(N-j)(M-j)}[j]!\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{N}$}\\
\scriptstyle{j}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{M}$}\\
\scriptstyle{j}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}E_{\alpha}^{M-j}E_{\alpha+\alpha^{\prime}}^{j}E_{\alpha^{\prime}}^{N-j}\,.

Clearly, all coefficients are in
\Lambda_{q}=\Lambda_{q,2}\,
. The same process is applied to (b) in Proposition 2.7 to express
E_{\alpha_{i}}^{N}E_{\beta_{0}}^{M}
as

\Lambda_{q}
-combinations of respective ordinary power generators with reversed cyclic order of indices, using also that
\psi_{0}=1
and
\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{N}$}\\
\scriptstyle{s}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{M}$}\\
\scriptstyle{s}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}\in\Lambda_{q}\,
. The other equations in Proposition 2.7 and 2.8 are modified, as before, by application of
\mho
and multiplication of factorials.

All other parts of the proof of Lemma 2.11 in
[
45
]
can be adapted verbatim. As in Proposition 2.12(b) the inclusion can be iterated to infer
Y^{*}_{n,1}\cdot X_{n,1}^{*}\subseteq Y^{*}_{1,1}\cdot X_{1,1}^{*}\,
, which is exactly the inclusion
U_{q}^{+}\subseteq\mathbf{B}^{+}\,
.

As noted in
[
46
]
for the case of divided powers, the proof for the non-simply laced cases follows the same type of inductive argument. Commutation relations of all divided power generators in the rank 2 case
\mathsf{B}_{2}=\mathsf{C}_{2}
are explicitly worked out in Sections 5.2 and 5.3 of
[
46
]
. As with the simply laced cases, it is straightforward to derive relations for
\mathsf{e}=2
and
\mathsf{e}=3
in Section 5.2 for the opposite orders of generators and, hence, after application of
\mho
, respective relations for our convention of generators. From these, analogs of the equations in Section 5.3 can be readily derived for our generators by rescaling arguments. The coefficient will thus differ only by units in
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\,
.

Multiplication of the analogs of equations (d) through (i) in the same section of
[
46
]
by respective quantum factorials readily yields commutation relations for ordinary powers with coefficients in
\Lambda_{q,3}\,
. The variant of (g) for our generators is, for example, is as follows,

(5.54)

E_{\gamma}^{k}E_{\delta}^{k^{\prime}}=\sum_{s=0}^{\min(k,k^{\prime})}\frac{1}{[2]^{s}}q^{2s(k+k^{\prime})-3s^{2}}(q-q^{-1})^{s}[s]_{2}!\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{k}$}\\
\scriptstyle{s}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{k^{\prime}}$}\\
\scriptstyle{s}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}_{2}E_{\delta}^{k^{\prime}-s}E_{\beta}^{2s}E_{\gamma}^{k-s}\,.

Here
\delta=\alpha_{2}
,
\gamma=\alpha_{2}+2\alpha_{1}
, and
\beta=\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}
with
\alpha_{2}
the long root. The coefficients are all in
\Lambda_{q,3}
but not in
\Lambda_{q}
due to the additional
\frac{1}{[2]}
factors. The respective variant for (h) is

(5.55)

E_{1}^{k}E_{\tau}^{k^{\prime}}=\sum_{s=0}^{\min(k,k^{\prime})}(-1)^{s}{[2]^{s}}q^{s(k+k^{\prime})-\frac{1}{2}s(7s+3)}[s]!\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{k}$}\\
\scriptstyle{s}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{k^{\prime}}$}\\
\scriptstyle{s}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}E_{\tau}^{k^{\prime}-s}E_{\tau+\alpha_{1}}^{s}E_{1}^{k-s}\,,

where
\tau=\alpha_{2}+\alpha_{1}
. Using respective multinomial coefficients and
\nu=\alpha_{2}
we also reexpress equation (i) in
[
46
]
as

(5.56)

E_{1}^{k}E_{\nu}^{k^{\prime}}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}r,s,t,u\geq 0\\
r+s+t=k^{\prime}\\
s+2t+u=k\end{subarray}}(-1)^{s}q^{-2r(u+t)+us}[s]!_{2}[2t]!\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{k}$}\\
\scriptstyle{s,2t,u}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-7.68222pt\raise 3.1298pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{k^{\prime}}$}\\
\scriptstyle{r,s,t}\vskip-3.1298pt\end{bmatrix}_{2}E_{\nu}^{r}E_{\nu+\alpha_{1}}^{s}E_{\nu+2\alpha_{1}}^{t}E_{1}^{u}\,.

It is immediate that the set of relations allows reordering of any monomial over
\Lambda_{q,3}
into the order on the positive roots of
\mathsf{B}_{2}
given by
w_{2}w_{1}w_{2}w_{1}
. Explicit relations for
\mathsf{G}_{2}
are given in Section 5.4 of
[
46
]
as well. Although more complicated, all of them can be multiplied by respective factorials and transformed into relations for our generators in the same manner, except that powers of
\frac{1}{[3]}
occur in addition to those of
\frac{1}{[2]}\,
.

The higher rank
BCF
cases follow as in the simply laced case from commutation relations obtained by application of Artin automorphisms to the rank 2 relations as well as those for the respective
A
type subalgebras. In the above ordering for the
B
case Lemma
5.6
readily implies that generators from consecutive boxes
R^{+}_{m,k}
and
R^{+}_{m,k+1}
skew-commute. Consider next required
commutation relations between elements
E_{\tau}
with
\tau\in R^{+}_{m,k}
and generators
E_{j}
for
j<m\,
. From
Proposition
5.1

it follows that
\mathit{\Gamma}_{d_{m}}(E_{j})=E_{j}
for
d_{m}=b_{n}\ldots b_{m+1}\in\mathscr{W}^{*}\,
, reducing the arguments to the case
m=n\,
and, hence,
E_{\tau}=E_{v}
with
v\leq_{R}b_{m}\,
.

In all cases in which
\tau+\alpha_{j}\not\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
it is then readily checked that
E_{\tau}
and
E_{j}
and, hence, all their powers commute up to signs.
For
\tau=\alpha_{m}+\ldots+\alpha_{j+1}
when
j>1
we invoke the known commutation relations for
\mathsf{A}_{n-1}\subset\mathsf{B}_{n}
. Applying
\mathit{\Gamma}_{w_{m}\ldots w_{3}}
to
(
5.55
) we see that the relation holds more generally for
\nu=\alpha_{m}+\ldots+\alpha_{2}
, yielding the needed relation between
E_{\nu}
and
E_{1}\,
. Similarly, applying
\mathit{\Gamma}_{w_{m}\ldots w_{3}}
to (
5.55
) extends the relation to the case

\tau=\alpha_{m}+\ldots+\alpha_{1}
. Note that in this case
\mathchoice{\left(\tau|\alpha_{1}\right)}{(\tau|\alpha_{1})}{(\tau|\alpha_{1})}{(\tau|\alpha_{1})}=0
, even as
\tau+\alpha_{1}\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\,
.

Finally, for
j>1
and

\tau=\alpha_{m}+\ldots+\alpha_{j}+2\alpha_{j-1}+\ldots+2\alpha_{1}
we find
E_{j}E_{\tau}=q^{-2}E_{\tau}E_{j}-E_{\tau+\alpha_{j}}
,
E_{\tau+\alpha_{j}}E_{j}=q^{-2}E_{j}E_{\tau+\alpha_{j}}
, and

E_{\tau+\alpha_{j}}E_{\tau}=q^{2}E_{\tau}E_{\tau+\alpha_{j}}\,
, which implies
E_{\tau}
and
E_{j}
fulfill the
\mathsf{A}_{2}
Serre relations with
q
replaced by
q^{2}
. This, again, implies the usual
\mathsf{A}
type commutation relations, only with
q
replaced by
q^{2}
.

The treatment for the
C
and
F
cases uses the same arguments and analogous computations. Indeed, choosing the numbering opposite to that of
[
13
]
is also good for
C
, leading to essentially the same relations as in the
B
case. The
\mathsf{F}_{4}
can be treated explicitly as an extension of
\mathsf{B}_{3}
or
\mathsf{C}_{3}\,
. This completes the proof for the basis

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
for one direction of multiplication.

It follows now immediately from (
5.25
) that

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w
provides a basis of
U_{q}^{+}
as well, since
\Upsilon
maps elements from

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
to those of

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w
up to unit factors. Similarly, (
5.24
) implies the respective statements for
U_{q}^{-}\,
with basis elements mapped to each other by
\Omega\,
.
∎

As noted in the introductory remarks, we could have also followed the Lusztig’s conventions with
the respectively renormalized commutation relations in the
\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}_{w}
. This would have yielded

{\phantom{\scalebox{.65}{$E$}}\accentset{\bullet\mkern-1.1mu\bullet}{\scalebox{.82}{\vphantom{$E$}}}\mathchoice{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-20.73613pt}{\hskip-16.49173pt}{\hskip-14.11131pt}{E}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
as a
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-basis for
U_{q}^{+}
for
w
compatible with the box ordering chosen in
[
45
,
46
]
.
Since
U_{q}^{+}
is invariant under
\mho
, we have from (
5.29
) that

{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w^{\dagger}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-29.39688pt}{\hskip-29.39688pt}{\hskip-18.51701pt}{\hskip-13.81374pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 29.39688pt}
is also a basis. So, after application
\Upsilon
, we find that

{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w^{\dagger}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-28.58025pt}{\hskip-28.58025pt}{\hskip-17.94536pt}{\hskip-13.40543pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 28.58025pt}
is a basis as well. For the general PBW theorem,
it suffices to establish a PBW statement for only one ordering, so that
the replacement of
w
by
w^{\dagger}
does not change the proof of Propositions
5.17

or Theorem
5.18
below.

Corollary 5.12
.

For
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
as in Proposition
5.11
the sets

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle\pm\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
and

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle\pm\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w
are bases of
U_{q}^{-}
as a free
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-module.

We conclude with another useful consequence of Proposition
5.11
, which allows us to identify subalgebras generated by a subset of generators as quantum algebras themselves.

Corollary 5.13
.

For any pair of distinct indices
i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}
, let
{U}_{\ \mkern-9.0muq}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}^{+}
be the rank 2 quantum algebra with respectively restricted Cartan data. Then the canonical algebra homomorphism
{U}_{\ \mkern-9.0muq}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}^{+}\rightarrow U_{q}^{+}
is well-defined and injective, and its image is the subalgebra of
U_{q}^{+}
generated by
E_{i}
and
E_{j}\,
.

Proof.

Surjectivity on the subalgebra generated by
E_{i}
and
E_{j}
is obvious. Similarly, it is clear the map is well-defined, since the relations of
{U}_{\ \mkern-9.0muq}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}^{+}
are also fulfilled in
U_{q}^{+}\,
. For
\mathsf{G}_{2}
(or any rank 2 case) the statement is also obvious. To show injectivity in the
\mathsf{A}_{1}\times\mathsf{A}_{1}
,
\mathsf{A}_{2}
, and
\mathsf{B}_{2}=\mathsf{C}_{2}
cases, we note that either numbering for each of these is a good numbering and can thus be chosen to inherit the order of the numbering imposed by
U_{q}^{+}\,
.

Since also the height and lead coefficients of positive roots are the same, the pre-order

\precsim\,
of
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
for
U_{q}^{+}
restricts to the pre-order of positive root system
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\mkern-2.0mu{\scriptstyle(i,j)}
of
{U}_{\ \mkern-9.0muq}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}^{+}\,
. This implies, by Proposition
5.11
, that we have a basis for
{U}_{\ \mkern-9.0muq}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}^{+}
that is mapped to basis elements of
U_{q}^{+}\,
, implying injectivity. Indeed,

{U}_{\ \mkern-9.0muq}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}^{+}
is a direct summand of
U_{q}^{+}
as a
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-module.
∎

We conclude our discussion of the existence of bases with a brief outline of other approaches.
As mentioned previously, Lusztig proves in
[
45
,
46
,
47
]
that the monomials

{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle(\psi)$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-10.37508pt}{\hskip-10.37508pt}{\hskip-6.18626pt}{\hskip-4.41876pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
from (
5.33
) define a PBW basis of his divided
power algebra
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{+}\,
over
\Lambda_{q}=\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]\,
. It can be correspondingly extended
to a basis of all of

{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}
over
\Lambda_{q}
at the expense of introducing additional generators in
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{0}\,
given by rational expressions in the
K_{i}
and
q
.

In
[
22
, Sec 12]
, De Concini and Procesi define the algebra
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{S}$}}{U}
to be the smallest subalgebra of

U_{q}\otimes\mathbb{k}(q)
over

\mathbb{k}[q,q^{-1}]
that contains the
singularized generators
\breve{E}_{i}
and
\breve{F}_{i}
from (
5.10
) and
is stable under the Artin group action generated by the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}\,
. They offer a proof
that the monomials
{\breve{E}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}K^{\mu}{\breve{F}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\chi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-2.24924pt}{\hskip-1.60658pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
from (
5.34
) form a

\Lambda_{q}
-basis of
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{S}$}}{U}
. Their argument is based on recursions formulae over
\mathbb{C}
in
[
43
]
and proves that recursion coefficients are indeed in
\mathbb{k}[q,q^{-1}]
for an appropriate
\mathbb{k}\,
.

The fact that the
{\breve{E}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}
are a basis of
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{S}$}}{U}^{+}
may also be inferred from
the Lusztig-Tanisaki pairing discussed in Section
9.4
and the PBW theorem for

{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{+}
in

[
45
,
46
,
47
]
. Comparing the
coefficients in (
5.33
), (
5.34
), and (
9.11
)
the pairing in (
9.25
) can be rewritten as

(5.57)

\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle_{z}:{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{-}\times{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{S}$}}{U}^{+}\rightarrow\Lambda_{q}\qquad\mbox{with}\quad\langle{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle(\psi)$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-10.37508pt}{\hskip-10.37508pt}{\hskip-6.18626pt}{\hskip-4.41876pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt},{\breve{E}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\phi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-2.10294pt}{\hskip-1.50209pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\rangle\,=\,\delta_{\psi,\phi}\cdot(-1)^{n(\psi)}\cdot q^{-\sum_{\alpha}d_{\alpha}\binom{\psi(\alpha)}{2}}

Since the pairings for
\psi=\phi
are units in
\Lambda_{q}
the span of the
{\breve{E}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\phi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-2.10294pt}{\hskip-1.50209pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}

is the exact
\Lambda_{q}
-dual to
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{-}\,
. The product and the
q
-braided coproduct
\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta

defined by Lusztig
[
47
]
on
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{-}
are then dual to respective structures on this span.
This now identifies the latter with
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{S}$}}{U}^{+}
so that the basis result for
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{S}$}}{U}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
is essentially the dual equivalent of Lusztig’s basis result on
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{L}$}}{U}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\,
.

However, as algebras over
\Lambda_{q}
or
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\,
,
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{S}$}}{U}^{+}
and
U_{q}^{+}
exhibit rather different behaviors. This becomes especially apparent in the
q\mapsto 1
specialization, realized by the obvious
ring maps
\Lambda_{q}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}
or
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}[{\mathsf{e}}^{-1}]
.
For example, for Lie type
\mathsf{A}_{n}
one easily sees from Proposition
7.7

that the specialization
{\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathscr{S}$}}{U}^{+}\otimes\mathbb{Z}
is the
commutative
polynomial algebra
in the
E_{i,j}\,
, while the specialization
U_{q}^{+}\otimes\mathbb{Z}
is the universal envelope
U(\mathfrak{n})
, where
\mathfrak{n}

is the Lie algebra of the strictly upper triangular matrices.

Another variant is to consider renormalized generators

\mathring{E}_{w}=[d_{w}]E_{w}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{w^{\flat}}(\mathring{E}_{i})\,
with
i=\tau(w)
and

\mathring{E}_{i}=[d_{i}]E_{i}\,
. The respective renormalization of the formulae (
5.54
,
5.55
,
5.56
) then yields expansion coefficients entirely in
\Lambda_{q}\,
. We, thus,
expect that there is a Hopf algebra
\mathring{U}_{q}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
over
\Lambda_{q}\,

with a PBW basis over this ring, even for the non-simply laced Lie types.

5.7.
Spanning Sets and Their Order Dependence

For any subset of exponent
functions
\psi\in\mathcal{E}(s)
for some
s\in\mathscr{W}

one can consider the submodule spanned by the respective monomials

{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
, where
s=\mathscr{r}(w)\,
. Numerous subalgebras and ideals we will consider later can be defined as such spans.
In this section we extract sufficient conditions on a set of exponent functions which imply
that the respective free submodule is independent of the choice of a convex root ordering or, equivalently,
dependent only on the Weyl element
s=\mathscr{r}(w)\,
.

Suppose
s\in\mathscr{W}\,
. We say
(a,b)
with
a,b\in\mathscr{W}
is a
relator pair
for
s
if

(5.58)

s=a\cdot\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\cdot b\qquad\mbox{with}\quad l(s)=l(a)+l(\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})+l(b)\,

for the longest element
\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}
is some rank 2 subsystem
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}}\mkern-0.3mu{\scriptstyle(ij)}\,
of

\mathsf{\Phi}

. Observe now that
Corollary
2.4
provides us with a bijection of inversion sets given as

(5.59)

\mathscr{b}_{(a,b)}=\mathrm{id}\sqcup a\sqcup a\cdot\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\,:\,\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(a)\sqcup\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})\sqcup\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(b)\,\longrightarrow\,\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\,.

Correspondingly, as in (
5.3
), we obtain the bijection of exponent sets

(5.60)

\mathscr{b}_{(a,b)}^{*}\,:\,\mathcal{E}(s)\,\rightarrow\,\mathcal{E}(a)\times\mathcal{E}(\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})\times\mathcal{E}(b)\,.

Given a subset
\mathsf{S}\subseteq\mathcal{E}(s)\,
we abbreviate its image in the Cartesian product as
\mathsf{S}_{(a,b)}=\mathscr{b}_{(a,b)}^{*}(\mathsf{S})\,
.

The following discussion assumes a general ground ring
\Lambda
with an extension of scalars function
f:\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\rightarrow\Lambda\,
. Note, that
Proposition
5.11
implies, that both

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
and

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
are bases of
{U}_{\ \mkern-9.0muq,\Lambda}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}^{+}={U}_{\ \mkern-9.0muq}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}^{+}\otimes_{f}\Lambda\,
.
Recall from Corollary
5.13
, that the latter may be viewed as the subalgebra generated by
E_{i}
and
E_{j}
.
We, thus, can define coefficients
\scalebox{.76}{$\boldsymbol{\mho}$}^{\varphi}_{\varphi^{\prime}}{}\in\Lambda
for any
\varphi,\varphi^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}(\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})
by

(5.61)

\mho({E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\varphi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-2.38876pt}{\hskip-1.70625pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt})={E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\varphi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-2.38876pt}{\hskip-1.70625pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}=\sum_{\varphi^{\prime}}\scalebox{.76}{$\boldsymbol{\mho}$}^{\varphi}_{\varphi^{\prime}}{}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\varphi^{\prime}$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-5.94058pt}{\hskip-5.94058pt}{\hskip-3.85126pt}{\hskip-3.16875pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}\,.

From these we define the following subsets of
\mathcal{E}(\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})
for any
\varphi\in\mathcal{E}(\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})

and
\mathsf{Q}\subseteq\mathcal{E}(\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})\,
:

(5.62)

\mho_{\{ij\}}(\varphi)=\bigl\{\varphi^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}(\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})\,:\,\scalebox{.76}{$\boldsymbol{\mho}$}^{\varphi}_{\varphi^{\prime}}{}\neq 0\bigr\}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\mho_{\{ij\}}(\mathsf{Q})=\bigcup_{\varphi\in\mathsf{Q}}\mho_{\{ij\}}(\varphi)\,.

Note that, since
\mho
is an involution,
we have
\mho_{\{ij\}}(\mathsf{Q})=\mho_{\{ji\}}(\mathsf{Q})
. Commutation of
\mho
with

\Upsilon
and (
5.25
) imply that the sets are the same if the oppositely ordered basis elements are used instead. Commutation with
\Omega
shows the same for the respective bases of
U_{q}^{-}\,
. The sets may, however, depend on the choice of
the ground ring as
f
may map some non-zero coefficients in
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
to
zero in
\Lambda\,
.

For given
s\in\mathscr{W}
we say an exponent set
\mathsf{S}\subseteq\mathcal{E}(s)
is
relator stable
if for
any relator pair
(a,b)
for
s
we have the implication

(5.63)

(\chi,\varphi,\xi)\in\mathsf{S}_{(a,b)}\quad\mbox{and}\quad\varphi^{\prime}\in\mho_{\{ij\}}(\varphi)\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad(\chi,\varphi^{\prime},\xi)\in\mathsf{S}_{(a,b)}\,.

Defining
U^{\mathsf{S},a,b}_{\chi,\xi}\subseteq{U}_{\ \mkern-9.0muq,\Lambda}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}^{+}
as the
\Lambda
-span
of the set
\{{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\varphi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-2.38876pt}{\hskip-1.70625pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}:\,(\chi,\varphi,\xi)\in\mathsf{S}_{(a,b)}\}
, it is clear from (
5.61
) that this
condition may be equivalently restated as the requirement that
\mho(U^{\mathsf{S},a,b}_{\chi,\xi})\subseteq U^{\mathsf{S},a,b}_{\chi,\xi}
for all relator pairs
(a,b)
and
(\chi,\xi)\in\mathcal{E}(a)\times\mathcal{E}(b)
.

Note that we only need to consider cases when
m_{ij}=l(\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})\in\{3,4,6\}
since the condition is void for
m_{ij}=2
.
Indeed, in the latter case
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}}\mkern-0.3mu{\scriptstyle(ij)}=\{\alpha_{i},\alpha_{j}\}
and
E_{i}
and
E_{j}
commute so that

{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\varphi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-2.38876pt}{\hskip-1.70625pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}={E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\varphi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-2.38876pt}{\hskip-1.70625pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}
. Thus

\mho_{\{ij\}}(\varphi)=\{\varphi\}
, rendering (
5.63
) trivially true.

Equipped with this terminology, we state the following criterion for word independence of spanning sets, which may be viewed as a reformulation of Matsumoto’s equivalence as a property of exponent sets.

Proposition 5.14
.

Let
w,\tilde{w}\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
be two reduced words representing the same element

s=\mathscr{r}(w)=\mathscr{r}(\tilde{w})
in
\mathscr{W}
. Assume further that
\mathsf{S}\subseteq\mathcal{E}(s)
is a relator stable exponent set for given ground ring
\Lambda\,
. Then we have for the
\Lambda
-spans
{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-8.11118pt}{\hskip-8.11118pt}{\hskip-4.9681pt}{\hskip-3.54861pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-16.1402pt}{\hskip-11.52873pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.68861pt}={\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-8.11118pt}{\hskip-8.11118pt}{\hskip-4.9681pt}{\hskip-3.54861pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\tilde{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.27078pt}{\hskip-26.27078pt}{\hskip-18.05592pt}{\hskip-14.48442pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.27078pt}\,
. Further, if the elements of

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
are linearly independent, then so are those of

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\tilde{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
.

The analogous assertions hold for the

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},-\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
and

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},\pm\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w
and their spans.

Proof.

By Matsumoto’s Theorem (see Corollary
2.1
) the exists a sequence of reduced words, starting with
w
and ending with
\tilde{w}
, each of which is obtained from the previous one by replacing a substring of the form

\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}
by
\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}\,
, vice versa. By transitivity of the assertions, it suffices to consider the case in which
\tilde{w}
is obtained from
w
by one such substitution. That is,
w=u\cdot\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\cdot v
and
\tilde{w}=u\cdot\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}\cdot v
as reduced decompositions. Thus, with
a=\mathscr{r}(u)
and
b=\mathscr{r}(v)
, we find
s=a\cdot\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\cdot b
and
l(s)=l(a)+m_{ij}+l(b)\,
. In particular,
(a,b)
is a relator pair for
s
.

Suppose now
\psi\in\mathsf{S}
so that
{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
is a spanning element for

{\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
and let
(\chi,\varphi,\xi)=\mathscr{b}_{(a,b)}^{*}(\psi)
.
Applying (
5.26
) twice, we find

{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}={E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\chi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-2.24924pt}{\hskip-1.60658pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle u\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.65712pt}{\hskip-24.65712pt}{\hskip-15.055pt}{\hskip-10.75359pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.65712pt}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{a}({E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\varphi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-2.38876pt}{\hskip-1.70625pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt})\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{a\cdot\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}}({E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\xi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-2.47224pt}{\hskip-2.47224pt}{\hskip-1.3271pt}{\hskip-0.94792pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle v\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.18025pt}{\hskip-24.18025pt}{\hskip-14.80089pt}{\hskip-10.57208pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.18025pt})\,
. Expanding

{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\varphi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-4.0931pt}{\hskip-2.38876pt}{\hskip-1.70625pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}
as in (
5.61
) into a sum of

{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\varphi^{\prime}$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-5.94058pt}{\hskip-5.94058pt}{\hskip-3.85126pt}{\hskip-3.16875pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}\,
, each term can then be rewritten as some

{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\tilde{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.48463pt}{\hskip-25.48463pt}{\hskip-17.80553pt}{\hskip-14.30556pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.48463pt}
using again (
5.26
). More precisely, writing

\psi(\varphi^{\prime})=(\mathscr{b}_{(a,b)}^{*})^{-1}(\chi,\varphi^{\prime},\xi)
for fixed
\chi
and
\xi
we find

(5.64)

{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\,=\,{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi(\varphi)$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-15.63483pt}{\hskip-15.63483pt}{\hskip-9.39168pt}{\hskip-6.70834pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\,=\,\sum_{\varphi^{\prime}}\scalebox{.76}{$\boldsymbol{\mho}$}^{\varphi}_{\varphi^{\prime}}{}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi(\varphi^{\prime})$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-17.48232pt}{\hskip-17.48232pt}{\hskip-10.85417pt}{\hskip-8.17084pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\tilde{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.48463pt}{\hskip-25.48463pt}{\hskip-17.80553pt}{\hskip-14.30556pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.48463pt}\,.

Condition (
5.63
) finally ensures that all basis elements on the right side are
in

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\tilde{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
whenever
\scalebox{.76}{$\boldsymbol{\mho}$}^{\varphi}_{\varphi^{\prime}}{}\neq 0
.
Thus
{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\in{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-8.11118pt}{\hskip-8.11118pt}{\hskip-4.9681pt}{\hskip-3.54861pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\tilde{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.48463pt}{\hskip-25.48463pt}{\hskip-17.80553pt}{\hskip-14.30556pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.48463pt}
and, therefore,
