{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-8.11118pt}{\hskip-8.11118pt}{\hskip-4.9681pt}{\hskip-3.54861pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\subseteq{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{S},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-8.11118pt}{\hskip-8.11118pt}{\hskip-4.9681pt}{\hskip-3.54861pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\tilde{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.48463pt}{\hskip-25.48463pt}{\hskip-17.80553pt}{\hskip-14.30556pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.48463pt}\,
.
The opposite inclusion is implied by
\mho
-symmetry.

Now, for fixed
\chi
and
\xi
, (
5.64
) yields a transformation
of the spanning elements
B^{(\chi,\xi)}_{w}=\{{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi(\varphi)$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-15.63483pt}{\hskip-15.63483pt}{\hskip-9.39168pt}{\hskip-6.70834pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}:\,\psi(\varphi)\in\mathsf{S}\}

to those of

via the restricted involution expressed by

. Thus,

is a basis if and only if

is a basis, proving the second statement.
Similarly, applications of

and

yield the assertions for the other types of spans.
∎

As an example, we may consider the following basic type of exponent sets.
Given two sets

5.8.
General Ordering Bases and Module Restrictions

The aim of this section is to extend the special bases from Proposition
5.11
to bases for any convex ordering and the entire
U_{q}
algebra. We will, further, consider extensions of scalars to ground rings
\Lambda
or
\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
as in
(
3.15
)
for given homomorphisms
f:\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\rightarrow\Lambda
and
f^{\,\,{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}:\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\rightarrow\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}\,
. Since the associated
functor
-\otimes_{\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}}\Lambda
maps free modules to free modules, any
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-basis of
U_{q}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}
is also a
\Lambda
-basis for
U_{q,\Lambda}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\,
, with

{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\in\{+,-,0,{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\}\,
. Similar considerations apply to
U_{q,\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.74861pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}}\,
.

We begin by adapting Rosso’s arguments for the tensor decomposition of the full quantum algebra over a field to our situation for rings
\Lambda
or
\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}\,
.
Lemma 2 in
[
64
]
proves that
U_{q,\Lambda}^{0}
is isomorphic to
\Lambda[\{K^{\pm}_{i}\}]\cong\Lambda[\mathbb{Z}^{n}]
and admits a
\Lambda
-basis is given by

(5.67)

\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}^{\,0}\,=\,\left\{{K^{\nu}:\,\nu\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}}\right\}

for
\Lambda
a field. The argument there does not require the latter assumption so that the
statement holds for any integral domain
\Lambda
as a ground ring.
We next consider multiplication maps, such as the following.

(5.68)

\displaystyle U_{q,\Lambda}^{0}\otimes_{\Lambda}U_{q,\Lambda}^{+}

\displaystyle\rightarrow\;U_{q,\Lambda}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{19.91692pt}U_{q,\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.74861pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}}^{+}\otimes_{\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.74861pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}}U_{q,\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.74861pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}}^{0}\otimes_{\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.74861pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}}U_{q,\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.74861pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}}^{-}

\displaystyle\rightarrow\;U_{q,\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.74861pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}}

Obvious additional maps are given by permuting the tensor factors as well as swapping the algebras

U_{q}^{+}\leftrightharpoons U_{q}^{-}
and
U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\leftrightharpoons U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
.

To show surjectivity of these maps, it suffices to show that their respective images are preserved under the left regular action of the respective target algebra, which is immediate from the commutation relations (
3.13
) and (
3.13
). For example, applying
E_{k}
to a general element in the image of the first type of map yields with
E_{k}(K^{\nu}E_{i_{1}}\ldots E_{i_{N}})=q^{-\mathchoice{\left(\nu|\alpha_{k}\right)}{(\nu|\alpha_{k})}{(\nu|\alpha_{k})}{(\nu|\alpha_{k})}}(K^{\nu}E_{k}E_{i_{1}}\ldots E_{i_{N}})
again an element in the image. Similarly, for the second type of maps,

F_{k}(E_{i_{1}}\ldots E_{i_{N}}K^{\nu}F_{j_{1}}\ldots F_{j_{M}})
can be expressed as a
\Lambda_{q}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
-combination of summands of the form

E_{i_{1}}\ldots E_{i_{N}}K^{\nu}F_{k}F_{j_{1}}\ldots F_{j_{M}}
and

E_{i_{1}}\ldots\widehat{E_{i_{s}}}\ldots E_{i_{N}}K^{\mu}F_{j_{1}}\ldots F_{j_{M}}
, where
\mu\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
and the hat denotes omission whenever
i_{s}=k\,
.

The proofs of Proposition 1 and 2 in
[
64
]
for injectivity assume that the quantum algebra is defined over a field. As before, a straightforward inspection of the arguments there immediately shows that the only assumptions needed are the existence of a free basis over the ground ring as well as a grading-preserving coalgebra structure. The former is assured by Proposition
5.11
and Corollary
5.12
above. The latter is clearly also defined over the respective integral domains, and its grading properties are listed in (
4.6
) and (
4.7
). These observations are summarized next.

Lemma 5.16

(
[
64
]
)
.

The multiplication maps from (

\Lambda
or
\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}

Suppose

and

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle-\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w

are
\Lambda
-bases for
U_{q,\Lambda}^{-}
.

Proof.

Proposition
5.11
ensures that there is at least one reduced word

w^{*}\in\mathscr{r}^{-1}({s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}})
for which

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w^{*}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
and

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w^{*}
are
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-bases of
U_{q}^{+}
and hence also
\Lambda
-bases of
U_{q,\Lambda}^{+}\,
. Suppose now
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
is another presentation of
{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}\,
.

The full exponent set
\mathsf{S}=\mathcal{E}({s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}})=\mathbb{N}_{0}^{{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}}\,
is clearly of the form (
5.65
)
with
{V\mkern-5.0mu}_{d}=\mathbb{N}_{0}\,
. Moreover, as already noted in the proof of Corollary
5.15
, we have for
the full
\Lambda
-span

{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}\!\!={\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}\!\!={U}_{\ \mkern-9.0muq,\Lambda}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(i,j)$}^{+}\,
.
Thus, the second condition of Corollary
5.15
is also fulfilled, which
implies that
{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w^{*}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-28.85246pt}{\hskip-28.85246pt}{\hskip-18.1398pt}{\hskip-13.59987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 28.85246pt}\!\!={\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
. Thus

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
also spans
U_{q,\Lambda}^{+}\,
and is linearly independent.
The second case for
U_{q}^{-}
follows readily from Corollary
5.12
in the same manner.
∎

Clearly, Lemma
5.16
implies that, given bases for the tensor factors on the left sides of (
5.68
), their products as spanning sets yield bases for the quantum algebras on the right side. This, combined with Proposition
5.17
and the observation for
U_{q}^{0}
in (

), now yields the following general construction of PBW bases.

Theorem 5.18
.

Let
w,u\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
be any reduced words of maximal length and
\Lambda
,
\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
rings as in (

).
Then any of the spanning sets
\,{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-16.1402pt}{\hskip-11.52873pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.68861pt}\!\mkern-1.8mu\centerdot\mkern-1.8mu\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}^{\,0}\,
,
\,\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}^{\,0}\!\mkern-1.8mu\centerdot\mkern-1.8mu{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-16.1402pt}{\hskip-11.52873pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.68861pt}\,
,

\,{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-27.50525pt}{\hskip-27.50525pt}{\hskip-16.71185pt}{\hskip-11.93704pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 27.50525pt}\!\mkern-1.8mu\centerdot\mkern-1.8mu\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}^{\,0}\,
, or
\,\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}^{\,0}\mkern-1.8mu\centerdot\mkern-1.8mu{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-27.50525pt}{\hskip-27.50525pt}{\hskip-16.71185pt}{\hskip-11.93704pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 27.50525pt}

.

The analogous statement holds for
U_{q,\Lambda}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\,
.
Moreover, the spanning set
{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-16.1402pt}{\hskip-11.52873pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.68861pt}\!\mkern-1.8mu\centerdot\mkern-1.8mu\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}^{\,0}\mkern-1.8mu\centerdot\mkern-1.8mu{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle-\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-0.3349pt}{\hskip-0.3349pt}{\hskip-0.52795pt}{\hskip-0.89737pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle u\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.44327pt}{\hskip-25.44327pt}{\hskip-15.30539pt}{\hskip-10.93245pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.44327pt}
and any reordering of the factor sets as well as any direction reversals (24 versions in total) is a
\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
-basis for
U_{q,\Lambda^{{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.56221pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}}
.

One elementary but useful application of this theorem arises when subspaces constructed over fields need to be pulled back to submodules over the other rings. More concretely, suppose

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

is any
\Lambda
-basis as above for one of the algebras
U_{q,\Lambda}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\,
. Assume that
\Lambda
is an integral domain and
\mathbb{F}
its field of fractions so that we may view

U_{q,\Lambda}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}
as a subalgebra of
U_{q,\mathbb{F}}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\,
.

Suppose now
\mathcal{I}\subset\mathcal{B}
is a subset of basis elements and denote
I=\langle\mathcal{I}\rangle
its
\Lambda
-span in
U_{q,\Lambda}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\,
. Similarly, let
I_{\mathbb{F}}\cong I\otimes\mathbb{F}
be the respective
\mathbb{F}
-span in

U_{q,\mathbb{F}}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\,
. Since
I
is a direct summand, we then immediately have

(5.69)

I\,=\,I_{\mathbb{F}}\cap U_{q,\Lambda}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\,.

6.
Skew-Commutative Algebras at Roots of Unity

In this section, we turn to the specialization
q\mapsto\zeta
of a quantum group to a primitive

\mathscr{k}
-th root of unity
\zeta
. The main focus of our discussion are the primitive power generators

X_{\alpha}=E_{\alpha}^{\ell_{\alpha}}\,
, where
\ell_{\alpha}
is the order of

\zeta^{\mathchoice{\left(\alpha|\alpha\right)}{(\alpha|\alpha)}{(\alpha|\alpha)}{(\alpha|\alpha)}}
. For odd
\mathscr{k}
, the algebra
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\bullet}
generated
by these elements lies in the center of
U_{\zeta}

and has been studied, for example, in
[
21
,
22
]
.

Our treatment here includes, in addition,
all
even
\mathscr{k}>2{\mathsf{e}^{*}}
.
In many of these cases, the generators
X_{\alpha}

commute only up to signs with other elements in
U_{\zeta}
. Depending on Lie type and
the congruence of
\mathscr{k}
modulo 8, the algebra
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\bullet}
may be central,
commutative but not central, or neither. Besides a classification of these cases, we also prove
word independence of respective partial subalgebras
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
(with one exception)
and invariance under automorphisms.
Various types of implied and induced ideals are discussed as well.

6.1.
Quantum Numbers and Rings at Roots of Unity

Assume a root system with integers
d_{i}\in\{1,2,3\}
as in Section
2.1
such that

1=\min_{i}\{d_{i}\}
and
\mathsf{e}=\max_{i}\{d_{i}\}\,
. Fix an integer
\mathscr{k}\in\mathbb{N}
with

(6.1)

\mathscr{k}\not\in\{1,2,\mathsf{e},2\mathsf{e}\}\,.

The ring
\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]
of cyclotomic integers may be understood as the quotient of either
\mathbb{Z}[q]
or
\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]
by the principal ideal
J_{\mathscr{k}}=(\Phi_{\mathscr{k}}(q))
of the
\mathscr{k}
-th cyclotomic polynomial. Equivalently, we may view
\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]
as the ring of integers of the cyclotomic field
\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)
, considered as a subfield of
\mathbb{C}
for a given a choice of a primitive
\mathscr{k}
-th root of unity
\zeta\in\mathbb{C}\,
. That is, the kernel of the map
\mathbb{Z}[q]\rightarrow\mathbb{C}:q\mapsto\zeta
is precisely
J_{\mathscr{k}}\,
(see, for example,
[
74
]
for details).
We use the same notation as in (
3.1
) for the images of the quantum numbers in
\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]
.

Denote by
\ell\mkern-3.0mu=\mathscr{k}/\gcd(\mathscr{k},2)\,
the order of
\zeta^{2}\,
. For integers
d_{i}
as above write
\zeta_{i}=\zeta^{d_{i}}\,
and denote by
\mathscr{k}_{i}=\mathscr{k}/\gcd(\mathscr{k},d_{i})\,
the order of
\zeta_{i}\,
. Similarly, we set

\ell_{i}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu/\gcd(\ell\mkern-3.0mu,d_{i})=\mathscr{k}/\gcd(\mathscr{k},2d_{i})=\mathscr{k}_{i}/\gcd(\mathscr{k}_{i},2)
to be the order of

\zeta_{i}^{2}=\zeta^{2d_{i}}=\zeta^{\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{i}\right)}{(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{i})}{(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{i})}{(\alpha_{i}|\alpha_{i})}}\,
.
Note also that for short roots we have
\ell_{i}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu\,
since, by definition,
d_{i}=1\,
.

Condition (
6.1
) is indeed equivalent to requiring
\zeta^{2}_{i}\neq 1
for all

i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}
. This ensures that the factor
(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})^{-1}
occurring in
(
3.13
) exists in
\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)
so that the specialization
q\mapsto\zeta
for quantum groups is well-defined. Similarly, (
6.1
) implies that
m=\ell_{i}
is precisely the smallest positive integer for which
[m]_{i}=0\,
.

The following additional powers of
\zeta
will frequently appear in subsequent formulae.

(6.2)

\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{i}=\zeta_{i}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}}=\zeta^{d_{i}\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}}=\zeta^{\mathrm{lcm}(d_{i},\ell)}\qquad\qquad\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta_{i}=\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{i}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}}=\zeta_{i}^{{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}}^{2}}\qquad\qquad\raise 0.8251pt\hbox{$\rotatebox{90.0}{\scalebox{1.15}{$\bullet$}}$}\mkern-8.3mu\zeta_{i}=\zeta_{i}^{\binom{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}}{2}}

We note that
\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{i},\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta_{i}\in\{+1,-1\}\,
. Specifically,
\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{i}=-1
if and only if
\mathscr{k}_{i}
is even, and

\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta_{i}=-1
if and only if
\mathscr{k}_{i}\equiv 2\mod 4\,
. Moreover,
\raise 0.8251pt\hbox{$\rotatebox{90.0}{\scalebox{1.15}{$\bullet$}}$}\mkern-8.3mu\zeta_{i}\,
is a primitive fourth root of unity (
\raise 0.8251pt\hbox{$\rotatebox{90.0}{\scalebox{1.15}{$\bullet$}}$}\mkern-8.3mu\zeta_{i}^{2}=-1
) if
\mathscr{k}_{i}\equiv 0\mod 4
, we have
\raise 0.8251pt\hbox{$\rotatebox{90.0}{\scalebox{1.15}{$\bullet$}}$}\mkern-8.3mu\zeta_{i}=-1\,
if
\mathscr{k}_{i}\equiv 6\mod 8
, and
\raise 0.8251pt\hbox{$\rotatebox{90.0}{\scalebox{1.15}{$\bullet$}}$}\mkern-8.3mu\zeta_{i}=1\,
in all other cases. These relations also imply the identity
\raise 0.8251pt\hbox{$\rotatebox{90.0}{\scalebox{1.15}{$\bullet$}}$}\mkern-8.3mu\zeta_{i}^{2}=(-1)^{\ell_{i}-1}\,
in all cases.

As for generic
q
, if
d_{i}=1\,
, we will often drop the
i
subscript from the
roots of unity appearing in (
6.2
) as well as the quantum numbers.
In any of these, we may replace any subscript
i
by a subscript
\alpha
if
\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
is in the
\mathscr{W}
-orbit of
\alpha_{i}\,
. So, for example,
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}
,
\mathscr{k}_{\alpha}=\mathscr{k}_{i}
,
\zeta_{\alpha}=\zeta_{i}
, and
\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{\alpha}=\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{i}
. Analogously, for a reduced word

w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
we will write
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{w}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}
,
\zeta_{w}=\zeta_{i}
,
\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{w}=\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{i}
, and so forth if
i=\tau(w)
or, equivalently,
\gamma(w)
is in the
\mathscr{W}
-orbit of
\alpha_{i}\,
.

The commutation relations in (
3.13
) for the standard definition of quantum groups also contain denominators
(q_{i}-q_{i}^{-1})^{-1}\,
, which
a priori
map only to
\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)
but not
\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]
. A slightly sharper statement asserts that
the image
(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})^{-1}
is an element of the smaller ring
\mathbb{Z}[\zeta,\tfrac{1}{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}}]\subset\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)\,
. This follows readily from the following formula, in which
r=\ell\mkern-3.0mu/\gcd(m,\ell)
is the order of
\zeta^{2m}\,
:

(6.3)

(\zeta^{m}-\zeta^{-m})^{-1}\,=\,-\frac{1}{r}\sum_{j=0}^{r-2}(r-j-1)\zeta^{m(2j+1)}\qquad\in\;\mathbb{Z}[\zeta,\tfrac{1}{r}]\,\subset\,\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)\,.

For non-prime orders
\mathscr{k}
, smaller denominators may be chosen as, for example,
(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{-1}\in\mathbb{Z}[\zeta,\tfrac{1}{3}]
if
\ell\mkern-3.0mu=\mathscr{k}=9\,
. The use of singularized generators as in
(
5.10
) would avoid these denominators.

Aside from vanishing quantum numbers, the specialization also leads to additional units. For example, if
r
and
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}
are coprime, then
[r]_{i}
is a
unit in
\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]\,
. More generally, for any
m\in\mathbb{N}
and
d=\gcd(m,\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i})
we have the factorization
[m]_{i}=[d]_{i}\cdot u
, where
u
is a (cyclotomic) unit in
\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]
.

From (
6.3
) we also find that
([m]_{i})^{-1}\in\mathbb{Z}[\zeta,\tfrac{1}{s}]
, where
s=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}/d\in\mathbb{Z}\,
is the order of
\zeta_{i}^{2m}=\zeta^{2d_{i}m}\,
.
The next identity expresses the last non-vanishing factorial in terms of the order
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}
and the element
(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})\,
.

(6.4)

\mathcal{D}_{i}\,=\,[\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}-1]_{i}!\,=\,\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}\cdot\raise 0.8251pt\hbox{$\rotatebox{90.0}{\scalebox{1.15}{$\bullet$}}$}\mkern-8.3mu\zeta_{i}^{-1}\cdot(\zeta_{i}^{-1}-\zeta_{i})^{-\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}+1}\;

For an integer
n>1
, we introduce the following notation for specializations of the rings in (
3.8
), which will be used frequently in later sections.
They are well-defined as subrings of
\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)\,

if and only if
n\leq\ell\mkern-3.0mu\,
, which we will thus assume.

(6.5)

\displaystyle\Lambda_{\zeta}

\displaystyle=\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]

\displaystyle\Lambda_{\zeta,n}=\mathbb{Z}\textstyle{\left[\zeta,\frac{1}{[n-1]!}\right]}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{19.91692pt}\Lambda_{\zeta}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}

\displaystyle=\mathbb{Z}\textstyle{\left[{\zeta,\frac{1}{\zeta-\zeta^{-1}}}\right]}

\displaystyle\Lambda_{\zeta,n}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}=\mathbb{Z}\textstyle{\left[\zeta,\frac{1}{\zeta-\zeta^{-1}},\frac{1}{[n-1]!}\right]}

The minimal rings
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
and
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
over which
U_{q}^{\pm}
and
U_{q}
are defined specialize to
\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
and
\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
, respectively, if and only if
\ell\mkern-3.0mu\geq{\mathsf{e}^{*}}\,
, where
{\mathsf{e}^{*}}=\mathsf{e}+1\in\{2,3,4\}
is as in (
2.3
) depending on Lie type. As a condition on
\mathscr{k}
, the bound on
\ell
is equivalent to requiring (
6.1
) and, additionally,
\mathscr{k}\neq 4
whenever
\mathsf{e}=3
.
The latter exclusion refers to the
\mathsf{G}_{2}
quantum group, which is well-defined for

\mathscr{k}=4
but for which the braid automorphisms from Section
4.3
are not defined.

Previous remarks about cyclotomic units imply that
\Lambda_{\zeta}=\Lambda_{\zeta,n}
and

\Lambda_{\zeta}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}=\Lambda_{\zeta,n}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
if
j
and
\ell\mkern-3.0mu
are coprime (
\gcd(\ell\mkern-3.0mu,j)=1
)
for all
1\leq j\leq n
. This is, of course, the case if
\ell\mkern-3.0mu
itself is a prime or if
n=1\,
.
Consequently, we have

\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}=\Lambda_{\zeta}
and
\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}=\Lambda_{\zeta}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
for types
\mathsf{ADE}
and all
\ell\mkern-3.0mu>1
, for
types
\mathsf{BCF}
if
\ell\mkern-3.0mu
is odd, and for type
\mathsf{G}_{2}
if
\gcd(\ell\mkern-3.0mu,6)=1\,
.

As before, the relation
(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})=[d_{i}](\zeta-\zeta^{-1})
implies that

(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})^{-1}\in\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\,
. The definition of an
R
-matrix in our setting will require all non-zero factorials to appear as denominators, thus requiring
n=\ell\mkern-3.0mu\,
.
It is clear that all rings listed in (
6.5
) are subrings of

\Lambda_{\zeta,\ell\mkern-3.0mu}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\,
. In fact, equations (
6.3
) and (
6.4
) imply
the equality of rings

\Lambda_{\zeta,\ell\mkern-3.0mu}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}=\mathbb{Z}[\zeta,\frac{1}{\ell\mkern-3.0mu}]\;.

The evaluation of quantum binomial coefficients at a root of unity also leads to vanishing patterns and factorizations of classical binomial coefficients that will be important later. In order to describe the former, we introduce functions
\mathbb{c}_{i}:\mathbb{N}_{0}\times\mathbb{N}_{0}\rightarrow\{0,1\}
depending on
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}
as follows. For two integers
u,v\in\mathbb{N}_{0}\,
, write
u=a\cdot\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}+r
and
v=b\cdot\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}+s
with remainders
r,s\in\{0,\ldots,\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}-1\}\,
. Define then

(6.6)

\displaystyle\mathbb{c}_{i}(u,v)=\left\lfloor{\frac{u+v}{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}}}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor{\frac{u}{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}}}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor{\frac{v}{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}}}\right\rfloor\,=\,\mathbb{c}_{i}(r,s)\,=\,\begin{cases}1&\text{for }r+s\geq\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}\\
0&\text{for }r+s<\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}\,.\end{cases}\;

Here
\lfloor{x}\rfloor
is the floor function, which yields the greatest integer less than or equal to
x
. The expression clearly only depends on the classes
\overline{u},\overline{v}\in\mathbb{Z}/\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}\mathbb{Z}
and, as a map on these, is the standard 2-cocycle in
\mathrm{Z}^{2}(\mathbb{Z}/\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}\mathbb{Z})
generating
\mathrm{H}^{2}(\mathbb{Z}/\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}\mathbb{Z})\,
.

Lemma 6.1
.

With integers
u,v,r,s\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
as above, the image of the quantum binomial coefficient in
\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]
is given by the formula

(6.7)

\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$u+v$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
u\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{i}\,=\,\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{i}^{(as+br)}\cdot\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta_{i}^{ab}\cdot\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$r+s$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
r\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{i}\cdot{\binom{a+b}{a}}\;,

so that

\displaystyle\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$u+v$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
u\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{i}\,=\,0\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad\mathbb{c}_{i}(u,v)\neq 0\,.

Both the quantum binomial coefficient in
r
and
s
at
\zeta_{i}
and the classical binomial coefficient in
a
and
b
are elements in
\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]\,
and the powers of
\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta
and
\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta
are signs
\pm 1
.
The vanishing criterion follows from inspection of the quantum binomial term in
r
and
s
.

Importantly, this implies that if
u+v
is a multiple of
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}
, then the expression is non-zero only if also both
u
and
v
are multiples of
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}
as well. In this case,
r=s=0
and the quantum binomial is given by the respective classical binomial up to a sign. A main ingredient in the derivation of (
6.7
) is that the quantum factorial for
u
in
\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]
is divisible by
[\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}]^{a}
and can thus be evaluated at
\zeta_{i}
. More precisely, we have for
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}>1
that

(6.8)

\displaystyle\left.\frac{[u]_{q_{i}}!}{[\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}]_{q_{i}}^{a}}\right|_{q_{i}\rightarrow\zeta_{i}}=\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{i}^{ar}\cdot\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta_{i}^{\binom{a}{2}}\cdot[r]_{\zeta_{i}}!\cdot a!\cdot\mathcal{D}_{i}^{a}\,,

where the vertical line indicates the map to
\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]\,
. We will later use the following basic consequence of Lemma
6.1
for the mulitnomial coefficients from (
3.7
).

Corollary 6.2
.

Suppose
a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
such that
a_{1}+\ldots+a_{r}=\ell_{i}\,
. Then

\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$a_{1}+\ldots+a_{r}$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
a_{1}\,,\,\ldots\,,\,a_{r}\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{i}=\begin{cases}\;1&\mbox{ if }\,\exists s:\,a_{s}=\ell_{i}\,\mbox{ and }\,a_{t}=0\,\mbox{ for }t\neq s\\
\;0&\mbox{ otherwise }\end{cases}

We will distinguish two types of specializations of quantum groups to roots of unity, one given by the minimal choice
n={\mathsf{e}^{*}}
and the other by the maximal choice
n=\ell\mkern-3.0mu\,
. The notation is as follows, where
{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\in\{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},+,-\}\,
and the indicated extensions of scalars
are with respect to the evaluation maps
q\mapsto\zeta
between the rings in
(
3.8
) and those in (
6.5
).

(6.9)

\displaystyle U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}

\displaystyle=U_{q}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\otimes\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}

\displaystyle U_{\zeta}=U_{q}\otimes\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}

\displaystyle U_{\zeta,\mathbb{Q}}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}

\displaystyle=U_{q}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\otimes\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{19.91692pt}U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}

\displaystyle=U_{q}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\otimes\Lambda_{\zeta,\ell\mkern-3.0mu}

\displaystyle U_{\zeta,\ell}=U_{q}\otimes\Lambda_{\zeta,\ell\mkern-3.0mu}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}

Many properties established for quantum groups at generic
q
in previous sections extend without
changes to these quantum groups at roots of unity.

Corollary 6.3
.

The following statements hold.

i)

The algebras defined in (
6.9
) are free modules over their respective ground rings, with bases given as in Theorem
5.18
.

ii)

The natural inclusions of algebras in (
3.8
) induce respective embeddings for the algebras in (
6.9
).

iii)

All gradings and automorphisms defined in Section
4
factor into well-defined gradings and automorphisms for the algebras in (
6.9
).

The first assertion is obvious, since all modules are free. Similarly, the existence of compatible free bases for the natural inclusions assures that the induced maps are also injective, mapping basis elements to each other. The last assertion is clear as well, since all automorphisms are, in particular, module isomorphisms or module anti-isomorphisms with respect to the conjugations on the ground rings.

In later discussions, we will consider root lattice vectors

\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\alpha}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\cdot\alpha
for a given root
\alpha\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}
in a connected root system

\mathsf{\Phi}

of finite type and fixed
\ell>1\,
.
Let
\mathsf{e}=\max\{d_{i}\}_{i}\in\{1,2,3\}\,
as in Section
2.1
. If
\mathsf{e}
and
\ell
are coprime, then all
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}=\ell
so that
\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\alpha}=\ell\cdot\alpha\,
. Conversely, if
\mathsf{e}>1
and divides
\ell
, we have
\ell_{\alpha}=d_{\alpha}^{-1}\ell
so that

\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\alpha}=\ell\cdot\breve{\alpha}\,
in our convention for coroots.

The collection
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}_{\ell}=\{\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\alpha}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\cdot\alpha:\alpha\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\}
thus has the following properties.

Lemma 6.4
.

We have
\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}_{\ell}=\ell\cdot\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\,

if
\,\gcd(\mathsf{e},\ell)=1\,

and
\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}_{\ell}=\ell\cdot\breve{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}}\,
if
\,\gcd(\mathsf{e},\ell)>1\,
, where
\breve{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}}
denotes the coroot system. Thus
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}_{\ell}
is itself a root system that is canonically isomorphic to either

\mathsf{\Phi}

or

\breve{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}}
.

The Weyl group
\mathscr{W}
of

\mathsf{\Phi}

preserves
\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}_{\ell}\,
and its action coincides with that of the intrinsic Weyl group of
\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}_{\ell}\,
in the sense that

s_{\raise 1.6pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.5}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\alpha}}(\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\beta})=\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{(s_{\alpha}(\beta))}=s_{\alpha}(\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\beta})\,
.
Moreover, the set
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}_{\ell}=\{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}\alpha_{i}\}_{i}
is a basis of
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}_{\ell}\,
.

The assertions are immediate from the preceding discussion, the fact that uniform scaling of a root system does not change its isomorphism class, and well-known properties of coroot systems.

6.2.
Skew-Commutation Relations of Primitive Power Generators

In Lemma 3.1 of
[
21
]
De Concini and Kac observe that
\ell\mkern-3.0mu
-th powers of
E_{\alpha}
and
F_{\alpha}
generators commute with other generators of
U_{\zeta}
up to unit factors. In this section, we will sharpen this result to include the
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}
-th powers, where

\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu/\gcd(\ell\mkern-3.0mu,d_{\alpha})\,
. This extension is required for our later discussion since for
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}<\ell\mkern-3.0mu
, certain subsets of
E_{\alpha}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}}
elements will generate Hopf ideals, while the

E_{\alpha}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu}
elements generally do not give rise to Hopf ideals.

We provide here an explicit and conceptual proof of the commutation relations based on the
\mathbb{o}^{\pm}
-gradings introduced in Section
4.1
and their
\mathscr{W}
-covariance properties. Moreover, statements will be in terms of word-dependent generators, which allows us to study independence of the relations of root orderings.

The function

\mathsf{\kappa}

, defined in (
6.10
), keeps track of the signs in commutation relations. Here
\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{\alpha}=\zeta_{\alpha}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}}=\zeta^{d_{\alpha}\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}}\in\{+1,-1\}
is as in (
6.2
) and
\breve{\alpha}=d^{-1}_{\alpha}\alpha
denotes the coroot, implying the last equality below.

(6.10)

\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}\,:\,\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\times{\mathbb{F}_{2}}^{\Delta}\,\rightarrow\,\{+1,-1\}\qquad(\alpha,\bar{\mu})\,\mapsto\,\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\bar{\mu})$}}=\zeta^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\mathchoice{\left(\alpha|\bar{\mu}\right)}{(\alpha|\bar{\mu})}{(\alpha|\bar{\mu})}{(\alpha|\bar{\mu})}}=\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{\alpha}^{\mathchoice{\left(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu}\right)}{(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu})}{(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu})}{(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu})}}\,.

Note, the respective map
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}^{\Delta}\,\rightarrow\,\{+1,-1\}
, given by the same formula for

(\alpha,\mu)\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}^{\Delta}\,
, is a homomorphism in the
\mu
argument onto the group
\{+1,-1\}\cong\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\,
. The map thus factors into

\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\times{\mathbb{F}_{2}}^{\Delta}
as implied. It is also immediate from
\ell_{\alpha}=\ell_{s(\alpha)}
that

\mathsf{\kappa}

is
\mathscr{W}
-bivariant in the sense that
\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(s(\alpha),s(\bar{\mu}))$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\bar{\mu})$}}
for all
s\in\mathscr{W}\,
.

Note that
\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\bar{\mu})$}}=1\,
for all

\alpha
and
\bar{\mu}\,
if
\mathscr{k}
is odd since in this case
\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{\alpha}=1\,
. The next lemma discusses several cases for even
\mathscr{k}\,
.

Lemma 6.5
.

Let
\mathscr{k}=2\ell\,
.
Suppose
\ell
is odd or

\mathsf{\Phi}

is of oddly laced Lie type
\mathsf{ADEG}
. Then

\,\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\bar{\mu})$}}=\raise 0.09995pt\hbox{$\raise 0.70007pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}$}$}\mkern 0.0mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.92}{$(\bar{\alpha},\bar{\mu})$}}\,
for all
\alpha\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}
and
\bar{\mu}\in\mathbb{F}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
, where

\mathsf{\varepsilon}

is the bihomomorphism

(6.11)

\raise 0.70007pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}$}\,:\;\mathbb{F}_{2}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\times\mathbb{F}_{2}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\,\longrightarrow\,\{+1,-1\}\;:\quad(\bar{\nu},\bar{\mu})\,\mapsto\,\raise 0.09995pt\hbox{$\raise 0.70007pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}$}$}\mkern 0.0mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.92}{$(\bar{\nu},\bar{\mu})$}}=(-1)^{\mathchoice{\left(\bar{\nu}|\bar{\mu}\right)}{(\bar{\nu}|\bar{\mu})}{(\bar{\nu}|\bar{\mu})}{(\bar{\nu}|\bar{\mu})}}\,,

and
\bar{\alpha}
is the image of
\alpha
under the canonical map

\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\rightarrow\mathbb{F}_{2}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\,
.

If
\ell
is even (
\mathscr{k}\equiv 0\mod 4
) and

\mathsf{\Phi}

is of Lie type
\,\mathsf{B}_{n}\,
,
\mathsf{C}_{n}\,
, or
\mathsf{F}_{4}\,
with
n\geq 2\,
, then

(6.12)

\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\bar{\mu})$}}\,=\,(-1)^{\mathchoice{\left(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu}\right)}{(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu})}{(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu})}{(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu})}}\,,

which is not additive in the first argument and, thus, does not extend to a bihomomorphic lattice map.

The assertion for oddly laced types follows from the observations that in these cases
\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{\alpha}=-1
and
\mathchoice{\left(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu}\right)}{(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu})}{(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu})}{(\breve{\alpha}|\bar{\mu})}\equiv\mathchoice{\left(\alpha|\bar{\mu}\right)}{(\alpha|\bar{\mu})}{(\alpha|\bar{\mu})}{(\alpha|\bar{\mu})}\mod 2\,
. Moreover, for types
\mathsf{B},\mathsf{C}
and
\mathsf{F}
and odd
\ell
one verifies
\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{\alpha}=(-1)^{d_{\alpha}}\,
. Note that for
\mathsf{B}
the form
\mathchoice{\left(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,\right)}{(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,)}{(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,)}{(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,)}
is always even so that

\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}=\raise 0.70007pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varepsilon}$}}}$}=1
, given odd
\ell\,
.

For the doubly laced types
\mathsf{BCF}
but with even
\ell
, equation
(
6.12
) follows from the fact that
\raise 1.22343pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.75}{$\boldsymbol{\sim}$}$}\mkern-8.0mu\zeta_{\alpha}=-1
for all
\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\,
.

Failure of additivity for even
\ell
is readily verified for type
\mathsf{B}_{2}
, which occurs as a subsystem in the listed Lie types. If
\alpha_{1}
is the short and
\alpha_{2}
the long root (so,
d_{1}=1
and
d_{2}=2
) one finds that
\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha_{1},\bar{\alpha}_{1})$}}=1
,
\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha_{2},\bar{\alpha}_{1})$}}=-1
, and

\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2},\bar{\alpha}_{1})$}}=1
as
\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}
is also a short root. So, clearly,

\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha_{1},\bar{\alpha}_{1})$}}\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha_{2},\bar{\alpha}_{1})$}}\neq\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2},\bar{\alpha}_{1})$}}\,
, obstructing an extension as a lattice map to
\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\supset{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\,
.

Since

\mathsf{\kappa}

will be more frequently used in combination with the
\mathbb{o}^{\pm}
-gradings from (
4.3
) and (
4.4
) it is convenient to introduce the following functions

\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}

(\,\cdot\,,\cdot\,)^{+}

and

\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}

(\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,)^{-}

. Here
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
is a (non-empty) reduced word and
b
is a

\mathbb{o}^{\pm}
-homogeneous element in either
U_{q}
or
U_{\zeta}
:

(6.13)

\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,b)^{\pm}$}}\,=\,\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\gamma(w),\mathbb{o}^{\pm}(b))$}}\,.

For
w
and
b
as above, suppose
w_{i}\cdot w
is also a reduced word. Using
\gamma(w_{i}\cdot w)=s_{i}(\gamma(w))
,
(
4.26
), and
\mathscr{W}
-bivariance of

\mathsf{\kappa}

(\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,)

we infer that for any
i
,

(6.14)

\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w_{i}\cdot w,\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(b))^{\pm}$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,b)^{\pm}$}}\,.

For a given non-empty, reduced word
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
,
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{w}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\tau(w)}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\gamma(w)}
, and root
\alpha\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}
we now introduce the notation for the respective
primitive power generators
:

(6.15)

X_{w}=E_{w}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{w}}\;,\qquad Y_{w}=F_{w}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{w}}\,,\quad\mbox{and}\quad L_{\alpha}=K^{(\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\cdot\alpha)}\,,

where
K^{\mu}
is as in (
4.1
) and
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\cdot\alpha
indicates the integer multiple of the root vector. That is,
L_{i}=L_{\alpha_{i}}=K_{i}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}}\,
.
For
\mu\in\mathbb{Z}^{\Delta}
,
\mu_{i}=\mu(\alpha_{i})
, and
\eta=\sum_{i}\mu_{i}\ell_{i}\alpha_{i}
set

(6.16)

L^{\mu}=L_{1}^{\mu_{1}}\cdot\ldots\cdot L_{n}^{\mu_{n}}=K^{\eta}\,.

The
\mathbb{w}
-grading in
\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
from Section
4.1
on a generator for
\alpha=\gamma(w)

is then given by

(6.17)

\mathbb{w}(X_{w})=\ell_{\alpha}\cdot\alpha=\frac{\ell}{\gcd(\ell,d_{\alpha})}\cdot\alpha=\begin{cases}\ell\cdot\alpha&\mbox{ if }\gcd(\ell,\mathsf{e})=1\\
\ell\cdot\breve{\alpha}&\mbox{ if }\gcd(\ell,\mathsf{e})=\mathsf{e}\,.\end{cases}

That is, if
\mathsf{e}
and
\ell
are coprime the generators are graded by the lattice of
\ell\cdot\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\cong\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\,
. However, if
\mathsf{e}
divides
\ell
the grading is given by the
\ell
-scaled (but equivalent) version of the lattice of the coroot system
\breve{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}}\,
. So, for example, if
\ell
is even and

\mathsf{\Phi}

is of type
\mathsf{B}_{n}
, then the
X_{w}

generators admit a natural grading in the root lattice for
\mathsf{C}_{n}\,
.

Recall that in Lusztig’s construction of the divided power algebras the elements
X_{w}
and
Y_{w}
are mapped to zero in the specialization
from a
\Lambda_{q}
-algebra to a
\Lambda_{\zeta}
-algebra.
Since the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{j}
are algebra automorphisms and the
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}
are
\mathscr{W}
-invariant, the definition in (
5.1
) readily translates into

(6.18)

X_{w}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{w^{\flat}}(X_{\tau(w)})=\mathit{\Gamma}_{u}(X_{v})\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad Y_{w}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{w^{\flat}}(Y_{\tau(w)})=\mathit{\Gamma}_{u}(Y_{v})\,,

assuming
w=u\cdot v
is reduced and
l(v)\geq 1\,
. Similarly, (
4.24
), (
6.15
), and the same
\mathscr{W}
-invariance imply

(6.19)

\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(L_{\alpha})=L_{s(\alpha)}\qquad\mbox{for all}\;\alpha\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}\;\mbox{ and }\;s\in\mathscr{W}\,.

Various other relations and properties for the
E_{w}
and
F_{w}
generators from Section
5.1
are easily extended to properties of the
X_{w}
and
Y_{w}
elements in the same manner. Remarkably, this includes the following identity that holds for all
\mathscr{k}\,
, due to the identity
\raise 0.8251pt\hbox{$\rotatebox{90.0}{\scalebox{1.15}{$\bullet$}}$}\mkern-8.3mu\zeta^{2}=(-1)^{\ell_{i}-1}
mentioned in Section
6.1
:

(6.20)

\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(X_{i})=-L_{i}^{-1}Y_{i}=-Y_{i}L_{i}^{-1}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(Y_{i})=-L_{i}X_{i}=-X_{i}L_{i}\,.

The following commutation relations for a rank 2 subsystem in
U_{q}^{+}
are obtained from equations (c) and (i) in Section 5.3 and equations (a2) and (a6) in Section 5.4 of
[
46
]
. As in Section
2.7
above, assume for a pair of indices
(i,j)
that
-A_{ji}=d_{i}=1
and
-A_{ij}=d_{j}=\mathsf{e}\in\{1,2,3\}\,
. The index notation for generators is as defined in (
5.2
)
or, specialized to the rank 2 setting, in (
5.19
), where also translations to Lusztig’s conventions are explained.

(6.21)

\displaystyle\mathsf{e}=1\quad

\displaystyle\left\{{\quad\begin{aligned} \rule[-5.69054pt]{0.0pt}{14.22636pt}E_{i}^{k}E_{j}&=q^{-k}E_{j}E_{i}^{k}+q^{-1}[k]_{i}E_{(ij)}E_{i}^{k-1}\end{aligned}}\right.

(6.22)

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{36.98857pt}\mathsf{e}=2\quad

\displaystyle\left\{{\quad\begin{aligned} E_{j}^{k}E_{i}&=q^{-2k}E_{i}E_{j}^{k}+q^{-2}[k]_{j}E_{(ji)}E_{j}^{k-1}\\
\rule{0.0pt}{18.49428pt}E_{i}^{k}E_{j}&=q^{2k}E_{j}E_{i}^{k}-q^{(k-1)}[k]_{i}E_{i}^{k-1}E_{(ji)}-q^{2(k-1)}[k]_{i}[k-1]_{i}E_{i}^{k-2}E_{(jij)}\end{aligned}}\right.

(6.23)

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{51.21495pt}\mathsf{e}=3\quad

\displaystyle\left\{{\quad\begin{aligned} E_{j}^{k}E_{i}&=q^{-3k}E_{i}E_{j}^{k}+q^{-3}[k]_{j}E_{(ji)}E_{j}^{k-1}\\
\rule{0.0pt}{18.49428pt}E_{i}^{k}E_{j}&=q^{3k}E_{j}E_{i}^{k}-q^{(k-1)}[k]_{i}E_{i}^{k-1}E_{(ji)}-q^{2(k-1)}[k]_{i}[k-1]_{i}E_{i}^{k-2}E_{(jiji)}\\
&\quad\;-q^{3(k-1)}[k]_{i}[k-1]_{i}[k-2]_{i}E_{i}^{k-3}E_{(jijij)}\end{aligned}}\right.

Since all equations in (
6.21
) are well-defined equations in
U_{q}^{+}
over
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}

they descend to the same equations in
U_{\zeta}^{+}
or
U_{\zeta}
via (
6.9
), upon specializing
q\mapsto\zeta\,
with the previous assumptions in the order of
\zeta
. If we set

in the equations with an

-term and
k=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{j}
in equations with an
E_{j}^{k}
-term, only the first term on the right side of each equation remains, since

[\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}]_{i}=[\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{j}]_{j}=0
by the restriction in (

).
The resulting relations can be summarized in the following lemma, where
X_{s}=X_{\alpha_{s}}=E_{s}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{s}}
.

Lemma 6.6
.

For all
r,s\in\{1,\ldots,n\}
we have
X_{s}E_{r}=\zeta^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{s}d_{s}A_{sr}}E_{r}X_{s}\,
.

Proof.

If
r\neq s
and
A_{rs}\neq 0
the
\zeta
power is easily verified to be identical to the respective lead coefficient in the formulae in (
6.21
) for
(s,r)=(i,j)
and
(s,r)=(j,i)\,
. If
A_{rs}=0
,
the relation is clear since
E_{s}
and
E_{r}
strictly commute to begin with. If
r=s
we find
\zeta^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{s}d_{s}A_{ss}}=\zeta^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{s}d_{s}2}=1
by definition and as desired.
∎

Note, further, that the relations in (
3.13
) and (
3.14
) entail commutation relations
E_{s}^{k}K_{r}=q^{-k\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r}\right)}{(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r})}{(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r})}{(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r})}}K_{r}E_{s}
and
[E_{s}^{k},F_{r}]=\delta_{sr}(q_{s}-q_{s}^{-1})^{-1}[k]_{s}E_{s}^{k-1}(q_{s}^{k-1}K_{s}-q_{s}^{-(k-1)}K_{s}^{-1})
in
U_{q}
,
which specialize for
k=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}
and
q\mapsto\zeta
to

(6.24)

X_{s}F_{r}=F_{r}X_{s}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad X_{s}K_{r}=\zeta^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{s}\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r}\right)}{(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r})}{(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r})}{(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r})}}K_{r}X_{s}\;.

Proposition 6.7
.

Let
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
be a non-empty, reduced word and
b
a
\mathbb{o}
-homogeneous element. Then

X_{w}b\,=\,\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,b)^{+}$}}\cdot bX_{w}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad Y_{w}b\,=\,\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,b)^{-}$}}\cdot bY_{w}\,.

Each relation holds in
U_{\zeta}
as well as each
U_{\zeta}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
with
{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\in\{+,-,{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\}\,
, provided the elements in the relation belong to the respective algebra.

Proof.

We begin by considering the relation for
X_{s}=X_{w_{s}}
in the full algebra
U_{\zeta}
. Since

\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w_{s},E_{r})^{+}$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\gamma(w_{s}),\mathbb{o}^{+}(E_{r}))$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha_{s},\alpha_{r})$}}=\zeta^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{s}\mathchoice{\left(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r}\right)}{(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r})}{(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r})}{(\alpha_{s}|\alpha_{r})}}=\zeta^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{s}d_{s}A_{sr}}\,
, Lemma
6.6

implies the desired relation for
b=E_{r}\,
. The calculation for

\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}

(w_{s},K_{r})^{+}

is exactly the same so that, by the second identity in (
6.24
), the assertion also holds for
b=K_{r}\,
. Further, the first identity in (
6.24
) together with
\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w_{s},F_{r})^{+}$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\gamma(w_{s}),\mathbb{o}^{+}(F_{r}))$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha_{s},0)$}}=1\,
shows the commutation formula for
b=F_{r}\,
.

Next, observe that
\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,bc)^{+}$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,b)^{+}$}}\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,c)^{+}$}}
for
\mathbb{o}
-homogeneous elements
b
and
c
because

\mathsf{\kappa}

is a homomorphism in the second argument and
\mathbb{o}
is a grading. Thus, we can establish
X_{s}b=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,b)^{+}$}}\cdot bX_{s}
for any
b=b_{1}\ldots b_{N}
with
b_{j}\in\{E_{r},F_{r},K_{r}\}
by iteration and, by additivity, further extend the relation to all
homogeneous
b\in U_{\zeta}\,
.

The proof for general
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
follows now by induction in
l(w)\,
.
Suppose
w
and
w_{i}\cdot w
are reduced words so that
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(X_{w})=X_{w_{i}\cdot w}\,
by (
6.18
). Assume further the commutation relation holds for
w
and any homogeneous element in
U_{\zeta}\,
. Applying the automorphism
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
to

X_{w}c\,=\,\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,c)^{+}$}}\cdot cX_{w}
then yields

X_{w_{i}\cdot w}b\,=\,\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,c)^{+}$}}\cdot bX_{w_{i}\cdot w}\,
, where
b=\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(c)\,
. From
(
6.14
) we find that
\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,c)^{+}$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w_{i}\cdot w,b)^{+}$}}\,
. Since
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
is a bijection among homogeneous elements, this shows that the relation also holds for
w_{i}\cdot w
and, hence, for all reduced words.

Note that (
5.5
) implies
\Omega(X_{w})=Y_{w}
, and we have

\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,\Omega(b))^{+}$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,b)^{-}$}}
by (
4.17
).
From this, the second relation with
Y_{w}
is inferred by applying
\Omega
to the first, using also that
the
\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(w,b)^{\pm}$}}\in\{+1,-1\}\,
. Finally,
the relations in
U_{\zeta}
imply the same relations in the embedded algebras
U_{\zeta}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\,
via Corollary
6.3
.
ii)
.
∎

Define also
\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,b)^{\circ}$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\mathbb{w}(b))$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\mathbb{o}^{+}(b))$}}\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\mathbb{o}^{-}(b))$}}\,
for a root
\alpha\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}
and a
fully homogeneous element
b
, where the second equality results from

\mathbb{w}=\mathbb{o}^{+}-\mathbb{o}^{-}
, noted in Section
4.1
. Equation
(
4.2
) now immediately implies the following
commutation relations for generators defined
in (

) and (
