):

(6.25)

L_{\alpha}b=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,b)^{\circ}$}}\cdot bL_{\alpha}\qquad\mbox{ and }\qquad L^{\mu}b=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\kappa}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\mu,b)^{\circ}$}}\cdot bL^{\mu}\,.

Commutation relations among the primitive power generators themselves are readily derived from Proposition
6.7
:

(6.26)

X_{v}X_{w}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(v,w)$}}X_{w}X_{v}\,,\qquad Y_{v}Y_{w}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(v,w)$}}Y_{w}Y_{v}\,,\quad\mbox{and}\quad X_{v}Y_{w}=Y_{w}X_{v}

where

(6.27)

\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\pi}}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(v,w)$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\gamma(v),\gamma(w))$}}\qquad\mbox{with}\quad\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\beta)$}}=\zeta^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\beta}\mathchoice{\left(\alpha|\beta\right)}{(\alpha|\beta)}{(\alpha|\beta)}{(\alpha|\beta)}}\in\{+1,-1\}\;.

For the generators
L_{\alpha}
as in (
6.15
) we also derive from

K^{\eta}E_{w}=q^{\mathchoice{\left(\eta|\gamma(w)\right)}{(\eta|\gamma(w))}{(\eta|\gamma(w))}{(\eta|\gamma(w))}}E_{w}K^{\eta}
that

(6.28)

L_{\alpha}X=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\gamma(w))$}}XL_{\alpha}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad L_{\alpha}Y=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\pi}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\gamma(w))$}}YL_{\alpha}\,.

We conclude this section with criteria for strict commutativity of a primitive power generator
X_{v}
with
\alpha=\gamma(v)\,
for non-empty
v\in\mathscr{W}^{*}\,
. As before, we assume that the root system is indecomposable of rank
\geq 2\,
and denote by
\mathscr{k}
the order of
\zeta\,
.

Lemma 6.8
.

The power generator
X_{v}
is central in
U_{\zeta}^{+}
if and only if (at least) one of the following conditions holds.

i)

\mathscr{k}
is odd.

ii)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 2\mod 4
,
d_{\alpha}=2
(that is, the Lie type is
\mathsf{BCF}
and
\alpha
is a long root).

iii)

The Lie type is
\mathsf{B}
and
\alpha
is a short root (that is,
d_{\alpha}=1
).

In these cases
X_{v}
also commutes with all elements in
U_{\zeta}
. The analogous statement holds for
Y_{v}
and
L_{\alpha}
.

Note that the first condition includes all Lie types and was already observed in
[
21
]
. See also the remarks following
Proposition
6.12
below.
The third condition applies to all
\mathscr{k}\,
and it is the only allowed situation if
\mathscr{k}\equiv 0\mod 4\,
. The proof consists of checking for which
\alpha
, Lie types, and orders
\mathscr{k}
we have that
\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha,\bar{\mu})$}}=1
for all
\bar{\mu}
. As a weaker condition, one may consider commutation of
X_{v}
with only the other primitive power generators.

Lemma 6.9
.

X_{v}
commutes with all
X_{w}
if and only if (at least) one of the following conditions holds.

i)

\mathscr{k}
is odd or
\mathscr{k}\equiv 0\mod 8\,
.

ii)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 2\mod 4
and the Lie type is
\mathsf{B}
.

iii)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 2\mod 4
, the Lie type is
\mathsf{CF}
,
and
\alpha
is a long root (
d_{\alpha}=2
).

iv)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 4\mod 8
and the Lie type is

\mathsf{ACDEG}
.

v)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 4\mod 8
, the Lie type is
\mathsf{F}
, and
\alpha
is a short root.

vi)

\mathscr{k}
is arbitrary, the Lie type is
\mathsf{B}
, and
\alpha
is a short root.

In these cases
X_{v}
also commutes with all
Y_{v}
and
L_{\mu}
.
The analogous statement holds for
Y_{v}
and
L_{\alpha}
.

6.3.
Skew-Central Subalgebras and Monomial Bases

The
X_{w}
and
Y_{w}
elements introduced in Section
6.2
generate almost polynomial subalgebras whose indeterminate variables commute up to signs. This section establishes the basic properties of these algebras and classifies when they are central, commutative but not central, or neither. We begin with definitions of the monomial elements in analogy to those introduced in Section
5.3
.

Let
\mathfrak{l}\in\mathbb{N}_{0}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}}
be the length function
\mathfrak{l}(\alpha)=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\,
and, for
\psi\in\mathbb{N}_{0}^{A}
with
A\subseteq\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}
, denote by
\mathfrak{l}\cdot\psi
the point-wise product

(\mathfrak{l}\cdot\psi)(\alpha)=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\psi(\alpha)\in\mathbb{N}_{0}\,
. For a non-empty, reduced word
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}\,
,

\psi\in\mathcal{E}(s)\,
with
s=\mathscr{r}(w)\,
,
and with conventions as for (
5.20
), set

(6.29)

{X}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\,=\,{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathfrak{l}\cdot\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-10.58493pt}{\hskip-10.58493pt}{\hskip-6.91838pt}{\hskip-5.46194pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\,=\,X_{w[\beta_{1}]}^{\psi(\beta_{1})}\ldots X_{w[\beta_{L}]}^{\psi(\beta_{L})}\,=\,E_{w[\beta_{1}]}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\beta_{1}}\psi(\beta_{1})}\ldots E_{w[\beta_{L}]}^{\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\beta_{L}}\psi(\beta_{L})}\,.

Analogously, we denote

,
{Y}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}={F}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathfrak{l}\cdot\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-10.58493pt}{\hskip-10.58493pt}{\hskip-6.91838pt}{\hskip-5.46194pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}

(6.30)

\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\varsigma\,}\!}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\varsigma\,}\!}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\varsigma\,}\!}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\varsigma\,}\!}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\psi,\chi)_{w,u}$}}=\prod_{\begin{subarray}{c}\alpha\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\\

for which we observe that
\;\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varsigma}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varsigma}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varsigma}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varsigma}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\psi,\phi)_{w}$}}\,\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varsigma}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\varsigma}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varsigma}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\varsigma}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\phi,\psi)_{w}$}}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\varsigma\,}\!}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\hat{\varsigma\,}\!}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\varsigma\,}\!}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\hat{\varsigma\,}\!}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\psi,\phi)_{w,w}$}}\,
.

The commutation relations from (
6.26
) readily generalize to

with

.

-scaled exponent set

(6.34)

(\mathfrak{l},s)\,=\,\mathfrak{l}\cdot\mathcal{E}(s)\,=\,\left\{\phi\,:\,\phi(\alpha)\in\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\mathbb{N}_{0}\right\}\,.

In the notation from (
5.35
) we thus have
{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-11.07605pt}{\hskip-7.91145pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}=\{{X}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}:\,\psi\in\mathcal{E}(s)\}\,
and analogous identities for

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w
,

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},-\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
, and

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},-\hskip-3.01389pt

\scriptstyle{\mathsf{S}},\pm\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
from

) for these ground rings
\Lambda\,
.

Proposition 6.10
.

Suppose
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
and
s=\mathscr{r}(w)
.
Then both

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
and

{\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w
are
\Lambda
-bases for
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}\,
.
In particular,
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}={\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-11.07605pt}{\hskip-7.91145pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-16.1402pt}{\hskip-11.52873pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.68861pt}\!\!={\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-11.07605pt}{\hskip-7.91145pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-27.50525pt}{\hskip-27.50525pt}{\hskip-16.71185pt}{\hskip-11.93704pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 27.50525pt}
.

The subalgebra
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}\,
is isomorphic to the abstract
\Lambda
-algebra with
1
, freely generated by elements

{X}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-26.68861pt}{\hskip-16.1402pt}{\hskip-11.52873pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.68861pt}
and subject to the first set of relations in (
6.32
).
The analogous statements for
\mathcal{Z}^{-}_{w}\,
apply.

The subalgebra
\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{s}\,
is generated by
L_{i}^{\pm 1}
with
i\in J({s})\,
as in Section
2.3
. It is thus isomorphic to the group algebra
\Lambda\left[\left\{L_{i}^{\pm}:\,i\in J({s})\right\}\right]\cong\Lambda\left[{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Xi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Xi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Xi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Xi}$}}}(s)}\right]\,
.

Proof.

The relations in (
6.32
) imply that for any
v\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
with
v\leq_{R}w
we have

X_{v}\cdot{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-11.07605pt}{\hskip-7.91145pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\subseteq{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-11.07605pt}{\hskip-7.91145pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\!
, writing
X_{v}={X}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\chi_{\alpha}$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-7.46442pt}{\hskip-7.46442pt}{\hskip-4.98819pt}{\hskip-4.34554pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}

with
\chi_{\alpha}
the indicator function for
\alpha=\gamma(v)\,
. Thus

\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}=\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}\cdot 1\subseteq{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-11.07605pt}{\hskip-7.91145pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
. From
the definition in (
6.29
), it is further clear that
1
is a cyclic element of

{\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}

as a
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
-module and hence
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}={\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-20.14017pt}{\hskip-11.07605pt}{\hskip-7.91145pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\!
as desired. Linear independence established in Section
5
then completes the proof of the first claim. Independence under reversal of the direction of multiplication is
immediate from (
6.32
).

It is clear that the set of generators
{X}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}
of an abstractly defined algebra with relations as in
(
6.32
) is also a basis. Thus, the canonical map from this algebra onto
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
is an
isomorphism of
\Lambda
-modules and, hence, also an algebra isomorphism.

By its definition,
\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{s}\,
is the
\Lambda
-span of all
K^{\nu}
with
\nu
in the root
sublattice generated by all
\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\alpha}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\cdot\alpha\,
with
\alpha\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\,
.
Following Lemma
6.4
, we consider the root system
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}_{\ell}
with the same Weyl group
action. Since, clearly,
s(\alpha)\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{-}}
iff
s(\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\alpha})\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{-}}_{\ell}
the
inversion set
\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)_{\ell}

with respect to
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}_{\ell}
is given precisely by
\{\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\alpha}:\,\alpha\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\}
.
By Lemma
2.10
the root sublattice generated by this set is spanned by the simple roots
of
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}_{\ell}
with indices in
J({s})\,
. By Lemma
6.4
these are

\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\alpha_{i}}=\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{i}\alpha_{i}
, yielding the
L_{i}=K^{\raise 3.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.7}{$\ell$}}\mkern-2.0mu{\alpha_{i}}}
as free generators.
∎

The next observations are consequences of (
6.33
), particularly, in the case when
the word in the
\mho
formula is maximal so that
r=1\,
. The stated equivariance under the
antipode follows from (
4.16
).

Corollary 6.11
.

Suppose

Using division with remainder pointwise for each
\alpha
, any
\phi\in\mathcal{E}(s)
can be uniquely written as
\phi=\mathfrak{l}\cdot\psi+\rho
with
\rho\in[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s}
, where

(6.37)

[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s}=\left\{{\psi\in\mathcal{E}(s)\,:\,\psi(\alpha)<\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{\alpha}\;,\;\forall\alpha\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)}\right\}\quad\mbox{and}\qquad[0,\mathfrak{l})_{\bullet}=[0,\mathfrak{l})_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}\,.

It is now immediate that the multiplication map below is an isomorphism of
\Lambda
-modules, mapping pairs of PBW basis elements to another PBW basis element up to a sign.

(6.38)

\mathscr{m}^{+}_{w}:\,\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}\otimes_{\Lambda}{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-12.82538pt}{\hskip-9.77255pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\!\longrightarrow\,{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}

\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt

-module with its left regular action given by the signed shifts in (

for some

Note also that

\scriptstyle[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s},+\hskip-3.01389pt

, these are clearly different spaces. We will, however, prove below that
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
only depends on

for almost all Lie types.

Recall from Theorem
5.18
and Corollary
6.3
that
{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-3.77936pt}{\hskip-2.70573pt}{\hskip-2.45294pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}=U_{\zeta}^{+}
for a reduced word

w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
of maximal length. Variations of (
6.36
) and (
6.38
) are readily derived
with reversed directions or replacing
E
’s by
F
’s and
X
’s by
Y
’s.

Similar to the full quantum groups, we introduce combined subalgebras such as

(6.39)

\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{w}=\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}\cdot\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{s}\;,\quad\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{w}=\mathcal{Z}^{-}_{w}\cdot\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{s}\;,\quad\mbox{and}\quad\mathcal{Z}_{w}=\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}\cdot\mathcal{Z}^{-}_{w}\cdot\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{s}\,,

where
s=\mathscr{r}(w)
. Analogous statements about PBW bases and identifications with signed polynomial algebras hold for each of these subalgebras. Since all elements in
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
commute with all elements in
\mathcal{Z}^{-}_{w}
we do not require the denominators
(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{-1}
so that each
\mathcal{Z}_{w}
is well-defined over
\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\,
.
We next record the precise criteria for these subalgebras to be strictly central or strictly commutative.

Proposition 6.12
.

Suppose
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
is non-empty,
s=\mathscr{r}(w)\,
, and
{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\in\{\phantom{+},+,{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\}
.
The algebra
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
is central in
U_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
if and only if (at least) one of the following conditions holds:

i)

\mathscr{k}
is odd (any Lie type).

ii)

\mathscr{k}\not\equiv 0\mod 4
and the Lie type is
\mathsf{B}
.

iii)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 2\mod 4
, the Lie type is
\mathsf{CF}
,
and
s\in\mathscr{W}_{S}
.

iv)

Lie type is
\mathsf{B}
and
s\in\mathscr{W}_{L}
(any
\mathscr{k}
).

Thus, if
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
, then
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
is central if and only if (at least) one of
i)
and
ii)
hold. Analogous statements hold for
\mathcal{Z}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}_{w}\,
.

The subgroups
\mathscr{W}_{L}
and
\mathscr{W}_{S}
are as defined in (
2.17
). The one referred to in items
iii)
and
iv)
are of order 2 for the
\mathsf{B,C}
types and of order 6 for
\mathsf{F}_{4}
by Lemma
2.5
. The assertions in
Proposition
6.12
are readily derived from Lemma
6.8
. We note that the last statement for maximal words is commensurable with Corollary 3.1 of
[
21
]
. The elements considered there in part (b) correspond to our
X_{w}
if
\alpha=\gamma(w)
is a short root but to our
X_{w}^{2}
if
\alpha
is a long root in case
\mathscr{k}
is a multiple of 4. Requiring centrality of
X_{w}
rather than
X_{w}^{2}
then excludes this case.

In order to formulate criteria for commutativity of the subalgebras, we say that an element
s\in\mathscr{W}
is

mod-2 discrete
if

(6.40)

\mathchoice{\left(\breve{\alpha}|\beta\right)}{(\breve{\alpha}|\beta)}{(\breve{\alpha}|\beta)}{(\breve{\alpha}|\beta)}\equiv 0\,\mod 2\qquad\forall\alpha,\beta\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\;\mbox{ with }\,d_{\alpha}\geq d_{\beta}\,.

For example, for Lie type
\mathsf{A}_{5}
and
s=s_{1}s_{3}s_{6}
we have
\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)=\{\alpha_{1},\alpha_{3},\alpha_{6}\}
, which are all orthogonal so that
s
is mod-2 discrete. For non-simply laced types we will also call an element
s\in\mathscr{W}

mod-2 long discrete
if condition (
6.40
) is required only for pairs
\alpha,\beta\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)_{L}
.
The notion of
mod-2 short discrete
is analogous.

Proposition 6.13
.

Suppose
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
is non-empty and
s=\mathscr{r}(w)
. The subalgebra
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
is commutative if and only if (at least) one of the following conditions holds:

i)

s
is mod-2 discrete (any Lie type and
\mathscr{k}
).

ii)

\mathscr{k}
is odd or
\mathscr{k}\equiv 0\mod 8
(any Lie type).

iii)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 0\mod 4
and the Lie type is
\mathsf{ADEG}
.

iv)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 2\mod 4
, the Lie type is
\mathsf{BCF}
,
and
s
is mod-2 short discrete.

v)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 4\mod 8
, the Lie type is
\mathsf{BCF}

and
s
is mod-2 long discrete.

The identical statement holds for
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{w}\,
.

The extension from
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
to
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{w}
holds since, by (
6.28
), the sign occurring in the commutation of
X_{\alpha}
with
X_{\beta}
(with respect to some order) is
the same as the one in the commutation of
X_{\alpha}
with
L_{\beta}\,
. Note also that for type

\mathsf{A}_{1}
case
i)
holds for any
s\,
.

For the maximal case, observe that the longest element
{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}\in\mathscr{W}
is never mod-2 discrete for any Lie type of rank
\geq 2
. In the non-simply laced case we have that
{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}\in\mathscr{W}
is mod-2 short discrete if and only if the Lie type is
\mathsf{B}
. It is
mod-2 long discrete if and only if the Lie type is
\mathsf{C}\,
. This yields the following characterization of maximal commutative subalgebras, which can also be derived from Lemma
6.9
.

Corollary 6.14
.

Let
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
be a reduced word of maximal length. Then
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{z}
is commutative if and only if (at least) one of the following applies:

i)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 0,1,3,5,\mbox{ or }7\mod 8\,
(any Lie type).

ii)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 2\mbox{ or }6\mod 8\,
and the Lie type is
\mathsf{B}\,
.

iii)

\mathscr{k}\equiv 4\mod 8\,
and the Lie type is
\mathsf{ACDEG}
.

iv)

The Lie type is
\mathsf{A}_{1}
(any
\mathscr{k}
).

The identical statement holds for
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{z}\,
.

Remark 6.15
.

Corollary
6.14
implies that
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{z}
in type
\mathsf{B}_{2}=\mathsf{C}_{2}
is commutative for any
\mathscr{k}
and any
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
. However, it is central only if
\mathscr{k}
is not a multiple of 4 .
∎

It is immediate from Proposition
6.10
that, if
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
is strictly commutative, it is isomorphic to a free polynomial algebra, assigning each
X_{v}
with
v\leq_{R}w
to an in indeterminate
x_{\alpha}
, where
\alpha=\gamma(v)\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\,
and
s=\mathscr{r}(w)\,
. That is,

(6.41)

\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}\,\cong\,\Lambda\left[\{x_{\alpha}:\alpha\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\}\right]\,.

Comparing the criteria in Propositions
6.12
and Corollary
6.14
, we note that there are various situations in which the subalgebras are commutative but not central. Given a maximal
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
,
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
has this property if
\mathscr{k}\equiv 0\mod 8
for any Lie type
as well as if
\mathscr{k}\equiv 4\mod 8
and the Lie type is
neither
\mathsf{B}
nor
\mathsf{F}\,
. So, for example, in the simply laced cases
(\mathsf{ADE})
and
\mathscr{k}\equiv 0\mod 4

we have that
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
is commutative as in (
6.41
) but for any
b\in U_{q}
with
\mu=\mathbb{o}^{+}(b)
and
\alpha=\gamma(v)
we have

(6.42)

X_{v}b=(-1)^{\mathchoice{\left(\alpha|\mu\right)}{(\alpha|\mu)}{(\alpha|\mu)}{(\alpha|\mu)}}bX_{v}\,.

6.4.
\mho
-Invariance and Word Independence of
\mathcal{Z}_{w}

The definition of the algebras
\mathcal{Z}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}_{w}
in
Section
6.3

a priori
depends on a choice of a word
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}\,
. In this section, we show for Lie types different from
\mathsf{G}_{2}
that
\mathcal{Z}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}_{w}
depends
only on the respective Weyl element
s=\mathscr{r}(w)\,
, employing the techniques from Section
5.7
.

We begin with the derivation of formulae for the action of
\mho
on generators in
U_{q}
, starting with the generic case and coefficients in
\mathbb{Q}(q)\,
.
We continue here the conventions from Section
5.4
,
with
i
the index of a short root
(d_{i}=1)

and
j
the index of a (possibly) long root
(d_{j}=\mathsf{e})
.
Observe that specializing the left side of (
5.50
) to
z=-1
and
\mathscr{u}_{j}(\vec{n})=0
yields the expression for
E^{(N)}_{(ji)}
in (
5.52
) multiplied by
(-1)^{N}\,
. Similarly, for
z=-1
and
\mathscr{u}_{i}(\vec{n})=0
,
the left side of (
5.51
) yields the expression for
E^{(N)}_{b_{m-1}}
in (
5.52
) multiplied by
(-1)^{\mathsf{e}N}\,
. The products over the respective
(1-q_{\alpha}^{-2t})=q_{\alpha}^{-t}(q_{\alpha}-q_{\alpha}^{-1})[t]_{\alpha}
terms are then expressed as factorials, resulting in the following formulae.

In either case, we may specialize the identity to a root of unity
\zeta
, assuming that
\ell>\mathsf{e}\,
where

\ell
is the order of
\zeta^{2}\,
. This allows us, in particular, to derive
expansions for
X_{(ji)}=E^{\ell}_{(ji)}
and
X_{b_{m-1}}=E^{\ell_{j}}_{b_{m-1}}

in terms of the
{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle(\phi)$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-9.89171pt}{\hskip-9.89171pt}{\hskip-5.91403pt}{\hskip-4.22432pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-72.8805pt}{\hskip-52.68301pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 119.56487pt}
basis elements. The number of
non-zero terms will depend in either case on whether
\ell=\ell_{j}
or
\ell>\ell_{j}\,
, that is,
whether
\gcd(\ell,\mathsf{e})=1
or not. To keep subsequent formulae more compact, it is convenient to introduce

(6.49)

\mathfrak{d}=\gcd(\ell,\mathsf{e})\,\in\,\{1,\mathsf{e}\}

for given
\ell
and
\mathsf{e}
. Using the Kronecker notation, we can then express the evaluation of
the factorial ratio from (
3.6
) at
q=\zeta\,
as

(6.50)

\left\{\ell_{j}\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu\mathsf{e}\right\}\,=\,\delta_{\mathfrak{d},1}\cdot\mathsf{e}\cdot\zeta^{-(\mathsf{e}-1)\binom{\ell+1}{2}}\,,

implying that
\left\{\ell_{j}\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu\mathsf{e}\right\}=0
if
\ell\mkern-3.0mu_{j}<\ell\,
. The other factorial ratio
from (
3.6
) can be evaluated at
q=\zeta\,
using (
6.4
).

Lemma 6.16
.

Suppose
\ell=\mathsf{e}\cdot\ell_{j}
. Then

[\ell_{j}\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu\mathsf{e}]\mkern-1.6mu{\rotatebox[origin]{180.0}{!}}\mkern-1.6mu{\rotatebox[origin]{180.0}{!}}=\mathsf{e}\cdot\zeta^{-\binom{\mathsf{e}}{2}\ell_{j}^{2}}\cdot(\zeta^{-1}-\zeta)^{-(\mathsf{e}-1)\ell_{j}}\,.

Another quantity that frequently appears in the computations below is the expression

(6.51)

{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{j}\mkern-1.0mu\coloneqq(\zeta_{j}-\zeta_{j}^{-1})^{\ell_{j}}=[\mathsf{e}]^{\ell_{j}}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{\ell_{j}}\,.

This is the singularization factor of
X_{j}
in the sense of (
5.10
), as we introduce the analogous notation
\breve{X}_{j}=\breve{E}^{\ell_{j}}_{j}=(-1)^{\ell_{j}}{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{j}\mkern-1.0muE_{j}^{\ell_{j}}
.
Notice also that
{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{j}\mkern-1.0mu^{\mathfrak{d}}={\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{i}\mkern-1.0mu\cdot[\mathsf{e}]^{\ell}
.

The next two propositions consider the specializations of (
6.45
) and (
6.46
) to a root of unity
\zeta
with

and

, respectively.
These yield explicit expressions for

and

Proposition 6.17
.

We have
X_{(ji)}\in\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}}
as a ring over

\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]
, given by

(6.52)

\displaystyle(-1)^{\ell}X_{(ji)}

\displaystyle=\,\zeta_{j}^{\ell}X_{a_{m-1}}\,+\,\zeta_{j}^{\binom{\ell}{2}}{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{j}\mkern-1.0mu^{\mathfrak{d}}X_{j}^{\mathfrak{d}}X_{i}\,+\,(1-\delta_{\mathfrak{d},1})\cdot\mathsf{e}\cdot(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{-\ell}\cdot T_{1}\vskip 22.76219pt

\displaystyle\mbox{where}

\displaystyle T_{1}=\begin{cases}(-\zeta)^{\ell_{j}}{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{j}\mkern-1.0mu^{2}X_{j}X_{(ij)}&\mathsf{e}=2\\
(-\zeta_{j})^{-\ell_{j}^{2}}{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{j}\mkern-1.0mu^{3}X_{j}^{2}X_{(ij)}\,+\,\zeta_{j}^{-\binom{\ell_{j}+1}{2}}{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{j}\mkern-1.0mu^{2}X_{j}X_{(ijij)}&\mathsf{e}=3\,.\end{cases}

The computation starts with the observation that, by Corollary
6.2
, we only need to consider cases in which one of the terms in the large multinomial coefficient for each
\llparenthesis\phi,j\rrparenthesis_{\mathsf{e}}
in
(
6.47
) is equal to
\ell
and all the other
k_{s}
with
1\leq s\leq m-1
are zero. The value of
k_{m}
is then determined via

\mathscr{u}_{j}(\phi)=0
and (
5.44
) from the non-zero
k_{s}\,
.

The first term in (
6.52
) results from the case
k_{m-1}=\ell
and all other
k_{s}=0
. The second term accounts for the case
k_{1}=k_{m}=\ell
and all other
k_{s}=0
. Note also that
2k_{3}=\ell
for
\mathsf{e}=3
will still lead to
\llparenthesis\phi,j\rrparenthesis_{\mathsf{e}}=0
due to the extra binomial term.

All other cases require that
\mathsf{e}
divides
\ell
, meaning
\mathfrak{d}=\mathsf{e}>1\,
and
\ell=\mathsf{e}\ell_{j}
. For
\mathsf{e}=2

the only remaining situation is then
k_{2}=k_{4}=\ell_{j}
and
k_{1}=k_{3}=0
.
For
\mathsf{e}=3
we have two cases, the first of which is

k_{2}=\ell_{j}
,
k_{6}=2\ell_{j}
and
k_{1}=k_{3}=k_{4}=k_{5}=0
. The second is
given by
k_{4}=\ell_{j}
,
k_{6}=\ell_{j}
and
k_{1}=k_{2}=k_{3}=k_{5}=0
.

The coefficients for each of these values of
k_{s}
are then worked out using Lemma
6.16
. Next, we provide the expressions for
X_{b_{m-1}}
, where we use the additional notation

(6.53)

\mathfrak{n}=\frac{\mathsf{e}}{\mathfrak{d}}\qquad\mbox{so that}\qquad\mathfrak{n}\cdot\ell=\mathsf{e}\cdot\ell_{j}\,.

Note that the third term in (
6.54
) is non-zero only if
\mathsf{e}>1
and
\gcd(\ell,\mathsf{e})=1
. As remarked in Section
6.1
this condition
implies that
[\mathsf{e}]
is a unit, meaning
[\mathsf{e}]^{-1}\in\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]
. Analogous to
(
6.51
) we also write

{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{i}\mkern-1.0mu=(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{\ell}
.

Proposition 6.18
.

We have
X_{b_{m-1}}\in\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}}
as a ring over

\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]
, given by

(6.54)

\displaystyle(-1)^{\mathsf{e}\ell_{j}}X_{b_{m-1}}

\displaystyle=\,\zeta_{j}^{\ell_{j}}X_{(ij)}\,+\,\zeta^{\binom{{\mathfrak{n}\cdot\ell}}{2}}{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{i}\mkern-1.0mu^{\mathfrak{n}}X_{j}X_{i}^{\mathfrak{n}}\,+\,\delta_{\mathfrak{d},1}\cdot(1-\delta_{\mathsf{e},1})\cdot\mathsf{e}\cdot[\mathsf{e}]^{-\ell}\cdot T_{2}\vskip 22.76219pt

\displaystyle\mbox{where}

\displaystyle T_{2}=\begin{cases}\zeta^{\ell}{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{i}\mkern-1.0muX_{(iji)}X_{i}&\mathsf{e}=2\\
\zeta^{-\binom{\ell}{2}}{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{i}\mkern-1.0muX_{(iji)}X_{i}\,+\,\zeta^{\ell(\ell+1)}{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{i}\mkern-1.0mu^{2}X_{(ijiji)}X_{i}^{2}&\mathsf{e}=3\,.\end{cases}

As for Proposition
6.17
, the only contributing terms are those for which exactly one of
the integers in the multinomial expressions of (
6.48
) is
\ell_{j}
and all others are zero, once we set
N=\ell_{j}\,
and
q=\zeta
in (
6.46
). The first term in (
6.54
) accounts for the case when
k_{2}=\ell_{j}
, implying by
\mathscr{u}_{i}=0
that all other
k_{s}=0
. The second term
corresponds to the case
k_{m}=\ell_{j}
, which entails

and all remaining

.

The last terms for
\mathsf{e}>1
all involve coefficients
\left\{\ell_{j}\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu\mathsf{e}\right\}
, which, by
(
6.50
), are non-zero only if
\mathfrak{d}=1\,
and hence
\ell=\ell_{j}\,
. The extra term for
\mathsf{e}=2
corresponds to
k_{3}=k_{1}=\ell_{j}=\ell
and all other indices zero. As before, for
\mathsf{e}=3
we only need to consider the cases

and

, which imply

and

, respectively.

Comparing Propositions
6.17
and
6.18
, we note that additional terms and exponents occur in the non-simply laced cases in exactly the opposite situations with respect
to whether
\ell
and
\mathsf{e}
are coprime or not. In addition, a term by term matching, up to coefficients, can also be achieved by switching an
X_{a_{j}}
by an
X_{a_{m+1-j}}\,
. This
can be thought of replacing the underlying root system by a corresponding coroot system as in (

.

We discuss a normalization of the generators
X_{\alpha}
in Appendix
D
for which the above formulae are integral. The main application of (
6.52
) and (
6.54
) word independence of the skew-central subalgebras.

Theorem 6.19
.

Suppose

\mathsf{\Phi}

is not of Lie type
\mathsf{G}_{2}
. Assume
w,u\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
are reduced words for the same Weyl element
s=\mathscr{r}(w)=\mathscr{r}(u)
. Then
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}=\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{u}
as
\mathbb{w}
-graded subalgebras in
U_{\zeta}^{+}
over
\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\,
.

Proof.

By Proposition
6.10

\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
is as a
\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
-module given by

{\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w
. We note that
(\mathfrak{l},s)
, as defined in (
6.34
),
is of the form prescribed in
(
5.65
) by choosing
{V\mkern-5.0mu}_{d}=\ell_{d}\cdot\mathbb{N}_{0}
with
\ell_{d}=\ell/\gcd(d,\ell)\,
.

Following Corollary
5.15
it thus suffices to show
that
\mho
maps
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}}\!={\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-112.48584pt}{\hskip-112.48584pt}{\hskip-68.04858pt}{\hskip-49.23164pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-119.56487pt}{\hskip-72.8805pt}{\hskip-52.68301pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 119.56487pt}\!\!

to itself for any pair

(i,j)
that occurs for relator pairs.
Now,

{\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}
is spanned by monomials in the skew-commuting generators
X_{a_{s}}
. Note also that by (
5.32
) and (
5.16
) and with words as in (
2.32
) we also have

(6.55)

\mho(X_{a_{s}})=X_{b_{m+1-s}}\,.

Thus
\mho
-invariance of the space

{\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},s)},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}
is given by showing that it contains all

X_{b_{k}}
. This is obvious for
X_{b_{1}}=X_{j}
and
X_{b_{m}}=X_{i}\,
, implied, for example, by (
5.18
).
For
X_{b_{2}}=X_{(ji)}
this is verified in Proposition
6.17
and for

X_{b_{m-1}}
in Proposition
6.18
. Thus, if
m\in\{3,4\}
all cases are covered.

By construction any
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
inherits the
\mathbb{w}
-grading from
U_{\zeta}
since it admits a
\mathbb{w}
-graded basis. The graded components of
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
and

\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{u}
thus also have to coincide.
∎

Missing from the proof for the
\mathsf{G}_{2}
Lie type are computations that show also
X_{b_{3}}
and
X_{b_{4}}

can be written as a polynomial expression in the
\{X_{a_{i}}\}
only, meaning they are in

{\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle{(\mathfrak{l},\mathchoice{{s}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{s}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}
. We leave this as a question, which appears to be open, at least for even
\mathscr{k}\,
.

Conjecture 6.20
.

Theorem
6.19
extends also to the
\mathsf{G}_{2}
case for all
\mathscr{k}>6
.

For Lie types different from
\mathsf{G}_{2}
, we may thus unambiguously
write
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{s}
for an element in
s\in\mathscr{W}
. In the
\mathsf{G}_{2}
case,

\mathcal{Z}_{s}^{+}
is, of course, also well-defined for
l(s)\leq 5
,
since there is only one reduced expression for such
s\,
. For the longest element

{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}\,
, there are exactly two reduced expressions. So,
the only missing equality between subalgebras addressed by this conjecture is
the one between

\mathcal{Z}_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}}^{+}
and
\mathcal{Z}_{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}^{+}\,
.

Assuming the other Lie types, we denote the maximal subalgebras associated to
the unique longest element
{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}\in\mathscr{W}
as

(6.56)

\mathcal{Z}^{\pm}_{\bullet}=\mathcal{Z}^{\pm}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}\,,\quad\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}=\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\bullet}\cdot\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{\bullet}\,,\quad\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}=\mathcal{Z}^{-}_{\bullet}\cdot\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{\bullet}\,,\,\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}=\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\bullet}\cdot\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{\bullet}\cdot\mathcal{Z}^{-}_{\bullet}\,,

where
\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{\bullet}
is the full subalgebra generated by the
L_{i}\,
.
Also immediate from the definition is that

(6.57)

\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{t}\subseteq\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{s}\qquad\forall s,t\in\mathscr{W}\;\mbox{ with }\;t\leq_{R}s\,.

Analogous statements hold for the
\mathcal{Z}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}_{s}
algebras with
{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\in\{\phantom{+},-,{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\}
. Note also that Corollary
6.35
and Theorem
6.19
imply for these Lie types

(6.58)

\Omega(\mathcal{Z}_{s}^{\pm})=\mathcal{Z}_{s}^{\mp}\,,\qquad\mho(\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{\pm})=\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{\pm}\,,\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad S(\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}})=\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\;.

Combining this with
\mho
-correspondence with Lusztig’s conventions from
Proposition
5.5
we make the following observations.

Corollary 6.21
.

The maximal algebras in (
6.56
) remain unchanged if the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
are replaced by

T_{i}
in the definition of the generators
E_{w}
and
X_{w}\,
.

We conclude this section with a proof that the full maximal algebra is invariant under the actions of Lusztig’s
T_{i}
automorphisms. It uses the explicit expression of the Garside element
\mathit{\Gamma}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}\,
from Section
5.2
.

Theorem 6.22
.

Assuming Lie types other than
\mathsf{G}_{2}
and any
\mathscr{k}>2\mathsf{e}
(or
\mathscr{k}=3
for
\mathsf{e}=2
), the full algebra
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}
over
\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
is invariant under the
Artin group action generated by the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}\,
.

Proof.

Invariance of
\mathcal{Z}^{0}_{\bullet}
under
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
follows immediately from (
6.19
) and Proposition
6.10
. It thus suffices to show
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\bullet})\subset\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}\,
for each fixed
i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\,
,
which implies
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(\mathcal{Z}^{-}_{\bullet})\subset\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}\,
via
(
6.58
) and commutation of
\Omega
with
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}\,
.

Let
u\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
be a reduced word for
q_{\eta(i)}=s_{i}\cdot{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}={s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}\cdot s_{\eta(i)}
as in (
2.22
) so that
z=w_{i}\cdot u
and
w=u\cdot w_{\eta(i)}
are maximal reduced words

z,w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}\,
. By Theorem
6.19
we can view
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\bullet}=\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}\,
, as
generated by
X_{v}
with
v\leq_{R}w=u\cdot w_{\eta(i)}\,
. The latter generating set splits into the union

\{X_{v}:v\leq_{R}u\}\sqcup\{X_{w}\}
. If
v\leq_{R}u
we have that
w_{i}\cdot v
is reduced since

w_{i}\cdot u
is reduced. Hence
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(X_{v})=X_{w_{i}\cdot v}\in\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\bullet}\subset\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}\,
by
(
5.4
) and (
6.18
).

Now, by definition,
X_{w}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{u}(X_{\eta(i)})
so that
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(X_{w})=\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{u}(X_{\eta(i)})=\mathit{\Gamma}_{z}(X_{\eta(i)})=\mathit{\Gamma}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}(X_{\eta(i)})
since
z=w_{i}\cdot u
is reduced and maximal. The formula (
5.14
)
in the proof of Corollary
5.3
then implies that

\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(X_{w})=\mathit{\Gamma}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}(E_{\eta(i)}^{\ell_{i}})=(-K_{i}^{-1}F_{i})^{\ell_{i}}=-L_{i}^{-1}Y_{i}\in\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}\subset\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}\,
. Thus,
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}

maps all generators of
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
to
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}\,
as desired.
∎

The action of the Artin groups on the maximal skew-commutative algebras is rather non-trivial.
We leave it here as an open question whether
\mathscr{A}
acts effectively or faithfully, as
suggested by the identifications with actions on Lie groups discussed in Sections
7.4
and
8.4
.

For illustration, we gather below explicit formulae for the Lie type
\mathsf{A}_{2}
and odd
\mathscr{k}\,
, with

{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{\;}\mkern-1.0mu=(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{\ell}
. The action of
\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}
on the Cartan algebra, given by

\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}(L_{1})=L_{1}^{-1}
and
\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}(L_{2})=L_{2}L_{1}^{-1}
, factors through
the quotient
\mathscr{A}=B_{3}\rightarrow\mathscr{W}=S_{3}\,
. The remaining expressions are
as follows.

(6.59)

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{13.37277pt}\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}(X_{1})

\displaystyle=-L_{1}^{-1}Y_{1}\ \quad

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}(X_{2})

\displaystyle=X_{(12)}\quad

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}(X_{(12)})

\displaystyle=-X_{2}+{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{\;}\mkern-1.0muL_{1}^{-1}X_{(12)}Y_{1}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{13.37277pt}\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}(Y_{1})

\displaystyle=-L_{1}X_{1}

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}(Y_{2})

\displaystyle=Y_{(12)}

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}(Y_{(12)})

\displaystyle=-Y_{2}-{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{\;}\mkern-1.0muL_{1}Y_{(12)}X_{1}

Those in the first two columns are immediate from (
6.20
) and (
6.18
).
For those in the third column, we invoke the identity
X_{(12)}+X_{(21)}+{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{\;}\mkern-1.0muX_{1}X_{2}=0
with
{\scalebox{.9}{$\nabla$}\mkern-3.0mu}_{\;}\mkern-1.0mu=(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{\ell}
,
which is obtained by specializing Propositions
6.17
. We also use
the identity
\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}(X_{(21)})=X_{2}
, which is implied by Propositions
5.1
.
The action on
Y_{(12)}
follows via application of
\Omega\,
.

It is now not hard to find many infinite families of braids in
B_{3}
for which the action in (
6.59
) on generators produces polynomials whose (naïve) degrees monotonously increase
with the crossing numbers of the braids.

6.5.
\mathcal{Z}
-Induced Ideals,
\mathscr{G}
-Invariance, and
\mathscr{G}
-Grading

In this section, we describe the general process of obtaining ideals for the full quantum groups from ideals of the skew-central subalgebras. To keep the exposition more readable, we will often
suppress the choice of a maximal word
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}

in the notation of the maximal algebra
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}=\mathcal{Z}_{z}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}
.
By Theorem
6.19
this is unambiguous for Lie types other than
\mathsf{G}_{2}
. In the case

\mathsf{G}_{2}
it is tacitly understood that there may be (at most) two or four choices, depending on
\scriptscriptstyle\Box
.

As skew-polynomial algebras, the
\mathcal{Z}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}_{\bullet}
have a rich ideal structure. Ideals in
\mathcal{Z}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}_{\bullet}
extend to ideals in
U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\,
provided they are commensurable with the action of an elementary abelian 2-group stemming from commutation relations as in Proposition
6.7
.

More formally, the latter group is defined as
\mathscr{G}=\mathbb{F}_{2}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\times\mathbb{F}_{2}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
, acting
on the algebra
\mathcal{Z}_{w}
for any
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}\,
.
An element
(\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\mu},\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\nu})\in\mathscr{G}
acts on generators in

\mathcal{Z}_{w}
associated to some
v\leq_{R}w
by multiplication with
\pm 1
via the
formulae

(6.60)

(\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\mu},\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\nu})\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}X_{v}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\gamma(v),\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\mu})$}}X_{v}\;,\quad(\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\mu},\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\nu})\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}Y_{v}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\gamma(v),\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\nu})$}}Y_{v}\;,\quad\mbox{and}\quad(\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\mu},\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\nu})\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}L_{i}=\raise 1.19995pt\hbox{$\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\kappa}$}}}$}\mkern-1.5mu\hbox{\scalebox{0.85}{$(\alpha_{i},\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\mu}+\accentset{\rule{0.0pt}{0.7pt}}{\nu})$}}L_{i}\;.

Since the
\{X_{v},Y_{v},L_{i}:v\leq_{R}w,1\leq i\leq n\}
are independent (sign-commuting) generators of
\mathcal{Z}_{w}
,
the formulae in (
6.60
) uniquely extend to a
\mathscr{G}
-action on
\mathcal{Z}_{w}
as algebra automorphisms.
The action clearly preserves all
\mathcal{Z}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}_{w}
subalgebras and specializes to a

\mathbb{F}_{2}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
-action on either
\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{w}
or
\mathcal{Z}^{-}_{w}\,
as one of the components acts trivially.

The commutation relations from Proposition
6.7
and (
6.25
) can now
be rephrased more compactly using the
\mathscr{G}
-action. Specifically, for a fully homogeneous element
b\in U_{q}
and

W\in\mathcal{Z}_{w}
we find

(6.61)

W\cdot b=b\cdot\mathbb{o}^{*}(b)\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}W\;,\quad\mbox{where}\quad\ \mathbb{o}^{*}(b)=(\mathbb{o}^{+}(b),\mathbb{o}^{-}(b))\in\mathscr{G}\;,

by straightforward verification on the generators. Here we use also
\mathbb{w}=\mathbb{o}^{+}+\mathbb{o}^{-}\mod 2
and the extension to general elements via standard action properties. We say that a subspace
A\subseteq\mathcal{Z}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}_{w}
is

\mathscr{G}
-invariant
if
g\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}x\in A
for all
g\in\mathscr{G}
and
x\in A\,
.

Lemma 6.23
.

The
\mathscr{G}
-action on
\mathcal{Z}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}_{\bullet}
does not depend on a choice of
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}\,
.

If
W\in\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}=\mathcal{Z}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}
and
w,z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
represent

{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}
denote by
(\bar{u},\bar{\nu})\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}\!^{w}
and
(\bar{u},\bar{\nu})\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}\!^{z}
the respective actions defined via (
6.60
).
Equation (
6.61
) then implies

b\cdot\mathbb{o}^{*}(b)\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}\!^{z}W=b\cdot\mathbb{o}^{*}(b)\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}\!^{w}W
for homogeneous elements
b
. Choosing respective PBW basis elements one may then infer
that the actions need to be the same. Another immediate consequence of (
6.61
) is as follows.

Lemma 6.24
.

If
J
is a
\mathscr{G}
-invariant left or right ideal in
\mathcal{Z}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}_{\bullet}
, then
J
is also a two-sided ideal.

For example, suppose
J
is left sided,
W\in J
, and
b\in\mathcal{Z}^{+}_{\bullet}
is homogeneous. Then
W\cdot b=b\cdot W^{\prime}
where

W^{\prime}=\mathbb{o}^{*}(b)\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}W\in J
by
\mathscr{G}
-invariance. Thus
W\cdot b=b\cdot W^{\prime}\in J
since
J
is a left ideal and, hence, also a right ideal.
It is not difficult to find counterexamples to Lemma
6.24
if the
condition of
\mathscr{G}
-invariance is dropped.
In the next proposition, we
consider
algebra
ideals only, disregarding any coalgebra structures.

Proposition 6.25
.

Suppose
J
is a
\mathscr{G}
-invariant
(any-sided) ideal in
\mathcal{Z}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}_{\bullet}
.
Then
{\widehat{J}}=J\cdot U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\,
is a two-sided ideal in
U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}
.
Moreover, the multiplication map from (
6.38
) induces an isomorphism of
\mathcal{Z}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}_{\bullet}
-modules,

(6.62)

\left(\mathcal{Z}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}_{\bullet}/J\right)\otimes_{\Lambda}{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-12.82538pt}{\hskip-9.77255pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle z\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.82289pt}{\hskip-24.82289pt}{\hskip-14.99458pt}{\hskip-10.71045pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.82289pt}\!\longrightarrow\,U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}/{\widehat{J}}\,:\;([z],b)\,\mapsto\,[z\cdot b]\,,

where
[.]
denotes the class of an element in the respective quotient algebra and
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
is a reduced word of maximal length.

Proof.

{\widehat{J}}
is a right ideal by definition. To see it is also a left ideal, write general elements

B\in U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}
and
C\in J
as

B=\sum_{s}b_{s}
and
C=\sum_{t}W_{t}c_{t}
where
b_{s},c_{t}\in U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}
are fully homogeneous and
W_{t}\in J\,
.
(
6.61
) then implies
B\cdot C=\sum_{s,t}\mathbb{o}^{*}(b_{s})\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}(W_{t})b_{s}c_{t}\,
. By

\mathscr{G}
-invariance of
J
we have
\mathbb{o}^{*}(b_{s})\raise-2.0pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$\smalltriangleright$}}(W_{t})\in J
so that

B\cdot C\in{\widehat{J}}
. Thus
U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\cdot J\subseteq{\widehat{J}}
,
which implies

U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\cdot{\widehat{J}}=U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\cdot J\cdot U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\subseteq{\widehat{J}}\cdot U_{\zeta}^{{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}}\subseteq{\widehat{J}}
as desired.

For the second assertion, it suffices to show that
\,\mathscr{m}^{+}_{z}\left(J\otimes_{\Lambda}{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-12.82538pt}{\hskip-9.77255pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle z\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-14.74419pt}{\hskip-10.53159pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.03674pt}\!\right)={\widehat{J}}\,
. The inclusion of the image in
{\widehat{J}}
is clear from
the ideal property.
Surjectivity of the restriction of
\mathscr{m}^{+}_{z}
from
J\otimes_{\Lambda}{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-12.82538pt}{\hskip-9.77255pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle z\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-14.74419pt}{\hskip-10.53159pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.03674pt}\!
to
{\widehat{J}}
is immediate from the commutative diagram below, where the top horizontal arrow is an isomorphism and the two vertical arrows are surjections.

\textstyle{\quad J\otimes_{\Lambda}{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-12.82538pt}{\hskip-9.77255pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle z\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-14.74419pt}{\hskip-10.53159pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.03674pt}}

\textstyle{\quad J\otimes_{\Lambda}{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-20.92198pt}{\hskip-12.82538pt}{\hskip-9.77255pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle z\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-14.74419pt}{\hskip-10.53159pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.03674pt}}
