r_{i}+\ldots+r_{j}=N\end{subarray}}q^{\sum_{i\leq s<t\leq j}r_{s}r_{t}}(q^{-1}-q)^{\sum_{i<s<j}r_{s}}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$N$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
r_{i},\ldots,r_{j}\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}\left(T^{i,j}_{i}\right)^{r_{i}}\ldots\left(T^{i,j}_{j}\right)^{r_{j}}\,.

7.3.
Identification of
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}
as a (Semi) Classical Matrix Algebra

We consider next the specialization to a primitive
\mathscr{k}
-th root of unity
\zeta
, with
\ell
the order of
\zeta^{2}\,
. In the simply laced setting all
\ell_{\alpha}=\ell\,
. Thus,
for the root
\alpha=\alpha_{i}+\ldots+\alpha_{j-1}=\epsilon_{i}-\epsilon_{j}\,
, we have

X_{\alpha}=X_{i,j}=E_{i,j}^{\ell}

with respect to the ordering given by (
7.9
). We extend this notation to
X_{i,i}=1
. Write also
L_{i,j}=L^{\alpha}=K_{i,j}^{\ell}\,
as in (
6.16
) and
define
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}=\mathcal{Z}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
as in (
6.39
)
and (
6.56
).

The coproducts of the
X_{\alpha}
have been computed
in
[
9
, (2.24)]
for a 2-parameter version
U_{r,s}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n})\,
, which coincides with
U_{\zeta}
if
r=s^{-1}
is a respective root of unity.
The results there imply that the collection of all
X_{\alpha}
generate a
Hopf ideals, leading to a well-defined (2-parameter) restricted quantum group.
A general form for the coproduct for other cases can also be found in
[
20
, Sect. 5.5]
, though the stated formulae are modulo higher ideal terms and no explicit coefficients are offered. A similar version of the next lemma can be found in
[
9
]
.

Lemma 7.9
.

For
1\leq i<j\leq n+1
and with notation as above, we have

(7.25)

\Delta(X_{i,j})=\sum_{k=i}^{j}b_{k}X_{i,k}\otimes L_{i,k}X_{k,j}\;,

where
\;b_{k}=(\zeta^{-1}-\zeta)^{\ell}\zeta^{\binom{\ell}{2}}\;
for
i<k<j
and
b_{i}=b_{j}=1\,
.

In particular,
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is a Hopf subalgebra of
U_{\zeta}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\,
.

Proof.

Setting
N=\ell
in (
7.24
) and with Corollary
6.2
we are left with a summation over terms in which one index
r_{k}=\ell
and all other indices are zero. For
i<k<j
we, further, note that

(T^{i,j}_{k})^{\ell}=(E_{i,k})^{\ell}\otimes(K_{i,k}E_{k,j})^{\ell}=\zeta^{\binom{\ell}{2}}E_{i,k}^{\ell}\otimes K_{i,k}^{\ell}E_{k,j}^{\ell}
since
K_{i,k}E_{k,j}=\zeta^{-1}E_{k,j}K_{i,k}\,
. The resulting formula
for the coproduct in
(
7.25
) as well as
\Delta(L_{i,j})=L_{i,j}\otimes L_{i,j}
contain only generators of
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
, so that
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is a sub-bialgebra.

As noted in the proof of Theorem
6.19
in Section
6.4
,

\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is also invariant under
\mho
. From Item
iv)

in Proposition
4.1
we also know that

\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit i\!d}_{u}(X_{i,j})=\lambda K^{\ell(\epsilon_{i}-\epsilon_{j})}X_{i,j}=\lambda L_{i,j}X_{i,j}\,
,
where

\lambda=\pm\zeta^{a}
for some
a\in\mathbb{Z}
. Relation (
4.16
) now implies that
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is also invariant under the antipode
S\,
.
∎

A normalization of generators for which the coproduct structure is defined over
\mathbb{Z}
is discussed in Appendix
D
.
The fact that the full skew-central subalgebra forms a Hopf subalgebra allows us now to prove that the ideals defined in Section
6.5
are indeed Hopf ideals.

Theorem 7.10
.

For any
s\in\mathscr{W}
the augmentation ideal
\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
as in (
6.63
)
is a Hopf algebra ideal in
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
.

Proof.

Since
s\leq_{R}{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}
there are reduced words
w,b\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
with
z=w\cdot b\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
,
{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}=\mathscr{r}(z)
, and
s=\mathscr{r}(w)
. As in Section
2.3
, this imposes a total convex
ordering
\prec_{z}
on
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
. As in the remarks following (
6.63
), word independence of Theorem
6.19

implies that
\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is the ideal generated by all
X_{v}
with
\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$}\neq v\leq_{R}w
. Given the fixed
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}\,
,
we may relabel generators
X_{\alpha}=X_{z[\alpha]}
analogous to (
5.3
). Thus, with
\gamma=\gamma(w)
and this notation,
\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is the ideal generated by
X_{\beta}
with
\beta\preceq_{z}\gamma\,
.

Next, note that, by Proposition
6.10
, the monomials

L^{\mu}{X}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle z\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-14.74419pt}{\hskip-10.53159pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.03674pt}=\pm L^{\mu}\prod_{\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}}X_{\alpha}^{\psi(\alpha)}
are a basis for

\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
. Since, by Lemma
7.9
,
\mathcal{K}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is a Hopf algebra
over
\Lambda
, we can write
\Delta(X_{\beta})
with
\beta\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
as a
\Lambda
-linear combination of terms of the form

L^{\nu}X_{\beta_{1}}\ldots X_{\beta_{s}}\otimes L^{\mu}X_{\beta_{s+1}}\ldots X_{\beta_{k}}
, where the sequence of roots
\beta_{i}\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
may have repetitions.

By
\mathbb{w}
-grading, we must have
\beta=\sum_{i}\beta_{i}
. Lemma
2.6
now implies that for at least
one
j
we have
\beta_{j}\preceq_{z}\beta
. Thus, if
\beta\preceq_{z}\gamma
also
\beta_{j}\preceq_{z}\gamma
and, hence,
that
X_{\beta_{j}}\in\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\,
. Therefore, any of these terms is in

\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\otimes\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\,+\,\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\otimes\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
,
which, thus, contains
\Delta(X_{\beta})
for every generator
X_{\beta}
of
\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
(with

\beta\preceq_{z}\gamma\,
) and, consequently, also
\Delta(\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}})\,
.
∎

The proof of Theorem
7.10
extends to other classical Lie types for which
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
can be shown to be a Hopf subalgebra, as well as other Lie types to which Lemma
2.6
can be generalized.

The
\mathcal{Z}_{w}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
subalgebras, however, will generally
not
form sub-bialgebras. For example, for type
\mathsf{A}_{2}
and
w=w_{1}w_{2}=z_{2}[1,2]
we have that
\mathcal{Z}_{w}^{+}
is the subalgebra generated by
X_{1,3}
and
X_{2,3}
. Yet,

\Delta(X_{1,3})
will also contain a
X_{1,2}
factor.

Conversely, call a subset
C\subseteq{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
a
lower set
if
\mu+\nu\in C
for
\mu,\nu\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
implies
\mu,\nu\in C
. The coproduct in (
7.25
) implies that

\langle X_{\alpha},L_{\alpha}:\,\alpha\in C\rangle

is a Hopf subalgebra for any lower set
C
, where the generators are defined with respect to the maximal word from (
7.9
). For a given root
\beta=\epsilon_{i}-\epsilon_{j}=\alpha_{i}+\ldots+\alpha_{j-1}\,
, let
C_{\beta}
be the set of all positive roots
\leq\beta
in the usual partial order, which is just the root subsystem
\{\epsilon_{s}-\epsilon_{r}:i\leq s<r\leq j\}\,
. It is clear that a subset
C
has the above property if and only if it is a union of (possibly intersecting) sets
C_{\beta}\,
.

One may, further, ask for which
s\in\mathscr{W}
, both, the algebra
\mathcal{Z}_{s}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is a Hopf subalgebra so that
\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is a Hopf ideal. In the
\mathsf{A}_{n}
case with
\mathscr{W}=S_{n+1}\,
it is not difficult to see that the root set
\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)
for
\mathcal{Z}_{s}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is a lower set if it is the
disjoint
union of sets
C_{\beta}\,
. Particularly, the lower set property for

\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)
implies that if
(i,j)
with
i<j
is an inversion pair for
s\in S_{n+1}
then any
(a,b)
with
i\leq a<b\leq j
also needs to be an inversion pair. Suppose that
[i,j]
is a maximal interval with
\epsilon_{i}-\epsilon_{j}\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)
. It is then not hard to see that
s
then maps the intervals
[1,i-1]
,
[i,j]
, and
[j+1,n]
respectively to themselves and that it acts on
[i,j]

via the longest (full inversion) element
of
S_{j-1+1}\,
.

Thus, by induction,
s
must be the product of longest elements on disjoint intervals
a_{s}=[i_{s},j_{s}]
, with
j_{s}<i_{s+1}\,
.
The associated subalgebra
\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{s}

is then identified with
\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}(a_{1})\otimes\ldots\otimes\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}(a_{m})
, where
each
\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}(a_{s})
is the subalgebra generated
X_{\alpha}
and
L_{\alpha}
with
\alpha
in the respective
\mathsf{A}_{j_{s}-i_{s}+1}
subsystem. Requiring the augmentation ideals
\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
to derive from Hopf algebras, thus, leaves us with only these obvious examples.

In the remainder of this section, we discuss identifications of the Hopf algebra
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
as in
Lemma
7.9
with (semi) classical Hopf algebra constructions
that are (mostly) independent of a choice of roots of unity
\zeta
.
These are more conveniently worked out for the quantum group associated to
\mathfrak{gl}_{n+1}\,
,
which contains the standard one for
\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}\,
.

The generators of
U_{q}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n+1})
are given by the usual
E_{i}
and
F_{i}
for
1\leq i\leq n
as well as

P_{i}^{\pm 1}
for
1\leq i\leq n+1\,
. The elements
P_{i}^{\pm 1}
are required to be group like and to commute with each other. Relations (
3.13
) and (
3.16
) are replaced by ones in which we substitute
K_{i}
by
P_{i}P_{i+1}^{-1}
. The conjugation relations in (
3.14
) are replaced by

(7.26)

P_{i}E_{j}P_{i}^{-1}=q^{\mathchoice{\left(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha_{j}\right)}{(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha_{j})}{(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha_{j})}{(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha_{j})}}E_{j}=q^{\delta_{i,j}-\delta_{i,j+1}}E_{j}\qquad\mbox{ and }\qquad P_{i}F_{j}P_{i}^{-1}=q^{-\mathchoice{\left(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha_{j}\right)}{(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha_{j})}{(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha_{j})}{(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha_{j})}}F_{j}=q^{-\delta_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j+1}}F_{j}\,,

and the Serre relations (
3.11
) and (
3.12
) remain unchanged.

A
\mathbb{Z}
-grading
\mathbb{p}
on
U_{q}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n+1})
is provided by setting
\mathbb{p}(P_{i})=1
and
\mathbb{p}(E_{i})=\mathbb{p}(F_{i})=0\,
for all
i=1,\ldots,n\,
.
The original algebra
U_{q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})
is then recovered as the 0-graded subalgebra of
U_{q}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n+1})
with respect to
\mathbb{p}\,
. The inclusion map of
U_{q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})
into
U_{q}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n+1})
is now given by

K_{i}\mapsto P_{i}P_{i+1}^{-1}
on the Cartan subalgebra and identity on all other generators.

The specialization of
U_{q}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n+1})
to a root of unity
\zeta
is commensurable with this inclusion. The analogous
skew-central subalgebra
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}
is generated by
Q_{i}=P_{i}^{\ell}
as well as the
X_{i,j}\,
as before. The
\mathbb{p}
-grading extends to
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}
with
\mathbb{p}(Q_{i})=\ell\,
.

The ground ring
\Lambda
may be any extension of
\Lambda_{\zeta}=\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]
, such as the ones from (
6.5
).
If
(\zeta-\zeta)^{-1}
is not in
\Lambda
, we denote by
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
the subalgebra generated
by
Q_{i}=P_{i}^{\ell}
and
(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{\ell}X_{i,j}\,
. Thus, for example for
\Lambda=\Lambda_{\zeta}
, the quotient

\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}/\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
is a torsion module for
\Lambda\,
.
Conversely, if the ground ring extends
\Lambda_{\zeta}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
we have
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}=\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}\,
.

As for the generic case, the original subalgebra
\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}
is identified with the zero-graded component of

\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet}
with respect to
\mathbb{p}\,
. Analogously, we write
\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}

for the subalgebra generated by the
L_{j}
and
(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{\ell}X_{i,j}\,
, or, equivalently, the zero-graded
part of
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}\,
.

We next consider a smaller variant of the extended quantum matrix algebra introduced by Artin, Schelter, and Tate in
[
7
]
.
Suppose
\,\mathsf{c}:\{1,\ldots,n\}^{2}\rightarrow\Lambda^{\times}\,
are coefficients for which
\mathsf{c}\scalebox{0.75}{$(i,j)$}=\mathsf{c}\scalebox{0.75}{$(j,i)$}^{-1}
and
\mathsf{c}\scalebox{0.75}{$(i,i)$}=1\,
. Define
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\Lambda,\mathsf{c})
to be
the unital algebra over
\Lambda
with generaPlease provide the text you want me to spell check.tor set
\{R_{i,j}:1\leq i\leq j\leq n\}\sqcup\{R_{i,i}^{-1}:i=1,\ldots,n\}\,
and relations

(7.27)

R_{i,j}R_{s,t}\,=\,\frac{\mathsf{c}\scalebox{0.75}{$(i,s)$}}{\mathsf{c}\scalebox{0.75}{$(j,t)$}}\,R_{s,t}R_{i,j}\qquad\mbox{and }\qquad R_{i,i}^{-1}R_{i,i}=1=R_{i,i}R_{i,i}^{-1}

for all valid indices. This algebra differs from the one in
[
7
]
in that we only use the coefficients on the subgroup

\mathrm{T}_{n}
of upper triangular matrices in
\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{C})\,
, and that an extra parameter there is
\lambda=1\,
.
The algebra
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\Lambda,\mathsf{c})
may also be viewed as a central extension of the polynomial
algebra
\Lambda[\{x_{i,j},x_{i,i}^{-1}\}_{i\leq j}]
, in which the
\mathsf{c}
expression features as the respective 2-cocyle.

The bialgebra portion of the following result is a straightforward adaption of Theorems 1 and 2 in
[
7
]
. As opposed
to the situation in
[
7
]
, an antipode is assured by the invertibility of the diagonal elements and does not require a
determinant relation. Its explicit form below is readily verified by direct computation.

Proposition 7.11
.

The algebra
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\Lambda,\mathsf{c})
is a free
\Lambda
module with basis given by monomials
\prod_{i\leq j}R_{i,j}^{n_{i,j}}
, where
n_{i,i}\in\mathbb{Z}
and
n_{i,j}\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
for
1\leq i<j\leq n\,
(for some fixed ordering).

Further,
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{c},\Lambda)
admits the structure of a Hopf algebra over
\Lambda
with coproduct defined by

(7.28)

\Delta(R_{i,j})=\sum_{k=i}^{j}R_{i,k}\otimes R_{k,j}\;.

The counit is
\varepsilon(R_{i,j})=\delta_{i,j}\,
.
The unique antipode is given by
S(R_{i,i})=R_{i,i}^{-1}
and, for
j>i

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}}}}_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq m\leq j-i\\
i=s_{0}<s_{1}<\ldots<s_{m}=j\end{subarray}}(-1)^{m}\,R_{s_{0},s_{0}}^{-1}R_{s_{0},s_{1}}R_{s_{1},s_{1}}^{-1}R_{s_{1},s_{2}}\ldots R_{s_{m-1},s_{m-1}}^{-1}R_{s_{m-1},s_{m}}R^{-1}_{s_{m},s_{m}}\,.

Two special cases of fully symmetric and anti symmetric coefficient sets are given by

(7.29)

\mathsf{s}\scalebox{0.75}{$(i,j)$}=1\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\mathsf{a}\scalebox{0.75}{$(i,j)$}=-(-1)^{\delta_{ij}}\,.

We will also abbreviate
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\Lambda)=\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{s},\Lambda)
for the classical matrix algebra. Note also,
that the coefficients in (
7.29
) are units in
\mathbb{Z}
and the structure coefficients in Proposition
7.11
are integers as well. Thus, the matrix algebras can be defined over
\mathbb{Z}
so that

(7.30)

\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\Lambda)=\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathbb{Z})\otimes\Lambda\qquad\mbox{ and }\qquad\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\Lambda)=\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\mathbb{Z})\otimes\Lambda\,.

The algebra
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{c},\Lambda)
admits many integer gradings. One of them, given on generators as
\mathbb{n}(R_{i,j})=\epsilon_{j}-\epsilon_{i}
, extends to a Hopf algebra grading. Another is the total polynomial degree, given by
\mathbb{q}(R_{i,j})=1
and
\mathbb{q}(R_{i,i}^{-1})=-1
, which does not extend to a Hopf algebra grading. Nevertheless, it is not hard to see that the zero
graded subalgebra, spanned by monomials
M
with
\mathbb{q}(M)=0
, forms indeed a Hopf subalgebra, which we denote as

\mathcal{O}\!_{\circ}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{c},\Lambda)\,
. Similarly, we abbreviate
\mathcal{O}\!_{\circ}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\Lambda)=\mathcal{O}\!_{\circ}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{s},\Lambda)\,
.

The following identifications of the skew-central subalgebras assume that
\Lambda
contains
\Lambda_{\zeta}
, where
\zeta
is a primitive
\mathscr{k}
-th root of unity.

Theorem 7.12
.

Let
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
and
\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
be the subalgebra of
U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n})
and
U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n})
as defined above.
There exist isomorphisms of Hopf algebras over
\Lambda
as follows.

(7.31)

\displaystyle\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}

\displaystyle\cong\,\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\Lambda)

\displaystyle\mbox{ and }

\displaystyle\quad\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}

\displaystyle\cong\,\mathcal{O}\!_{\circ}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\Lambda)

\displaystyle\mbox{ if }\;\mathscr{k}\not\equiv 2\mod 4

\displaystyle\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}

\displaystyle\cong\,\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\Lambda)

\displaystyle\mbox{ and }

\displaystyle\quad\mathcal{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}

\displaystyle\cong\,\mathcal{O}\!_{\circ}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\Lambda)

\displaystyle\mbox{ if }\;\mathscr{k}\equiv 2\mod 4

Proof.

Set
b=(\zeta^{-1}-\zeta)^{\ell}\zeta^{\binom{\ell}{2}}
and consider the assignments of generators of
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{c},\Lambda)
to generators of

\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
given by

(7.32)

R_{i,j}\mapsto bQ_{i}^{-1}X_{i,j}\quad\mbox{for}\;i<j\qquad\mbox{ and }\qquad R_{i,i}\mapsto Q_{i}^{-1}\,.

Using
Q_{i}Q_{j}^{-1}=P_{i}^{\ell}P_{j}^{-\ell}=K_{i,j}^{\ell}=L_{i,j}
and the coproduct
formula in (
7.25
) we find

\displaystyle\Delta(bQ_{i}^{-1}X_{i,j})

\displaystyle=b(Q_{i}^{-1}\otimes Q_{i}^{-1})\Big(1\otimes Q_{i}Q_{i}^{-1}X_{i,j}+\sum_{i<k<j}bX_{i,k}\otimes Q_{i}Q_{k}^{-1}X_{k,j}\,+\,X_{i,j}\otimes Q_{i}Q_{j}^{-1}\Big)

\displaystyle=Q_{i}^{-1}\otimes bQ_{i}^{-1}X_{i,j}+\sum_{i<k<j}bQ_{i}^{-1}X_{i,k}\otimes bQ_{k}^{-1}X_{k,j}\,+\,bQ_{i}^{-1}X_{i,j}\otimes Q_{j}^{-1}\,.

That is, the assignment preserves the corelation of generators from (
7.28
).

The commutation relations
6.26
specialize to
X_{\alpha}X_{\beta}=\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta^{\mathchoice{\left(\alpha|\beta\right)}{(\alpha|\beta)}{(\alpha|\beta)}{(\alpha|\beta)}}X_{\beta}X_{\alpha}\,
in the simply laced case. Here

\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta=\zeta^{\ell^{2}}
, as in (
6.2
), is
\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta=-1
if
\,\mathscr{k}\equiv 2\mod 4
and
\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta=+1
otherwise. From (
7.26
)
we also have
Q_{i}X_{\alpha}=\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta^{\mathchoice{\left(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha\right)}{(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha)}{(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha)}{(\epsilon_{i}|\alpha)}}X_{\alpha}Q_{i}\,
. Thus,
Q_{i}^{-1}X_{\alpha}Q_{s}^{-1}X_{\beta}=\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta^{\mathchoice{\left(\alpha|\epsilon_{s}\right)}{(\alpha|\epsilon_{s})}{(\alpha|\epsilon_{s})}{(\alpha|\epsilon_{s})}+\mathchoice{\left(\epsilon_{i}|\beta\right)}{(\epsilon_{i}|\beta)}{(\epsilon_{i}|\beta)}{(\epsilon_{i}|\beta)}+\mathchoice{\left(\alpha|\beta\right)}{(\alpha|\beta)}{(\alpha|\beta)}{(\alpha|\beta)}}Q_{s}^{-1}X_{\beta}Q_{i}^{-1}X_{\alpha}\,
.
Setting
\alpha=\epsilon_{i}-\epsilon_{j}
and
\beta=\epsilon_{s}-\epsilon_{t}

with
i\leq j
and
s\leq t
we find the exponent is

\delta_{i,s}+\delta_{j,t}=(1+\delta_{i,s})+(1+\delta_{j,t})\mod 2\,
.

Thus

(Q_{i}^{-1}X_{i,j})(Q_{s}^{-1}X_{s,t})=\frac{\mathsf{c}\scalebox{0.75}{$(i,s)$}}{\mathsf{c}\scalebox{0.75}{$(j,t)$}}(Q_{s}^{-1}X_{s,t})(Q_{i}^{-1}X_{i,j})
,
where
\mathsf{c}\scalebox{0.75}{$(i,j)$}=\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta^{1+\delta_{i,j}}
.
Clearly, for
\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta=1
this matches the commutation relations in
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{s},\Lambda)
and for
\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta=-1
the ones for
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\Lambda)\,
. Consequently, the assignment
in (
7.32
) extends to an algebra homomorphism, with the previous observation, also to a bialgebra homomorphism, and, using uniqueness of antipodes, to a Hopf algebra homomorphism.

It is clear that this homomorphism maps PBW bases to each other, yielding an isomorphism of Hopf algebras and, thus, proving the statements for
the
U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n})
subalgebras. The respective statements for the
U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n})
are inferred from the fact
that the assignment in (
7.32
) maps a generator with
\mathbb{q}
-grading of 1 to an element with
\mathbb{p}
-grading
-\ell
. Therefore, the isomorphism restricts to an isomorphism of the respective zero-graded Hopf subalgebras.
∎

Theorem
7.12
together with (
7.30
) implies that in the skew-central subalgebras are determined by Hopf algebras that are
independent
of the choice of a root of unity, except for the
\!\mod 4
-parity of its order.

Conjecture 7.13
.

For given root system

\mathsf{\Phi}

, denote by
B
be the Borel subgroup of the respective complex, simply connected simple algebraic group and by
\breve{B}
the Borel subgroup so associated to the coroot system
\breve{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}}
. Let further

\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
be the analogous skew-central subalgebra in an extension of
U_{\zeta}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
for a primitive
\mathscr{k}
-th root of unity
\zeta\,
.

i)

\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}
is also a Hopf subalgebra for any
\mathscr{k}
, isomorphic to a centrally extended matrix algebra, generalizing the definition of
[
7
]
and associated to either
B
or
\breve{B}
or a finite quotient of these.

ii)

This extended matrix algebra depends up to isomorphism only on parity of
\mathscr{k}
modulo
4\mathsf{e}
.

7.4.
Ideals from Algebraic Subgroups of
\mathrm{T}_{n}
and Bruhat Subgroups

In this section we focus entirely on type
\mathsf{A}_{n-1}
algebras and the case

\mathscr{k}\not\equiv 2\mod 4
, for which
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}

is commutative. In this setting,
Theorem
7.12
yields an isomorphism between commutative rings, whose scalars we can be further extended to a field
\mathbb{k}=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)
or
\mathbb{k}=\mathbb{C}\,
, assuming an embedded ground ring
\Lambda\hookrightarrow\mathbb{k}\,
.

As before, let
\mathrm{T}_{n}<\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{k})
be the algebraic group of upper triangular matrices over
\mathbb{k}
. Denote also
\mathrm{P}\mathrm{T}_{n}<\mathrm{PGL}(n,\mathbb{k})
the respective subgroup of the projective linear group. We will use the following identifications with coordinate rings.

Corollary 7.14
.

Assume
\mathscr{k}\not\equiv 2\mod 4
and Lie types
\mathfrak{gl}_{n}
or
\mathfrak{sl}_{n}
as above. Then the isomorphisms from Theorem
7.12
composed with the assignment
R_{i,j}\mapsto\hat{x}_{i,j}\,
yield isomorphisms of Hopf algebras

\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\otimes\mathbb{k}\,\cong\,\mathbb{k}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\otimes\mathbb{k}\,\cong\,\mathbb{k}[\mathrm{P}\mathrm{T}_{n}]\,.

Proof.

Clearly,
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\otimes\mathbb{k}=\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}\otimes\mathbb{k}
and
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\otimes\mathbb{k}=\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet\;{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}}\otimes\mathbb{k}
.
It is also easy to see that
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathbb{k})\cong\mathbb{k}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]
as commutative Hopf algebras by comparing coproducts in (
7.8
) and (
7.28
). On the diagonal the assignment extends uniquely to
R_{i,i}^{-1}\mapsto\hat{x}_{i,i}^{-1}
. Recall that
{\mathrm{P}}\mathrm{T}_{n}
is defined as the quotient
\mathrm{T}_{n}/\mathrm{C}
by the center
\mathrm{C}=\mathbb{k}^{\times}\cdot 1
so that

\mathbb{k}[{\mathrm{P}}\mathrm{T}_{n}]
embeds in
\mathbb{k}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]
. Functions in
\mathbb{k}[{\mathrm{P}}\mathrm{T}_{n}]
are those constant on each
\mathrm{C}
-coset. For given
\lambda\in\mathbb{k}^{\times}
,
g\in\mathrm{T}_{n}
, and
\hat{x}^{f}=\prod_{i\leq j}\hat{x}_{i,j}^{f_{ij}}
a general monomial, one readily verifies that

\hat{x}^{f}(\lambda g)=\lambda^{\sum_{i\leq j}f_{ij}}\cdot\hat{x}^{f}(g)
. Thus

\hat{x}^{f}\in\mathbb{k}[\mathrm{P}\mathrm{T}_{n}]
iff
\sum_{i\leq j}f_{ij}=0
.
Since
\mathbb{q}(\prod_{i\leq j}R_{i,j}^{f_{ij}})=\sum_{i\leq j}f_{ij}
,
the isomorphism
\mathbb{k}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]\rightarrow\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathbb{k})
maps

\mathbb{k}[\mathrm{P}\mathrm{T}_{n}]
precisely to
\mathcal{O}\!_{\circ}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathbb{k})
, which is thus
identified with
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\otimes\mathbb{k}
.
∎

Note that the coalgebra structure for
\mathbb{k}[\mathrm{P}\mathrm{T}_{2}]\cong\mathbb{k}[\hat{\lambda},\hat{\lambda}^{-1},\hat{x}]
is given by
(
7.5
), whereas the coordinate ring of the Borel part in the 2-fold cover
\widetilde{\mathrm{P}\mathrm{T}_{2}}<\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C})
is of the form

\mathbb{k}[\hat{\chi},\hat{\chi}^{-1},\hat{x}]

with coproduct
\Delta(\hat{x})=\hat{x}\otimes\hat{\chi}+\chi^{-1}\otimes\hat{x}
.
Clearly, the two groups and their respective coordinate rings are
not
isomorphic.
To avoid these types of subtleties, we will confine our discussion below mostly to the case

\mathrm{T}_{n}<\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{C})
. Corollary
7.14
permits us now to
defined large families of Hopf ideals via the composition of maps

(7.33)

\mathscr{h}:\;\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\,\hookrightarrow\,\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\,\rightarrow\,\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\otimes\mathbb{C}\,\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\cong}}{{\longrightarrow}}\,\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]\,.

Lemma 7.15
.

Assume Lie type
\mathsf{A}_{n-1}
,
\Lambda\hookrightarrow\mathbb{C}
and
\mathscr{k}\not\equiv 2\mod 4
as above. Let
H\leq\mathrm{T}_{n}
be any subgroup of the complex subgroup of upper triangular matrices. Then

(7.34)

\mathcal{A}(H)\,=\,\left\{z\in\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\,:\;\mathscr{h}(z)(g)=0\;\forall\,g\in H\right\}

is a Hopf ideal in
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\,
.
Moreover,

\mathcal{A}(H)
depends only on the (Zariski) closure of
H\,
and for two closed algebraic subgroups
H,K\leq\mathrm{T}_{n}
we have
\mathcal{A}(H\cap K)=\mathcal{A}(H)+\mathcal{A}(K)\,
.

Proof.

The definition in (
7.34
) can be rephrased as

\mathcal{A}(H)=\mathscr{h}^{-1}(\mathcal{I}(H))
, with notation for the vanishing ideal of
H
in
\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]
as in Section
7.1
. Since
\mathscr{h}
is a Hopf algebra homomorphism as a composite of such, the preimage of a Hopf ideal is again a Hopf ideal. The other properties follow directly from
Lemma
7.1
.
∎

Subgroups of
P\leq\mathrm{T}_{2}
were discussed and classified already in Corollary
7.3
.
More general examples of algebraic subgroups may be structured using
\mathrm{T}_{n}=\mathrm{D}_{m}\ltimes\mathrm{U}_{n}
,
where
\mathrm{D}_{m}
and
\mathrm{U}_{n}
are as in Section
7.1
. Algebraic subgroups
A\leq\mathrm{D}_{m}

are given as products of finite groups and copies of
\mathbb{C}^{\times}\,
, yielding further
abelian subgroups
A^{\prime}=gAg^{-1}
for any
g\in\mathrm{U}_{n}\,
. Any such
A^{\prime}
acts on
\mathrm{U}_{n}
by conjugation,
and any algebraic subgroup
V\leq\mathrm{U}_{n}
that is
A^{\prime}
-stable yields an algebraic subgroup
A^{\prime}V\leq\mathrm{T}_{n}
.
Respective Hopf ideals in
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\,
for
A\mathrm{U}_{n}=A^{\prime}\mathrm{U}_{n}
are generated by
expressions of the form
\prod_{i}L_{i}^{k_{i}}-1
, while the ideals for general
A^{\prime}V
are typically
generated also by linear expressions in the coordinate functions.

More relevant for our purposes are algebraic subgroups closely related to the Bruhat decomposition
G=\bigsqcup_{s\in\mathscr{W}}C(s)
with Bruhat cells
C(s)=B\dot{s}B\,
defined as double cosets. Here
G
is a connected complex reductive algebraic group,

B\leq G
a Borel subgroup, and
\dot{s}\in N(T)
a representative of

s\in\mathscr{W}\cong N(T)/T
, where
T\leq B
is a maximal torus of
G\,
and
N(T)
its normalizer. We will call the following the
Bruhat subgroup
associated to an element
s\in\mathscr{W}
.

(7.35)

B(s)\,=\,B\,\cap\,\dot{s}B\dot{s}^{-1}\,.

To explain the relation to the Bruhat decomposition, let
U\leq B
be the usual unipotent group such that
B
is a semidirect product of
B=D\ltimes U
with the Cartan subgroup
D\geq T

(in the sense of
(\mathbb{C}^{\times})^{n}\geq(S^{1})^{n}
).
Analogous to (
7.35
), set
U(s)=U\cap\,\dot{s}U\dot{s}^{-1}=B(s)\cap U\,
, which is generated by subgroups
\{U_{\alpha}:\,\alpha\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s^{\llcorner})\}
, where
s^{\llcorner}
is as in (
2.20
). For each
s\in\mathscr{W}
, the map
U(s^{\llcorner})\rightarrow C(s)/B:\,u\mapsto[u\dot{s}]
is a bijection, thus relating the collection
\{U(s)\}
of subgroups to the Bruhat partition of the coset space
G/B\,
.
Note that,

U(s^{\llcorner})=U\cap\,\dot{s}U^{-}\dot{s}^{-1}
, where
U^{-}=\dot{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}U\dot{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}^{-1}
is the respective group associated to negative roots.
For details see, for example,
[
15
, Ch30]
,
[
67
, §8.3]
, or
[
18
, §10.3,N]
.

The augmentation ideals
\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}
, defined in (
6.63
), are next identified with the vanishing ideals on the Bruhat subgroups. Here, the latter are defined with respect to
G=\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{C})
,
B=\mathrm{T}_{n}
, and
U=\mathrm{U}_{n}
as above.

Theorem 7.16
.

For Lie type
\mathsf{A}
,
\mathscr{k}\neq 2\mod 4
, and any
s\in\mathscr{W}
we have

\mathcal{A}(B(s))=\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\;.

Proof.

Note first that for
s\in\mathscr{W}=S_{n}
the representative
\dot{s}
is given by the usual permutation matrix,
acting on the canonical basis by
\dot{s}e_{i}=e_{s(i)}\,
. Suppose
L\in\mathrm{T}_{n}
, meaning that
L_{i,i}\neq 0
and
L_{i,j}=0
for
i>j\,
. The additional condition
L\in\dot{s}B\dot{s}^{-1}
is then equivalent
to
L_{i,j}=0
if
i<j
but
s^{-1}(i)>s^{-1}(j)\,
. Thus, with
\alpha=\epsilon_{i}-\epsilon_{j}\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
, the latter is equivalent to
s^{-1}(\alpha)=\epsilon_{s^{-1}(i)}-\epsilon_{s^{-1}(j)}\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{-}}
and, hence,
\alpha\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\,
. It is thus clear that
a polynomial in
\hat{x}_{i,j}
and
\hat{x}_{i,i}^{-1}
is zero on
B(s)
if and only if it is
in the ideal generated by
\{\hat{x}_{i,j}:\,\epsilon_{i}-\epsilon_{j}\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\}\,
.
The
\mathscr{h}
-preimage of this set is then the ideal generated by

\{X_{\alpha}:\,\alpha\in\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\}\,
, which is precisely
\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\,
.
∎

It is important to keep in mind that the definition of
\mathcal{A}(H)

in Lemma
7.33

depends on the isomorphisms in Theorem
7.12
. These, in turn, depend on the choice of the ordering
in (
7.11
) which determine the
E_{i,j}
and thus
X_{i,j}
generators. The equality
in Theorem
7.16
implies now shared properties of the identified ideals.

Corollary 7.17
.

The following statements hold.

i)

\mathcal{A}(H)
does not depend on a choice of ordering or isomorphism if
H
is a Bruhat subgroup.

ii)

If
\mathscr{k}\not\equiv 2\mod 4\,
,
then
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
is a Hopf ideal in
U_{\zeta}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n})

and
U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n})
for any
s\in\mathscr{W}\,
.

The first statement is immediate from word-independence of
\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}
, which itself a consequence of Theorem
6.19
and the definition in (
6.63
).

For the second assertion recall the notation
\widehat{J}=J\cdot U_{\zeta}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\,
from Proposition
6.25
, extending ideals in the subalgebras
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
to ideals in the respective quantum algebras.
\mathscr{G}
-invariance
trivially holds in the commutative case. It is clear that, if
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
is a Hopf subalgebra and
J
a Hopf ideal in
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
, then
\widehat{J}
is a Hopf ideal in the quantum algebra as well. By Theorem
7.16
and Lemma
7.15
this is the case for
J=\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
for any
s\in\mathscr{W}\,
.

A natural question related to the first item in Corollary
7.17
asks, for which
closed algebraic subgroups
C\leq B
the resulting ideal
\mathcal{A}(C)
can be
constructed without the choice of a particular ordering.
The observation in Item
ii)

of the corollary will be proved for all Lie types in Theorem
9.20
below.

The full
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}=\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\cdot\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
subalgebra naturally also forms a Hopf subalgebra, which, over
\mathbb{C}
, can also be identified with the coordinate ring of the algebraic group
{\mathrm{W}}_{n}=\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{C})^{\#}
as
defined in (
1.1
). One Borel algebra
B^{+}=\mathrm{T}_{b}
is given by the
usual upper triangular matrices and the opposite
B^{-}=\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-}
by the lower triangular ones. The algebraic maximal torus
\mathrm{D}_{n}=\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-}\cap\mathrm{T}_{n}
is, hence, given by
the diagonal matrices in
\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{C})
. Rephrasing definition (
1.1
)
in this notation, we have

{\mathrm{W}}_{n}=\ker\left(\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-}\times\mathrm{T}_{n}\,\longrightarrow\,\mathrm{D}_{n}\times\mathrm{D}_{n}\,\longrightarrow\,\mathrm{D}_{n}\right)\,.

The construction also implies
{\mathrm{W}}_{n}\cong\mathrm{D}_{n}\ltimes(\mathrm{U}_{n}^{-}\times\mathrm{U}_{n})
, where
\mathrm{U}_{n}^{-}
and
\mathrm{U}_{n}
are the respective unipotent subgroups. The next result extends
Corollary
7.14
. Although the existence of a Hopf algebra isomorphism is already implied in

[
20
]
for odd
\mathscr{k}
, we construct the map here explicitly via assignments of the polynomial generators of the form
R_{i,j}^{\pm}\mapsto\hat{x}_{i,j}^{\pm}\,
and also include the case

\mathscr{k}\equiv 0\mod 4
.

Lemma 7.18
.

Suppose
\zeta
is a
\mathscr{k}
-th root of unity and
U_{\zeta}=U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n})
as defined above.

i)

\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}
is a Hopf subalgebra of
U_{\zeta}\,
.

ii)

For
\mathscr{k}\not\equiv 2\mod 4
there is an isomorphism of Hopf algebras
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}\otimes\mathbb{C}\cong\mathbb{C}[{\mathrm{W}}_{n}]
.

iii)

Moreover, for such
\mathscr{k}
, any closed algebraic subgroup of
{\mathrm{W}}_{n}
defines a Hopf ideal in
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}
and, hence, a Hopf ideal of
U_{\zeta}\,
.

Proof.

Recall that the involution
\Pi:U_{\zeta}\rightarrow U_{\zeta}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}}}

from (
4.13
)
maps
U_{\zeta}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}({\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}})}
to
U_{\zeta}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}({\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}})}
with the opposite coproduct. In particular,
since
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
is a Hopf subalgebra, then so is
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}=\Pi(\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}})\,
. The product map

\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\otimes\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\rightarrow\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}

is a surjective Hopf algebra homomorphism with kernel given by the Hopf ideal
J=\sum_{i}\boldsymbol{\left(\right.}L_{i}^{-1}\otimes L_{i}-1\boldsymbol{\left.\right)}\,
. Composing this with
\Pi\otimes\mathrm{id}
, we obtain a surjection

\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}}}\otimes\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\rightarrow\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}

with kernel
J^{\prime}=\sum_{i}\boldsymbol{\left(\right.}L_{i}\otimes L_{i}-1\boldsymbol{\left.\right)}\,
. Over
\mathbb{C}
the isomorphism from
Corollary
7.14
allows us to replace
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
with
\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]

and
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}}}
with
\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}}]
, where
\mathrm{T}_{n}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}}
is naturally
identified with
\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-}
via transposition.

The kernel of the resulting epimorphism

\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-}\times\mathrm{T}_{n}]=\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-}]\otimes\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]\rightarrow\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}

is now the ideal
J^{\prime\prime}=\sum_{i}\boldsymbol{\left(\right.}(\hat{x}_{i,i},\hat{x}_{i,i})-1\boldsymbol{\left.\right)}=\sum_{i}\boldsymbol{\left(\right.}\hat{x}_{i,i}\otimes\hat{x}_{i,i}-1\boldsymbol{\left.\right)}
. The subgroup
\mathcal{V}(J^{\prime\prime})
now consists of
(a,b)\in\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-}\times\mathrm{T}_{n}
such that

\hat{x}_{i,i}(a)\hat{x}_{i,i}(b)=1
for all
i=1,\ldots,n\,
. The set of these pairs is now exactly
the kernel
{\mathrm{W}}_{n}
defined above. Lemma
7.1
then implies
J^{\prime\prime}=\mathcal{I}({\mathrm{W}}_{n})
and thus

\mathbb{C}[{\mathrm{W}}_{n}]\cong\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}\,
. The last statement is now also immediate from
Lemma
7.1
.
∎

Consider the natural center action of
\mathbb{C}^{\times}
on
{\mathrm{W}}_{n}
, given by

\lambda.(b^{-},b^{+})=(\lambda^{-1}b^{-},\lambda b^{+})
with
b^{-}\in\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-}
and
b\in\mathrm{T}_{n}\,
. The respective

\mathbb{C}^{\times}
action on the coordinate ring of
{\mathrm{W}}_{n}
over
\mathbb{C}
yields a direct decomposition

\mathbb{C}[{\mathrm{W}}_{n}]=\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{C}[{\mathrm{W}}_{n}]_{k}
with
f\in\mathbb{C}[{\mathrm{W}}_{n}]_{k}

characterized by
\lambda.f=\lambda^{k}\!\cdot\!f\,
. It is easy to check that this decomposition coincides
with the one imposed by the
\mathbb{p}
-grading introduced in Section
7.3
.

Thus, for
\mathscr{k}\not\equiv 2\mod 4
, the isomorphism in Lemma
7.18
restricts to an isomorphism
of Hopf algebras between
\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}\otimes\mathbb{C}
and
\mathbb{C}[{\mathrm{W}}_{n}]_{0}
, the
\mathbb{C}^{\times}
-invariant part of the coordinate ring, which, in turn, may be identified with

\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{PGL}(n,\mathbb{C})^{\#}]\,
.

The Artin group
\mathscr{A}=B_{n}

action on
U_{q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n})
generated by the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
naturally extends to
an action on
U_{q}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n})
by
\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(P_{i})=P_{s(i)}
, where
i\mapsto s(i)
is the
usual permutation for
s\in\mathscr{W}=S_{n}\,
. Lemma
7.18
now implies an action of
B_{n}
by
algebra automorphisms of
\mathbb{C}[{\mathrm{W}}_{n}]
. Invoking the standard correspondence between algebra homomorphisms of
coordinate rings and morphisms of algebraic varieties, this implies an action of
B_{n}
on
{\mathrm{W}}_{n}
.

Corollary 7.19
.

There exists a non-trivial action of the braid group
B_{n}
on
n
strands by algebraic automorphisms
on the algebraic group

{\mathrm{W}}_{n}
, commensurable with Lusztig’s
B_{n}
-action on the quantum group of Lie type
\mathsf{A}_{n-1}\,
.

It is, worth contrasting the correspondence in Lemma
7.18
for the central subalgebras with that of the traditional correspondences for the original quantum groups. For the latter
U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
and

U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
are associated with the opposing Borel subgroups and
U_{q}=U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}\cdot U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}

with the original simple or reductive Lie group.

However, for the central subalgebras, the associated Lie group
{\mathrm{W}}_{n}
is a solvable group and thus
fundamentally different from
\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{C})
. Correspondingly, the coordinate ring

\mathbb{C}[{\mathrm{W}}_{n}]\cong\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}
is cosolvable in the sense of Corollary
7.5
,
whereas
\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{C})]
is cosemisimple since
\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{C})
is reductive.
Similarly, the of group algebraic characters
\mathrm{Spec}_{\mathfrak{m}}({\mathrm{W}}_{n})\cong Gr(\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet})\cong\mathbb{Z}^{n}
differs from the one in
(
7.4
).

Lemma
7.18
allows us to associate, for example, the Hopf ideal

\mathcal{I}((K\times H)\cap{\mathrm{W}}_{n})
to any pair of subgroups

H\leq\mathrm{T}_{n}
and
K\leq\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-}\,
, which then define Hopf ideals
\mathcal{A}(K,H)
in

\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}
as before. These may then be reexpressed as

\mathcal{A}(K,H)=\mathcal{A}(K,\mathrm{T}_{n})+\mathcal{A}(\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-},H)=(\mathcal{A}(K)^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}+\mathcal{A}(H)^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}})\cdot\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}\,
. Specialized to the Bruhat subgroups this yields, together with
Theorem
7.16
and a respective definition of a Bruhat subgroup
B(t)^{-}<\mathrm{T}_{n}^{-}
, the identity of ideals

(7.36)

\mathcal{A}(B(t)^{-},B(s))=(\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(t)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}+\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(s)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}})\cdot\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}\qquad\mbox{ for any }s,t\in\mathscr{W}.

Concluding our discussion of the
\mathsf{A}_{n-1}
algebras, we briefly address the case
\mathscr{k}\equiv 2\mod 4
, when
\raise 1.3657pt\hbox{$\scalebox{.7}{$\boldsymbol{=}$}$}\mkern-7.7mu\zeta=-1
, as well as an approach to the next simply laced Lie types.

We first provide a concrete description of Tanisaki’s isomorphism from
[
72
]
for the subgroup
\mathrm{T}_{n}<\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{C})
. Let
{\mathsf{I}}_{s}\in\mathrm{T}_{n}
be the diagonal matrix with

({\mathsf{I}}_{s})_{s,s}=-1
and
({\mathsf{I}}_{s})_{i,i}=1
for
i\neq s\,
. For any
1\leq s\leq t\leq n
define the
map
\tau_{s,t}:\mathrm{T}_{n}\rightarrow\mathrm{T}_{n}
by
\tau_{s,t}(b)={\mathsf{I}}_{s}\cdot b\cdot{\mathsf{I}}_{t}\,
. Clearly, all
\tau_{s,t}
are of order 2 and commute with each other, generating an
elementary abelian 2-group
\mathscr{G}
of isomorphisms of
\mathrm{T}_{n}
as an algebraic variety.
Obviously, none of the
\tau_{s,t}
are a group homomorphism of
\mathrm{T}_{n}
and
the quotient variety
\mathrm{T}_{n}/\mathscr{G}
retains no group structure either.

Lemma 7.20
.

Assume
\mathscr{k}\equiv 2\mod 4
and Lie type
\mathsf{A}_{n-1}
. Let
\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Fr}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
be the intersection of
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\otimes\mathbb{C}
with the center of
U_{\zeta,\mathbb{C}}
. Then there is a weight-preserving algebraic isomorphism of commutative algebras,

\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Fr}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\,\cong\,\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]^{\mathscr{G}}\,\cong\,\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}/{\mathscr{G}}]\,.

Proof.

It follows from the commutation relations in Section
6.2
that
\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Fr}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
is identical with the center of
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\otimes\mathbb{C}\cong\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\mathbb{C})
itself.
Denote
R^{f}=\prod_{i\leq j}R_{i,j}^{f_{i,j}}

for some fixed ordering and

\hat{x}^{f}=\prod_{i\leq j}\hat{x}_{i,j}^{f_{i,j}}
as before. Recall that
R_{i,j}R_{s,t}=(-1)^{\delta_{i,s}+\delta_{j,t}}R_{s,t}R_{i,j}
and
observe that
\tau_{s,t}^{*}(\hat{x}_{i,j})=(-1)^{\delta_{i,s}+\delta_{j,t}}\hat{x}_{i,j}\,
.
It is clear from these formulae that

R^{f}
is central if and only if
\hat{x}^{f}
is
\mathscr{G}
-stable. Write
M\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^{\binom{n+1}{2}}
for the set of exponents
f=(f_{i,j})
for which this is the case, namely,
those for which
\sum_{s\leq j}f_{s,j}+\sum_{i\leq t}f_{i,t}\equiv 0\mod 2
for all
s\leq t\,
.
Depending on the chosen ordering, it now follows from commutativity that
one can then choose a quadratic form
\vartheta
on

M\otimes\mathbb{Z}
such that for
\tilde{R}^{f}=(\scalebox{.75}{$\sqrt{-1}\,$})^{\vartheta(f)}R^{f}
we have

\tilde{R}^{f}\cdot\tilde{R}^{g}=\tilde{R}^{f+g}
. Thus,
\hat{x}^{f}\mapsto\tilde{R}^{f}

defines an isomorphism of algebras over
\mathbb{C}
.
∎

As an elementary example, it is easy to see that
\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{2}]^{\mathscr{G}}
corresponds to the subalgebra generated
by
R_{1,1}^{2}
,
R_{1,2}^{2}
, and
R_{2,2}R_{1,1}^{-1}
, which is clearly not a Hopf subalgebra. Also,
we have
\mathscr{G}\cong\mathbb{F}_{2}\times\mathbb{F}_{2}
acting component-wise on
\mathrm{T}_{2}\cong(\mathbb{C}^{\times})^{2}\times\mathbb{C}
by
(x_{11},x_{22})\mapsto(-x_{11},-x_{22})
and

x_{12}\mapsto-x_{12}
, respectively. So,
\mathrm{T}_{2}/\mathscr{G}
has no obvious group structure.

As an alternative approach to finding an interpretation of
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\mathbb{C})

and thus
\mkern 1.5mu\overset{\sim}{\rule{0.0pt}{3.7pt}}\mkern-12.0mu{\mathcal{Z}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\otimes\mathbb{C}

we may seek to retain the coordinate ring
\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]
as a target set, but modify the
multiplication and comultiplication maps as weighted averages with respect to some

\mathscr{G}
-action. We propose the following form of a possible Hopf algebra structure.

Conjecture 7.21
.

There exist modified multiplication
{\scriptstyle\star}
and comultiplication

\ddot{\Delta}
on
\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{T}_{n}]
of the form

(7.37)

\phi{\scriptstyle\star}\psi=\sum_{\sigma,\tau}\mu(\sigma,\tau)\,\tau^{*}(\phi)\sigma^{*}(\psi)\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\ddot{\Delta}(\phi)(a,b)=\sum_{\sigma,\tau}\eta(\sigma,\tau)\,\phi(\sigma(a)\tau(b))\,,

such that
(\mathbb{C}[B_{n}],{\scriptstyle\star},\ddot{\Delta})
is isomorphic to
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\mathbb{C})\,
.
Here summations are over algebraic involutions
\sigma:\mathrm{T}_{n}\rightarrow\mathrm{T}_{n}
with

\sigma^{*}(\hat{x}_{i,j})=\pm\hat{x}_{i,j}
and the weights
\mu
and
\eta
take values
in
\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1}{2}]\,
.

Again, the involutions are not required to be homomorphisms.
In this form, the definition of Hopf ideals as vanishing ideals on subgroups
then requires that these subgroups are
preserved under the groups of involutions. This is indeed the case for the Bruhat subgroups.
We mention that versions of the specific quantum matrix algebras
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\Lambda)
are recovered also in Proposition 2 of
[
17
]
as images of a Frobenius map.

Overall, however, the skew matrix algebras
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\Lambda)
are scarcely studied in the literature despite their natural occurrences, lacking any semi-classical interpretations one might expect.
Following
[
7
]
the algebra
\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{T}_{n},\mathsf{a},\Lambda)
is constructable from the skew coordinate algebra
generated by
\{x_{i}:i=1,\ldots,n\}
subject to relations
x_{i}x_{j}=-x_{j}x_{i}
if
i\neq j\,
. Particularly, the generators
x_{i}

remain of infinite order and the algebra is fundamentally distinct from finite-dimensional exterior or Clifford algebras.
There, thus, appear to be no obvious identifications of the skew matrix algebras with function algebras on super or spin groups.

Among the simply laced Lie types,
\mathsf{D}_{n}
has several well understood
relations to
\mathsf{A}
type algebras.
Clearly, it contains an
\mathsf{A}_{n-2}
algebra and we, conjecturally, expect there to be a
quotient of the respective algebras from the
\mathsf{A}_{2n-1}
onto the
\mathsf{D}_{n}
. The derivations of explicit coproduct formulae
as those in (
7.22
) and (
7.25
), however, are considerably more challenging.

Kharchenko
[
41
]
provides explicit coproduct formulae for the generic
\mathsf{D}_{n}
algebra with coefficients over
\Lambda_{q}
reminiscent of the ones in
(
7.22
) for type
\mathsf{A}
. Computations of powers to arrive
at the analogues of (
7.25
), however, are substantially more
complicated since two types of basis generators are involved. They are
defined via recursions as the one in (
7.17
) but in opposing directions,
and neither subset of generators spans a subcoalgebra.

8.
The Structure of
\mathcal{Z}
and Hopf Ideals for Type
\mathsf{B}_{2}

The accessible computational tools for
\mathfrak{gl}_{n}
allowed us to verify the claims in
Conjectures
7.13
and
8.11
computationally for all

\mathsf{A}_{n-1}
algebras. As additional evidence for these conjectures, we prove them
in this section also for the simplest non-simply laced Lie type
\mathsf{B}_{2}=\mathsf{C}_{2}
.
The descriptions of isomorphisms and subspaces will be in very explicit terms,
while computations are much more involved. The latter are assured to play a central
role in extensions to other doubly-laced Lie types, as they illustrate
additional methods and principles for the construction of isomorphisms.

Throughout this section, we assume that the order of
\zeta
is
\mathscr{k}>4
or
\mathscr{k}=3
,
but impose no other restrictions on
\mathscr{k}
. As pointed out in
Remark
6.15
for
\mathsf{B}_{2}
, the subalgebra

\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}
is commutative for
all

\mathscr{k}
,
though central in
U_{\zeta}
only if
\mathscr{k}
is not a
multiple of 4.

In Section
8.1
we describe the explicit Hopf algebra structure of
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}
,
deferring the computation of coproducts for non-simple roots to Section
8.2
.
The fact that
\mathcal{Z}
is a Hopf subalgebra may be indirectly inferred also from
[
20
]

for odd
\mathscr{k}
, though no explicit formulae or computations are given there, leaving open
also the case of even roots of unity.
The Hopf algebra structure of the Borel
coordinate ring
\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{SO}_{5}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}]
is explicitly determined in Section
8.3
.
A similarly explicit isomorphism of
\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{SO}_{5}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}]
with
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}\otimes\mathbb{C}
is established in Section
8.4
.

8.1.
Coalgebra Structure of
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}
for Type
\mathsf{B}_{2}

This section provides the
full list of
coproduct formulae for the generators of
\mathcal{Z}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}_{\bullet}
for Lie type

\mathsf{B}_{2}\,
, preceded by a review of essential notation and conventions.

As in Section
2.7
, we denote by
\alpha_{i}
the short root of
\mathsf{B}_{2}
and by

\alpha_{j}
the long root. Thus,
s_{j}(\alpha_{i})=\alpha_{i}+\alpha_{j}
is the second short root and

s_{i}(\alpha_{j})=2\alpha_{i}+\alpha_{j}
the second long root. The default ground ring for the generic

\mathsf{B}_{2}
algebra is

\Lambda=\Lambda_{q,3}=\mathbb{Z}\textstyle{\left[q^{\pm 1},[2]^{-1}\right]}
as defined in (
3.8
).

Recall the formulae for the standard generators with respect to
\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}
as defined in (
5.19
), which follow readily from the automorphisms in (
4.20
) and (

), as well as their
