{\hat{\mathcal{L}}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-15.6448pt}{\hskip-11.17485pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.55244pt}=U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}\cdot{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-15.6448pt}{\hskip-11.17485pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.55244pt}\cdot U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}
.
Analogously, the subspaces
{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}={\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-15.6448pt}{\hskip-11.17485pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.55244pt}\hat{\otimes}{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-15.6448pt}{\hskip-11.17485pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.55244pt}
are defined
from formal sums
\sum_{\phi,\psi\in\mathcal{E}(s)}R_{\phi,\psi}({E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\chi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-2.24924pt}{\hskip-1.60658pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}\otimes{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt})
with
R_{\phi,\psi}\in({\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle-\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-0.3349pt}{\hskip-0.3349pt}{\hskip-0.52795pt}{\hskip-0.89737pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}\!\cdot U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{0})^{\otimes 2}
, generating the

U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{\otimes 2}
-sub-bimodules
{\hat{\mathcal{L}}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-15.6448pt}{\hskip-11.17485pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.55244pt}={\hat{\mathcal{L}}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-15.6448pt}{\hskip-11.17485pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.55244pt}\hat{\otimes}{\hat{\mathcal{L}}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-25.55244pt}{\hskip-15.6448pt}{\hskip-11.17485pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.55244pt}
.

The next lemma follows by applying (
5.37
) or (
5.26
) to the limiting expressions.

Lemma 9.6
.

Suppose
u_{1},u_{2}\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
are reduced words such that

w=u_{1}\cdot u_{2}
is reduced. Let
t_{i}=\mathscr{r}(u_{i})
and
s=t_{1}\cdot t_{2}=\mathscr{r}(w)

so that
l(s)=l(t_{1})+l(t_{2})\,
.
Then
\mathit{\Gamma}_{t_{1}}
extends to a linear map on
{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}u_{2}\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-17.3104pt}{\hskip-13.00743pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 28.04324pt}
as well as
{\hat{\mathcal{L}}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}u_{2}\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-17.3104pt}{\hskip-13.00743pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 28.04324pt}
with
images
\mathit{\Gamma}_{t_{1}}({\hat{\mathcal{L}}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}u_{2}\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-17.3104pt}{\hskip-13.00743pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 28.04324pt})\subseteq{\hat{\mathcal{L}}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.3386pt}{\hskip-26.3386pt}{\hskip-15.8952pt}{\hskip-11.35371pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.3386pt}
and

\mathit{\Gamma}_{t_{1}}({\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}u_{2}\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-17.3104pt}{\hskip-13.00743pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 28.04324pt})\subseteq{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.3386pt}{\hskip-26.3386pt}{\hskip-15.8952pt}{\hskip-11.35371pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.3386pt}
in
\hat{U}_{q,\mathbb{Q}}\,
.

Analogously,
\mathit{\Gamma}_{t_{1}}^{\otimes 2}
extends to a linear map on
{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}u_{2}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-29.2099pt}{\hskip-29.2099pt}{\hskip-18.12704pt}{\hskip-13.59076pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 29.2099pt}
and
{\hat{\mathcal{L}}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}u_{2}\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-17.3104pt}{\hskip-13.00743pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 28.04324pt}
with
images
\mathit{\Gamma}_{t_{1}}^{\otimes 2}({\hat{\mathcal{L}}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}u_{2}\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-28.04324pt}{\hskip-17.3104pt}{\hskip-13.00743pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 28.04324pt})\subseteq{\hat{\mathcal{L}}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.3386pt}{\hskip-26.3386pt}{\hskip-15.8952pt}{\hskip-11.35371pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.3386pt}
and

\mathit{\Gamma}_{t_{1}}^{\otimes 2}({\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}u_{2}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-29.2099pt}{\hskip-29.2099pt}{\hskip-18.12704pt}{\hskip-13.59076pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 29.2099pt})\subseteq{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-27.50525pt}{\hskip-27.50525pt}{\hskip-16.71185pt}{\hskip-11.93704pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 27.50525pt}
in
\hat{U}_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{\hat{\otimes}2}\,
.

Clearly,
\mathcal{P}_{i},\mathcal{P}_{i}^{-1}\in{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w_{i}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-28.90721pt}{\hskip-28.90721pt}{\hskip-18.16725pt}{\hskip-13.46397pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 28.90721pt}
with
w_{i}
a word of length one. Suppose
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}

with
\tau(w)=i
, so that
w=w^{\flat}\cdot w_{i}
. Then Lemma
9.6
allows us to define an
elementary
quasi-
R
-matrix associated to the reduced word
w
as

(9.9)

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{w}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{w^{\flat}}\otimes\mathit{\Gamma}_{w^{\flat}}(\mathcal{P}_{i})=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\dfrac{q^{j(j-1)/2}_{i}}{[j]!_{i}}(q_{i}-q^{-1}_{i})^{j}E_{w}^{j}\otimes F_{w}^{j}\,.

Following the conventions of (
2.15
) and Section
2.3
, we write
\beta^{j}=\gamma(w[1,j])
and
w^{j}=w[1,j]=w[\beta_{j}]
. Assume that
L=l(w)
. In the notation of Section
5.3
,
we define the
partial
quasi-
R
-matrix associated to
w
by the following products in
\hat{U}_{q,\mathbb{Q}}\hat{\otimes}\hat{U}_{q,\mathbb{Q}}\,
.

(9.10)

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}=\mathcal{P}_{w^{L}}\ldots\mathcal{P}_{w^{1}}=\mathcal{P}_{w[\beta_{L}]}\ldots\mathcal{P}_{w[\beta_{1}]}=\sum_{\psi\in\mathcal{E}(s)}\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu^{-1}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}\otimes{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}\quad\in{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}\,

Here
s=\mathscr{r}(w)
and the coefficients in
\mathbb{Q}(q)
are given by

(9.11)

\displaystyle\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}

\displaystyle=\frac{[\psi]!}{\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu}\quad\in\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\quad\mbox{where}\quad[\psi]!=\prod_{\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}}[\psi(\alpha)]!_{\alpha}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{17.07164pt}\quad\mbox{and}\quad\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}

\displaystyle=\prod_{\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}}\!q_{\alpha}^{\psi(\alpha)(\psi(\alpha)-1)/2}(q_{\alpha}-q_{\alpha}^{-1})^{\psi(\alpha)}=(-1)^{n(\psi)}\cdot\boldsymbol{\delta}^{\psi}\mkern-1.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu\cdot q^{\sum_{\alpha}d_{\alpha}\binom{\psi(\alpha)}{2}}\;.

The elements
[\psi]!
and
\boldsymbol{\delta}^{\psi}\mkern-1.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu
are as defined in (
5.33
) and (
5.34
), respectively.
Thus, in the product expressions, we consider all positive roots rather than just those in
\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)

and assume
\psi\in\mathcal{E}(s)
is extended to all of
{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
by setting
\psi
to zero outside of

\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)
.

The inclusion in
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
is obvious from the definitions, and the
formal sum expression in (
9.10
) is immediate from the definitions
in (
5.23
). It also implies the indicated inclusion into
{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}\,
.

Let
w=u_{1}\cdot u_{2}\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
and
t_{i}=\mathscr{r}(u_{i})
as above so that
l(s)=l(t_{1})+l(t_{2})

for
s=t_{1}t_{2}=\mathscr{r}(w)\,
. Lemma
9.6
now implies that
\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{t_{1}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{u_{2}}})
is well-defined and given by applying
\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{t_{1}}
to individual summands.
Since the
q_{\alpha}
depend only the
\mathscr{W}
-orbit of
\alpha
, one readily checks that

\mathbf{c}_{s^{*}(\psi)}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu=\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu
. In the situation where
\psi
and
(\psi_{1},\psi_{2})
are
related as in (
5.3
), we infer from this that

\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu=\mathbf{c}_{\psi_{1}}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu\mathbf{c}_{(t_{1}^{-1})^{*}(\psi_{2})}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu=\mathbf{c}_{\psi_{1}}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu\mathbf{c}_{\psi_{2}}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu
.
Together with (
5.26
) we then find the following well-defined recursion.

(9.12)

\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\,=\,\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{t_{1}}\left(\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{u_{2}}}\right)\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{u_{1}}}\quad\in{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}\,

A central property of the
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}
elements is that they intertwine
the standard coproduct
\Delta
with
\Delta^{\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}}
, the coproduct conjugated by the braid automorphism for the same word.

Proposition 9.7
.

Suppose
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
and
x\in U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}
. Then the following
relation holds in
{\hat{\mathcal{L}}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.3386pt}{\hskip-26.3386pt}{\hskip-15.8952pt}{\hskip-11.35371pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.3386pt}\,
,

(9.13)

\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\cdot\Delta(\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}(x))=\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}^{\otimes 2}(\Delta(x))\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\,.

Proof.

The proof proceeds by induction on the length of
w\,
. For a length one word
w=w_{i}
we have
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w_{i}}}=\mathcal{P}_{i}
, reducing (
9.13
) to

\mathcal{P}_{i}\cdot\Delta(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(x))=\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\otimes 2}(\Delta(x))\cdot\mathcal{P}_{i}\,.

This case is verified, for example, by taking a formal limit
{\ell_{i}}\rightarrow\infty
for the computations in Appendix
A
.
It also appears in some
equivalent variations in
[
44
, Prop.2.4.1]
,
[
42
, pg.429]
, or

[
3
, App.C.4]
.

Assume next that (
9.13
) holds for
w\in\mathscr{W}
and that
w\cdot w_{i}\in\mathscr{W}
is reduced. From (
9.12
) we obtain
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w\cdot w_{i}}}\,=\,\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}(\mathcal{P}_{i})\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}
as a well-defined relation in
{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\cdot w_{i}\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-39.73093pt}{\hskip-39.73093pt}{\hskip-22.35156pt}{\hskip-16.45274pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 39.73093pt}\hskip-4.30554pt
.
The expressions and calculations below are now well-defined on
{\hat{\mathcal{L}}}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w\cdot w_{i}\!$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-39.73093pt}{\hskip-39.73093pt}{\hskip-22.35156pt}{\hskip-16.45274pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 39.73093pt}\hskip-4.30554pt

by Lemma
9.6
. They
use both the induction hypothesis and the base case relations.

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w\cdot w_{i}}(\Delta(x))\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w\cdot w_{i}}}

\displaystyle=\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}\circ\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{i}(\Delta(x))\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}(\mathcal{P}_{i})\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}

\displaystyle=\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}\left(\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{i}\left(\Delta(x)\right)\cdot\mathcal{P}_{i}\right)\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}

\displaystyle=\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}\left(\mathcal{P}_{i}\cdot\Delta(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(x))\right)\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}

\displaystyle=\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}\left(\mathcal{P}_{i}\right)\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}\left(\Delta(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(x))\right)\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}

\displaystyle=\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}(\mathcal{P}_{i})\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\cdot\Delta(\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(x)))

\displaystyle=\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w\cdot w_{i}}}\cdot\Delta(\mathit{\Gamma}_{w\cdot w_{i}}(x))

This shows the assertion for
w\cdot w_{i}
, completing the proof.
∎

An identity similar to (
9.13
) can be found in
[
16
, Prop 8.3.7]
in the special case of
x=E_{i}
with
w\cdot w_{i}
reduced. The derivation there also involves certain quantum Weyl elements, which generally exist only in representations that admit a compatible
\mathscr{W}
-action and, hence, limiting the statement to an identity between linear maps on such representations.
We, therefore, abstain from the use of techniques using Weyl elements here.
See, Appendix
C
for further details.

A
full
quasi-
R
-matrix is associated to any reduced word of maximal length. The first step in verifying independence of the choice of word is an intertwining relation with a twisted coproduct defined on
generators by

(9.14)

\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta(E_{i})=E_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{-1}+1\otimes E_{i}\,,\qquad\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta(F_{i})=F_{i}\otimes 1+K_{i}\otimes F_{i}\,,\quad\mbox{and}\quad\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta(K_{i})=K_{i}\otimes K_{i}\;.

It is easy to check that
\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta\circ\amalg=\amalg^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta
, where

\amalg
is as in (
4.13
). The latter involution coincides with the bar involution
in
[
47
, 3.1.12]
so that
\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta
coincides with the alternate coproduct defined
in
[
47
, 4.1.1]
. The next result uses the fact that, for maximal length words, the
coproduct is conjugated by the Garside automorphism, for which we derived an explicit form
in Section
5.2
.

Lemma 9.8
.

Suppose
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
is a reduced word of maximal length and
x\in U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}
.
Then

(9.15)

\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\cdot\Delta(x)=\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta(x)\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\,.

Proof.

Recall from Corollary
5.3
that
\mathit{\Gamma}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}=\mbox{\hskip-12.80373pt
I}\circ\Pi\circ\mho\circ S
for the longest
element
{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}\in\mathscr{W}\,
. It is easy to check that

\Pi\circ\mho=\amalg\circ\Omega
for the commuting involutions defined in
Section
4.2
. Thus,
\mathit{\Gamma}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}=\amalg\circ Q
, where

Q=\mbox{\hskip-12.80373pt
I}\circ\Omega\circ S
. Recall that both
\Omega,S:U_{q}\rightarrow U_{q}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{cop}$}}}}
are anti-coalgebra anti-automorphisms and

I
, defined in (
5.12
), is a Hopf algebra automorphism. Thus,
Q
intertwines the coalgebra structure
Q^{\otimes 2}(\Delta(y))=\Delta(Q(y))
. Given that
{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}=\mathscr{r}(z)\,
, Proposition
9.7
now implies

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\cdot\Delta(x)

\displaystyle=\mathit{\Gamma}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}^{\otimes 2}\left(\Delta\bigl(\mathit{\Gamma}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}^{-1}(x)\bigr)\right)\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}

\displaystyle=\amalg^{\otimes 2}\circ Q^{\otimes 2}\left(\Delta\bigl(Q^{-1}\circ\amalg^{-1}(x)\bigr)\right)\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}

\displaystyle=\amalg^{\otimes 2}\left(\Delta(\amalg^{-1}(x))\right)\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}

\displaystyle=\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta(x)\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\;.

∎

In
[
47
, Thm.4.1.2(a)]
Lusztig shows that an element
\Theta
in some completion of

\oplus_{\nu}(U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{-})_{\nu}\otimes(U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{+})_{\nu}
is uniquely determined by the relation

\Theta\cdot\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}}(y)={\Delta\mkern-3.0mu}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}(y)\cdot\Theta
(since
[
47
]
uses the opposite coproduct of ours).
The required assumptions can be readily checked for
\Theta=(\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}^{-1})^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}}
using the
general form as in (
9.10
), the commutation (
9.15
), and
noting that the completions align. From the uniqueness of solutions to (
9.15
) we infer word independence for quasi-
R
-matices associated to reduced words of maximal length.

Corollary 9.9
.

There exists
\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}\in\hat{U}_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{\hat{\otimes}2}\,
such that
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}=\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\;
for all
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
.
Moreover,
\amalg^{\otimes 2}(\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet})=\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}^{-1}
.

9.3.
Pre-Triangular Structures for
U_{q}

Since the coefficients in (
9.9
) may be evaluated at
q=1
, the element
\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}\,

has a well-defined image
\,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}^{\hbar}\,
in the power series completion
U_{\hbar}(\mathfrak{g})\hat{\otimes}U_{\hbar}(\mathfrak{g})

over
\mathbb{Q}\lBrack\hbar\rBrack
as in Section
3.2
.
Originally, universal
R
-matrices were constructed in this setting by Drinfeld
[
25
]
as products

\mathcal{R}^{\hbar}=\mathcal{\mathcal{D}}\cdot\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}^{\hbar}
in
U_{\hbar}(\mathfrak{g})^{\hat{\otimes}2}\,
. The “diagonal” term is given by

(9.16)

\mathcal{D}=\exp\left(\hbar\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}(B^{-1})_{ij}H_{i}\otimes H_{j}\right)\,,

where

B_{ij}=A_{ij}d_{j}^{-1}=\mathchoice{\left(\breve{\alpha}_{i}|\breve{\alpha}_{j}\right)}{(\breve{\alpha}_{i}|\breve{\alpha}_{j})}{(\breve{\alpha}_{i}|\breve{\alpha}_{j})}{(\breve{\alpha}_{i}|\breve{\alpha}_{j})}=C_{ij}d_{i}^{-1}d_{j}^{-1}\in{\mathsf{e}}^{-1}\mathbb{Z}

with notation as in Section
2.1
.
Explicit formulae are obtained in
[
65
]
for the
\mathsf{A}_{n}
case and
[
42
]
for general Lie types, see also
[
16
]
. Tanisaki’s axioms in
[
71
]
or (
9.2
) above are motivated by the fact
that
\mathcal{D}
cannot be defined in
U_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{\otimes 2}
, but conjugation by
\mathcal{D}
can be expressed as an automorphism on
\hat{U}_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{\hat{\otimes}2}\,
.

Specifically, if
x
and
y
are homogeneously graded elements with

\mathbb{w}(x)=\mu,\mathbb{w}(y)=\nu\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
, we have
[H_{i}\,,x]=\mathchoice{\left(\mu|\breve{\alpha}_{i}\right)}{(\mu|\breve{\alpha}_{i})}{(\mu|\breve{\alpha}_{i})}{(\mu|\breve{\alpha}_{i})}x

and
[H_{j}\,,y]=\mathchoice{\left(\nu|\breve{\alpha}_{j}\right)}{(\nu|\breve{\alpha}_{j})}{(\nu|\breve{\alpha}_{j})}{(\nu|\breve{\alpha}_{j})}y
. From this we obtain

\sum_{i,j}(B^{-1})_{ij}[H_{i}\otimes H_{j}\,,x\otimes y]=x\otimes(H_{\mu}\cdot y)+(x\cdot H_{\nu})\otimes y
, where

H_{\mu}=\sum_{i}\mu_{i}d_{i}H_{i}
if
\mu=\sum_{i}\mu_{i}\alpha_{i}\,
. Exponentiation
t\mapsto e^{-\hbar t}
of the implied adjoint and
regular actions on
x\otimes y
together with the notation from (
4.1
)
then yields the identities below.

(9.17)

\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}(x\otimes y)=\mathcal{D}^{-1}(x\otimes y)\mathcal{D}=xK^{-\nu}\otimes K^{-\mu}y=q^{-\mathchoice{\left(\mu|\nu\right)}{(\mu|\nu)}{(\mu|\nu)}{(\mu|\nu)}}xK^{-\nu}\otimes yK^{-\mu}\,

Thus, although the Tanisaki automorphism is initially defined as
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}=\mathrm{Ad}(\mathcal{D}^{-1})

on
U_{\hbar}(\mathfrak{g})^{\hat{\otimes}2}\,
, it clearly maps the subalgebras
U_{q}^{\otimes 2}
and
\hat{U}_{q,\mathbb{Q}}^{\hat{\otimes}2}

to themselves. The form in (
9.16
) can often still be defined, at least up to scalars, on
tensor products of certain modules of
U_{q}^{\otimes 2}
, implying
solutions to the Yang Baxter equations or solutions to (
9.3
).

For example, for generic highest weight representations
V
and
W
, the maps
D_{V,W}
can be designed starting from generalized Verma modules. For a tuple
\kappa=(\kappa_{1},\ldots,\kappa_{n})\in\mathbf{u}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
with
\mathbf{u}
a group of units in the ground ring, the
generic Verma module

V(\kappa)
is defined as the induced representation from the one-dimensional
U_{q}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
representation, given by
K_{i}v_{\kappa}=\kappa_{i}v_{\kappa}
and
E_{i}v_{\kappa}=0
on a basis vector
v_{\kappa}
. As usual, there is a
linear isomorphism
U_{q}^{-}\rightarrow V(\kappa):x\mapsto x.v\,
.

Assume now for homogeneous
x,y\in U_{q}^{-}
that
-\mathbb{w}(x)=\mathbb{w}^{-}(x)=\mu
and
-\mathbb{w}(y)=\mathbb{w}^{-}(y)=\nu
and write
\kappa^{\mu}=\kappa_{1}^{\mu_{1}}\ldots\mu_{n}^{\mu_{n}}
for
\mu\in\mathbb{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}}
. Then linear maps on tensor
products of generic Verma modules are well-defined by the formula below. They are unique solutions to
the equation

D^{-1}cD=\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}(c)
of module maps (with

L
as in (
9.17
)) up to an overall scalar factor.

(9.18)

D_{V(\kappa),V(\lambda)}((x.v_{\kappa})\otimes(y,v_{\lambda}))=q^{\mathchoice{\left(\mu|\nu\right)}{(\mu|\nu)}{(\mu|\nu)}{(\mu|\nu)}}\kappa^{-\nu}\lambda^{-\mu}((x.v_{\kappa})\otimes(y.v_{\lambda}))\,

It is not hard to check that the respective isomorphisms

V(\kappa)\otimes V(\lambda)\rightarrow V(\lambda)\otimes V(\kappa)
, as defined in Corollary
9.4
, obey the Yang Baxter Equation and, thus, produce a
representation of the colored braid groupoids over
\mathbb{Q}(q)[\{\kappa_{i}^{\pm 1},\lambda_{i}^{\pm 1},\ldots\}]\,
.

The categorical triangle relations may be realized in a more general setting, in which we consider a
commutative ring

Z

with
\mathrm{char}(\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z})=0
and an extension of

\mathchoice{\left(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,\right)}{(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,)}{(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,)}{(\,\cdot\,|\,\cdot\,)}\,:\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\times\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\rightarrow\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z}
for the form from (
2.2
). Elements of the group ring
\mathbb{Z}[\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z}]
may be written
formally as
q^{x}
with
x\in\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z}
. Denoting
\mathbb{Q}(\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z})
as the field of fractions,
we have
\mathbb{Q}(\mathbb{Z})=\mathbb{Q}(q)\,
.
As a tensor category, one may then consider representations of
U_{q}
on
\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
-graded
vector spaces
V=\bigoplus_{\gamma}V_{\gamma}
subject to the condition that
K_{i}v=q^{\mathchoice{\left(\breve{\alpha}_{i}|\gamma\right)}{(\breve{\alpha}_{i}|\gamma)}{(\breve{\alpha}_{i}|\gamma)}{(\breve{\alpha}_{i}|\gamma)}}v
for

v\in V_{\gamma}
and
\gamma\in\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}\,
.
For two graded representations
V
and
W
,
define then
D_{V,W}
to be
q^{\mathchoice{\left(\gamma|\eta\right)}{(\gamma|\eta)}{(\gamma|\eta)}{(\gamma|\eta)}}
on the
V_{\gamma}\otimes V_{\eta}

component.

The relations (
9.3
) and (
9.17
) are now easily verified
on such modules, yielding a braided tensor category
\mathcal{C}
over
\mathbb{Q}(\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z})
. As an abelian
category the latter naturally splits in a sum
\bigoplus_{\rho}\mathcal{C}_{\rho}
with
\rho\in\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z}^{1}=\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z}/\mathbb{Z}\,
with the obvious
\scalebox{-.93}[1]{\hskip-13.51505pt
Z}^{1}
-graded behavior for tensors.

The main result for the generic case is summarized in the proposition below. It has been stated at various levels of rigor and formality in numerous other places in the literature. We adapt here results from
[
47
]
to our conventions, which itself is following similar calculations as those in
[
71
, Theorem 4.3.3]
.

Proposition 9.10
.

The triple
(\hat{U}_{q,\mathbb{Q}}\,,\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}\,,\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L})
is a pre-triangular bialgebra.

Proof.

A straightforward verification on generators shows that
\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta=\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}\circ{\Delta\mkern-3.0mu}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}
.
Lemma
9.8
then implies the last relation in (
9.2
).

The argument preceding Corollary
9.9
identifies Lusztig’s universal element with our quasi-
R
-matrix via
\Theta=(\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}^{-1})^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}
or, equivalently,
\overline{\Theta}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}=\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}\,
so that, restricted to
weight components, we have for any
\nu\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}

\overline{\Theta}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}_{\nu}=(\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet})_{\nu}=\sum_{\psi:\,\vec{\psi}=\nu}\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu^{-1}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\otimes{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\;,

with
\vec{\psi}
as defined in Section
5.3
and
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}\,
.
Exchanging Lusztig’s conventions with ours, namely
\Delta
with
{\Delta\mkern-3.0mu}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}
and
\tilde{K}_{-\nu}
by
K^{-\nu}
, the formula in
[
47
, pg 38]
reads

(\Delta^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}\otimes 1)\overline{\Theta}_{\mu}=\sum_{\nu^{\prime}+\nu^{\prime\prime}=\mu}\overline{\Theta}_{\nu^{\prime}}^{13}(1\otimes K^{-\nu^{\prime}}\otimes 1)\overline{\Theta}_{\nu^{\prime\prime}}^{23}\,.

Applying the
(13)
permutation to the tensor factors and substituting the
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}
components above we arrive at

(9.19)

(1\otimes\Delta){\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}}_{\mu}=\sum_{\nu^{\prime}+\nu^{\prime\prime}=\mu}{\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}}_{\nu^{\prime}}^{13}(1\otimes K^{-\nu^{\prime}}\otimes 1){\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}}_{\nu^{\prime\prime}}^{12}=\sum_{\nu^{\prime}+\nu^{\prime\prime}=\mu}\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}_{12}({\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}}_{\nu^{\prime}}^{13}){\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}}_{\nu^{\prime\prime}}^{12}\,,

using formula (
9.17
) for

L
. Summation, in the sense of the inverse limits,
then yields the first identity in
(
9.2
). The second follows analogously.
∎

A left inverse of
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet}
may be constructed by applying the map
a\otimes b\otimes c\mapsto a\otimes S^{-1}(c)b

to the first relation in (
9.19
). Using the antipode axiom for
\Delta^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}
,
the expression in (
9.10
) for a maximal word
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
,
the formulae for the antipode on basis elements in (
5.31
), as well as notations from (
5.21
) and (
2.19
) we obtain that

(9.20)

\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}=\sum_{\psi\in\mathcal{E}_{\bullet}}(-1)^{0pt(\vec{\psi})}q^{-\frac{1}{2}(\mathchoice{\left(\vec{\psi}|\vec{\psi}\right)}{(\vec{\psi}|\vec{\psi})}{(\vec{\psi}|\vec{\psi})}{(\vec{\psi}|\vec{\psi})}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho|\vec{\psi}\right)}{(\rho|\vec{\psi})}{(\rho|\vec{\psi})}{(\rho|\vec{\psi})})}\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu^{-1}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\otimes{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z^{\dagger}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-27.53116pt}{\hskip-27.53116pt}{\hskip-17.3714pt}{\hskip-12.99545pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 27.53116pt}\qquad\in{\mkern 5.0mu\raise 6.02773pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\circ}$}\mkern-11.0mu\mathcal{L}^{\,2}\!\!\!}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 1.16666pt}{\hskip 0.81665pt}{\hskip 0.58333pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}

is a left inverse of
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}

by summation over all graded components in the limit. A similar calculation, applying

a\otimes b\otimes c\mapsto a\otimes cS^{-1}(b)
and the automorphism
x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes yK^{\nu}
for
\mathbb{w}(x)=\nu
, shows that
\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}
is also a right inverse of
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\,
.

Applying
a\otimes b\otimes c\mapsto aS(b)\otimes c
and
a\otimes b\otimes c\mapsto S(a)b\otimes c
to the second relation in (
9.19
) shows that
\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z^{\dagger}}}
is also a two-sided inverse
of
\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}
so that

(9.21)

\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}^{-1}=\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}=\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z^{\dagger}}}=\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z^{\dagger}}}^{-1}\;.

From this identity together with
(
5.31
), (
9.17
), and word independence one readily derives

(9.22)

S\hat{\otimes}S(\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet})\,=\,\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}^{-1}(\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet})\,.

It is useful to express (
9.19
) also as a relation of (co)multiplication coefficients.
Suppose
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
is a reduced word of maximal length.
The PBW theorems from Section
5
, the fact that
U_{q}^{+}
is an algebra over
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
, and
U_{q}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
a coalgebra over
\Lambda_{q}
then imply that there are elements

\mathbf{m}_{\chi}^{\psi,\phi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\in\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
and
\mathbf{d}^{\chi}_{\phi,\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\in\Lambda_{q}
with

\psi,\phi,\chi\in\mathbb{N}_{0}^{{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}}
such that

(9.23)

{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\phi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-2.10294pt}{\hskip-1.50209pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}=\sum_{\chi}\mathbf{m}_{\chi}^{\psi,\phi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\chi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-2.24924pt}{\hskip-1.60658pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\Delta({F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\chi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-2.24924pt}{\hskip-1.60658pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt})=\sum_{\phi,\psi}\mathbf{d}^{\chi}_{\phi,\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\cdot K^{-\vec{\psi}}{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\phi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-2.10294pt}{\hskip-1.50209pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\otimes{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\,.

The summations are over only finitely many elements in
\mathbb{N}_{0}^{{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}}
since they are subject to the grading constraint
\vec{\chi}=\vec{\phi}+\vec{\psi}
. It is clear that the only allowed terms for

\Delta({F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\chi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-2.24924pt}{\hskip-1.60658pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt})
are those appearing in the sum (
9.23
).
Linear independence of the elements
{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\phi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-2.10294pt}{\hskip-1.50209pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\otimes K^{-\vec{\psi}}{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\phi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-2.10294pt}{\hskip-1.50209pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\otimes{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}
now implies that equation (
9.19
)
is, indeed,
equivalent
to the condition that

(9.24)

\mathbf{c}_{\chi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu\mathbf{m}_{\chi}^{\psi,\phi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}=\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu\mathbf{c}_{\phi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu\mathbf{d}^{\chi}_{\phi,\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\qquad\mbox{for all}\;\chi,\phi,\psi\in\mathbb{N}_{0}^{{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}}\,.

An analogous equation of (co) multiplication coefficients, equivalent to
the second Tanisaki relation in (
9.19
), can be derived in the same manner.

9.4.
Maximal Hopf Ideals from Tanisaki-Lusztig Pairings

Yet another viewpoint of the same axioms in (
9.19
)
is derived from the pairings used in
[
47
,
71
]
. Fix some
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}\,
and observe that, by (
9.11
),
we may define a pairing of
U_{q}^{+}
with
U_{q}^{-}
over
\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}
as follows using PBW bases.

(9.25)

\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle_{z}:U_{q}^{-}\times U_{q}^{+}\rightarrow\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\qquad\mbox{with}\quad\langle{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt},{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\phi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-2.10294pt}{\hskip-1.50209pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\rangle_{z}\,=\,\delta_{\psi,\phi}\cdot\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(q)$}\mkern 1.6mu\,.

Note that (
9.25
) is dual to (
9.10
) in the sense that

\left(\langle{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt},\,\cdot\,\rangle_{z}\,\hat{\otimes}\,\mathrm{id}\right)(\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}})={F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\,
. Word independence and
linearity of this relation imply that
\left(\langle f,\,\cdot\,\rangle_{z}\otimes\mathrm{id}\right)(\mathcal{P}_{\mkern-4.0mu\bullet})=f
for all
f\in U_{q}^{-}\,
.
This, in turn, shows that the pairing in (
9.25
) is independent of
z
as well.

Define a linear isomorphims
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}_{R}:A^{\otimes 2}\rightarrow A^{\otimes 2}
by
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}_{R}(x\otimes y)=x\otimes K^{-\mu}y
, where
x
is homogeneous with
\mathbb{w}(x)=\mu
and
A
is any graded subalgebra that contains
U_{q}^{0}\,
. The form of the coproduct
in (
9.23
) now implies that we have a well-defined map

(9.26)

\hat{\Delta}=\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}_{R}\circ{\Delta\mkern-3.0mu}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}:U_{q}^{-}\rightarrow U_{q}^{-}\otimes U_{q}^{-}\;,

which is a homomorphism with respect to the braided product structure. The latter is given on homogeneous elements in
(U_{q}^{-})^{\otimes 2}
by

(x\otimes y)(x^{\prime}\otimes y^{\prime})=q^{-\mathchoice{\left(\mu|\nu\right)}{(\mu|\nu)}{(\mu|\nu)}{(\mu|\nu)}}xx^{\prime}\otimes yy^{\prime}\,
, where
\mu=\mathbb{w}(y)
and

\nu=\mathbb{w}(x^{\prime})
. One easily checks that
\hat{\Delta}
is coassociative.

In this language,
the first relation in (
9.2
) as well as the coefficient relation in (
9.24
)
are equivalent to the requirement that
\hat{\Delta}
is adjoint to the multiplication in
U_{q}^{+}
with respect to the pairing in
(
9.25
). That is,

(9.27)

\langle\hat{\Delta}(a),b\otimes c\rangle=\langle a,bc\rangle\quad\mbox{for all}\quad a\in U_{q}^{-}\quad\mbox{and}\quad b,c\in U_{q}^{+}\,.

As before, analogous statements
hold for the second Tanisaki relation.

Consider next the specialization to a primitive
\mathscr{k}
-th root of unity
\zeta\,
such that
\ell>\mathsf{e}\,
. As in (
6.9
), denote for
\mathsf{e}+1={\mathsf{e}^{*}}\leq m\leq\ell
the algebras

(9.28)

U_{\zeta,m}=U_{q}\otimes\Lambda_{\zeta,m}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad U_{\zeta,m}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}=U_{q}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\otimes\Lambda_{\zeta,m}\quad\mbox{if}\quad{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}\in\{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},+,-\}\,.

The form (
9.25
) clearly specializes to a form

\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle_{\zeta,m}:U_{\zeta,m}^{-}\times U_{\zeta,m}^{+}\rightarrow\Lambda_{\zeta,m}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\,
but will be degenerate.
Denote by
N_{\zeta,m}^{\pm}\subset U_{\zeta,m}^{\pm}
the respective null spaces.

Lemma 9.11
.

With notation as in (
6.72
) and (
6.65
) we have
N_{\zeta,m}^{\pm}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\pm}\otimes\Lambda_{\zeta,m}\,
. In particular,

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\pm}
is uniquely defined for all Lie types.

Proof.

Observe that, with the exponent set from (
6.64
),

\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(\zeta)$}\mkern 1.6mu=0\qquad\mbox{if and only if}\quad\psi\in[\mathfrak{l},\infty)^{\bullet}\,.

The claim is now immediate from the relation in (
6.65
).
∎

Recall from Section
6.5
the remaining ambiguity for the
\mathsf{G}_{2}
type, which
is resolved here via the word independence of the pairing. As before, we will suppress the
ground ring from our notation
N_{\zeta,m}^{\pm}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\pm}
whenever it is clear
from the context.

Proposition 9.12
.

The ideals
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\subset U_{\zeta,m}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
and
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\subset U_{\zeta,m}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
are Hopf ideals, independent of choices of reduced words of maximal length.

Proof.

The identity (
9.27
) implies that the left null space has to
be a co-ideal with respect to
\hat{\Delta}
. Together with Lemma
9.11
we thus
obtain

\hat{\Delta}(\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{-})\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{-}\otimes U_{\zeta,m}^{-}+U_{\zeta,m}^{-}\otimes\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{-}\;.

With
U_{\zeta,m}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}=U_{\zeta,m}^{0}\cdot U_{\zeta,m}^{-}
and
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}=U_{\zeta,m}^{0}\cdot\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{-}
it is easy to check that
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}_{R}
maps
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\otimes U_{\zeta,m}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
as well as

U_{\zeta,m}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\otimes\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
to itself.
The co-ideal equation for
\hat{\Delta}
and (
9.26
) now imply the respective co-ideal
condition for the regular coproduct with respect to
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\,
.
Word independence of
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(z)$}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\,
from Lemma
9.11
and
relation (
6.66
) now entails that
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
is invariant
under the antipode and, hence, a Hopf ideal.
Finally, recall that
\Omega(\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(z)$}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}})\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(z)$}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
,

\Omega(U_{\zeta,m}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}})\subseteq U_{\zeta,m}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
,
\Omega^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta=\Delta^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}{\scalebox{.52}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{opp}$}}}\circ\Omega
, and
\Omega\circ S=S\circ\Omega
.
From these relations
one readily derives that
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
is also a Hopf ideal.
∎

We may consider now the full maxiaml ideal
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}=(\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}+\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\bullet}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}})\cdot U_{\zeta,m}

for the full algebra
U_{\zeta,m}
over
\Lambda_{\zeta,m}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\,
, which has all desired properties.

Corollary 9.13
.

Suppose
{\mathsf{e}^{*}}\leq m\leq\ell
.

i)

For any Lie type and root of unity with
\mathscr{k}
as in (
6.1
),

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
is a Hopf ideal in
U_{\zeta,m}
.

ii)

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
is equal to the ideal generated by
the set
\bigl\{X_{w},\,Y_{w^{\prime}}:\;\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$}\neq w\leq_{R}z,\,\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$}\neq w^{\prime}\leq_{R}z^{\prime}\bigr\}

for any choice of
z,z^{\prime}\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}\,
.

iii)

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
is stable under all automorphisms
discussed in Section
4
.

Proof.

The first part is immediate from
Proposition
9.12
. Invariance under the
automorphisms
\Omega
,
\mho
, and
S
follows from (
6.66
)
and word independence. Gradings and identities, such as (
5.15
) and
\Pi=\Upsilon\circ\Omega
, imply invariance for all others in Section
4.2
.

For the Artin generators
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
we may repeat the proof of Theorem
6.22
nearly verbatim. Specifically, for the choice of
w
therein, it is shown that for all
v\leq_{R}w
the element
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(X_{v})
is again some power generator and, hence, in
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}

by word independence.
∎

Thus, if we define the
restricted quantum groups
by the quotient

(9.29)

U_{\zeta,m}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}=U_{\zeta,m}/\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}\,,

then Corollary
9.13
implies that
U_{\zeta,m}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}
is indeed a Hopf algebra, which is independent of any choices made in its definition. The construction of a full
poset of ideals under
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
and respective quasi-
R
-matrices will be addressed in
the next sections with different techniques.

9.5.
Truncated Quasi-
R
-Matrices and Coproduct Formulas

In this section we develop a calculus of quasi-
R
-matrices at roots of unity analogous to the
one in Section
9.2
. To avoid singularities, the summations defining these

R
-matrices need to be truncated so that the corresponding identities hold only up to certain ideals.

It is, therefore, useful to
extend the ideals in
U_{\zeta}^{\pm}
defined (
6.65
) to the full algebra
U_{\zeta,m}
over
\Lambda_{\zeta,m}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
for a
given primitive
\mathscr{k}
-th root of unity
\zeta
and
{\mathsf{e}^{*}}\leq m\leq\ell\,
. For any pair of reduced words
u,w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}\,
, we write

(9.30)

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,w)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}=(\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u)$}}^{+}+\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{-})\cdot U_{\zeta,m}=\mathcal{K}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,w)$}}\cdot U_{\zeta,m}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$})$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}+\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$},w)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}\,,

which may, alternatively, be viewed as the two-sided ideal in
U_{\zeta,m}
generated by the set
\{X_{a},Y_{b}\,:\,\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$}\neq a,b\leq_{R}u\}\,
. Correspondingly, for reduced words
a,b\in\mathscr{W}^{*}\,
for which
a\cdot b
is also reduced, we infer that, for any Lie type,

(9.31)

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(a\cdot b,\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$})$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(a,\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$})$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}+\mathit{\Gamma}_{a}\bigl(\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(b,\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$})$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}\bigr)\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\Omega\bigl(\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(a,\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$})$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}\bigr)=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$},a)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}\,

hold as well as the respective identities with flipped arguments and summations over ideals. A useful symmetry for
various tensor identities is

(9.32)

\Omega^{\#}=(1\,2)\circ\Omega^{\otimes 2}:\,U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\otimes 2}\rightarrow U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\otimes 2}\,:\quad x\otimes y\mapsto\Omega^{\#}(x\otimes y)=\Omega(y)\otimes\Omega(x)\,,

which is an anti-linear anti-involution by the properties in (
4.10
).

To ensure minimal truncations, we consider
R
-matrices defined over the maximal ground rings
\Lambda_{\zeta,\ell}
or

\Lambda_{\zeta,\ell}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
, observing that
[s]!_{\alpha}\neq 0
whenever
s<\ell_{\alpha}\,
. We begin with the definition
of the
simple truncated
quasi-
R
-matrix associated to a given
\alpha_{i}\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}
,

(9.33)

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\,=\,\sum_{s=0}^{{\ell_{i}}-1}\dfrac{\zeta_{i}^{s(s-1)/2}}{[s]!_{i}}(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})^{s}\cdot E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s}\qquad\in\;U_{\zeta,\ell}^{+}\otimes U_{\zeta,\ell}^{-}\,,

which is well-defined over
\Lambda_{\zeta,\ell}\,
. Analogous to the generic case we, further, denote the conjugate
R
-matrix as

(9.34)

\displaystyle\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\,=\,\Omega^{\#}(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i})\,=\,\sum_{s=0}^{{\ell_{i}}-1}\dfrac{\zeta_{i}^{-s(s-1)/2}}{[s]!_{i}}(-1)^{s}(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})^{s}\cdot E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s}\qquad\in\;U_{\zeta,\ell}^{+}\otimes U_{\zeta,\ell}^{-}\,,

where
\Omega^{\#}
is as in (
9.32
). To express these as inverses, we introduce for any

w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
the ideals

(9.35)

{\mathcal{N}\mkern-5.0mu}_{\circ}(w)=(\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{+}\otimes\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{-})\otimes\Lambda_{\zeta,\ell}=(\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w,\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$})$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}}\otimes\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$},w)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}})\cap(U_{\zeta,\ell}^{+}\otimes U_{\zeta,\ell}^{-})\,,

generated by all
X_{a}\otimes Y_{b}
with
\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$}\neq a,b\leq_{R}w\,
.
In calculations throughout this
section, we also employ the standard notation
x\equiv y\mod V
to mean

x-y\in V\,
for a given submodule
V
.

Lemma 9.14

(
cf.

[
59
, Lemma A.1]
)
.

For all
\alpha_{i}\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}
we have

\displaystyle\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\,\equiv\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\,\equiv\,1\otimes 1\quad\mod\,{\mathcal{N}\mkern-5.0mu}_{\circ}(w_{i})\,.

Proof.

We start with a direct computation and resummation.

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}

\displaystyle=\sum_{r,n=0}^{{\ell_{i}}-1}\dfrac{\zeta_{i}^{r(r-1)/2-n(n-1)/2}}{[r]!_{i}[n]!_{i}}(-1)^{n}(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})^{r+n}E_{i}^{r+n}\otimes F_{i}^{r+n}

\displaystyle=\sum_{k=0}^{2{\ell_{i}}-2}\rho_{k}\cdot\zeta_{i}^{-k(k-1)/2}(-1)^{k}(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})^{k}E_{i}^{k}\otimes F_{i}^{k}\;,

where

\displaystyle\qquad\rho_{k}=\sum_{r=\max(0,k-({\ell_{i}}-1))}^{\min(k,{\ell_{i}}-1)}\dfrac{1}{[r]!_{i}[k-r]!_{i}}(-1)^{r}\zeta_{i}^{r(k-1)}\;.

For
0<k<\ell_{i}
, we compute

\displaystyle\rho_{k}

\displaystyle=\sum_{r=0}^{k}\dfrac{1}{[r]!_{i}[k-r]!_{i}}(-1)^{r}\zeta_{i}^{r(k-1)}\quad=\dfrac{1}{[k]!}\sum_{r=0}^{k}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$k$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
r\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}_{i}(-1)^{r}\zeta_{i}^{r(k-1)}

\displaystyle=\dfrac{1}{[k]!}\prod_{t=1}^{k}(-\zeta_{i}^{2(t-1)}+1)\quad=0\,,

where we used (
3.4
) with substitutions
a\mapsto k
,
k\mapsto r
,
q\mapsto\zeta_{i}^{-1}
, and
z\mapsto-\zeta_{i}^{-2}\,
. Observing that
\rho_{0}=1
,
X_{i}=E_{i}^{\ell_{i}}
, and
Y_{i}=F_{i}^{\ell_{i}}
we now find

(9.36)

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}=1\otimes 1\,+\,(X_{i}\otimes Y_{i})\sum_{k=\ell_{i}}^{2{\ell_{i}}-2}\rho_{k}\cdot\zeta_{i}^{-k(k-1)/2}(-1)^{k}(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})^{k}E_{i}^{k-\ell_{i}}\otimes F_{i}^{k-\ell_{i}}\,,

for which the latter term is clearly in
{\mathcal{N}\mkern-5.0mu}_{\circ}(w_{i})\,
. The verification for

\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}
is nearly identical.
∎

Analogous to the generic case and using definitions from (
5.11
), we now define the
elementary
truncated quasi-
R
-matrices associated to a reduced word
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
as

(9.37)

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w}

\displaystyle=\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w^{\flat}}\left(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\tau(w)}\right)=\sum_{s=0}^{\ell_{w}-1}\dfrac{\zeta^{s(s-1)/2}_{w}}{[s]!_{w}}(\zeta_{w}-\zeta^{-1}_{w})^{s}E_{w}^{s}\otimes F_{w}^{s}\,

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{23.90028pt}\mbox{and}

\displaystyle\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w}

\displaystyle=\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w^{\flat}}\left(\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\tau(w)}\right)=\sum_{s=0}^{\ell_{w}-1}\dfrac{\zeta^{-s(s-1)/2}_{w}}{[s]!_{w}}(-1)^{s}(\zeta_{w}-\zeta^{-1}_{w})^{s}E_{w}^{s}\otimes F_{w}^{s}\,,

with notations as in (
2.8
) and
\zeta_{w}=\zeta_{\tau(w)}=\zeta_{\gamma(w)}\,
.
The following assertion is readily derived by applying
\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w^{\flat}}
to (
9.36
) with
i=\tau(w)\,
, resulting in the same equation with
i
replaced by
w\,
.

Corollary 9.15
.

For all
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
we have

\displaystyle\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w}\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w}\,\equiv\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w}\cdot\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w}\,\equiv\,1\otimes 1\quad\mod\,{\mathcal{N}\mkern-5.0mu}_{\circ}(w)\,.

We define, similarly, the
partial
truncated quasi-
R
-matrices associated to some
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
as

(9.38)

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}=\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w^{L}}\ldots\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w^{1}}

\displaystyle=\sum_{\psi\in[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s}}\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(\zeta)$}\mkern 1.6mu^{-1}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}\otimes{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}w$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-26.7191pt}{\hskip-16.46146pt}{\hskip-11.75818pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 26.7191pt}\,

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{19.91692pt}\mbox{and}
