\displaystyle\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}=\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w^{1}}\ldots\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w^{L}}

\displaystyle=\sum_{\psi\in[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s}}\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(\zeta^{-1})$}\mkern 1.6mu^{-1}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\otimes{F}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-25.90247pt}{\hskip-15.8898pt}{\hskip-11.34987pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 25.90247pt}\;,

with notation as in (
9.10
),
L=l(w)\,
, and
[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s}=[0,\mathfrak{l})_{\bullet}\cap\mathcal{E}(s)
as in (
6.37
).
The identities below, with
a,b\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
such that
a\cdot b
is reduced, are straightforward from Corollary
9.15
, the mentioned properties of
\Omega^{\#}
, and (
5.26
).

(9.39)

\displaystyle\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}

\displaystyle=\Omega^{\#}(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}})

\displaystyle\qquad\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}

\displaystyle\equiv 1^{\otimes 2}\equiv\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\mod{\mathcal{N}\mkern-5.0mu}_{\circ}(w)

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{17.07164pt}\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{a\cdot b}}

\displaystyle=\mathit{\Gamma}_{a}^{\otimes 2}(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{b}})\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{a}}

\displaystyle\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{a\cdot b}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}

\displaystyle=\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{a}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{a}^{\otimes 2}(\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{b}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}})\,

The relevant ideals for the intertwining relations of the truncated
R
-matrices are
given for each
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
as

(9.40)

{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w,\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$})$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}}\otimes U_{\zeta,\ell}+U_{\zeta,\ell}\otimes\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$},w)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}}\,,

which is the ideal in
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\otimes 2}
generated by all
X_{a}\otimes 1
and
1\otimes Y_{b}
with
\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$}\neq a,b\leq_{R}w\,
. Assuming
w\cdot u
is reduced for
w,u\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
, one easily verifies the identities

(9.41)

{\mathcal{N}\mkern-5.0mu}_{\circ}(w)\subset{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)\,,\quad{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w\cdot u)=\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}^{\otimes 2}\bigl({\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(u)\bigr)+{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)\,,\quad\mbox{and}\quad\Omega^{\#}({\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w))={\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)\,.

The truncated analog of Proposition
9.7
for a simple reflection
w_{i}
and simple generators is now stated as follows.

Lemma 9.16
.

Let

\mathsf{\Phi}

be of any Lie type and
1\leq i,j\leq n
. Then

(9.42)

\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(E_{j})\,\equiv\,\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{i}\circ\Delta(E_{j})\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\qquad\mod{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})\,.

The proof of this lemma is provided in Appendix
A
by explicit computations of both sides of (
9.42
), depending on the Cartan matrix entries

A_{ij}
and
A_{ji}
. The properties of automorphisms and ideals developed thus far allow us to extend this identity
to all words and generators.

Proposition 9.17
.

Let

\mathsf{\Phi}

be of any Lie type,
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
, and
x\in U_{\zeta,\ell}
. Then

\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}(x)\,\equiv\,\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}\circ\Delta(x)\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\qquad\mod{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)\,.

Proof.

We start with the case
w=w_{i}
for which
\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
and
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w_{i}}}=\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\,
. Denote the quotient algebra

\mathbf{U}(w)=U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\otimes 2}/{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)
and note that by Corollary
9.15
and
(
9.41
) the images of
\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}
and
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}
in
\mathbf{U}(w_{i})
are inverse to each other. The maps from
U_{\zeta,\ell}
to
\mathbf{U}(w_{i})
given by
x\mapsto[\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(x)]
and

x\mapsto[\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{i}\circ\Delta(x)\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}]
are thus algebra homomorphisms.
Since, by Proposition
9.16
, they coincide on generators, they have to be equal
on all of
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{+}\,
.

Note next that
\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
and
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta
coincide on any
K^{\nu}
and, further, that
K^{\nu}\otimes K^{\nu}
commutes with
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}
. This implies that the
two homomorphisms also coincide on
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{0}
and, hence, that the identity above
holds for
x\in U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
and
w=w_{i}\,
.

Recall that, with
\Omega^{\#}
as in (
9.32
),
\Omega^{\#}(\Delta(x))=\Delta(\Omega(x))
and
\Omega^{\#}
commutes with
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\otimes 2}
. It readily follows from the fact that
\Omega^{\#}
is an anti-linear anti-involution,
(
4.10
), and (
9.34
)
that
\Omega^{\#}(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i})=\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\,
. Applying
\Omega^{\#}
to the identity in Proposition
9.16

for some
x\in U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\,
, these observations now imply the same relation for
\Omega(x)\in U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\,
, using also that
{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)
is
\Omega^{\#}
-invariant by (
9.41
). Hence, the relation holds for any
x\in U_{\zeta,\ell}\,
, completing the
proof for
w=w_{i}\,
.

The extension to general words is similar to the one in Corollary
9.15
. We proceed by induction on
L=l(w)
, starting from the base case already proven above. For a reduced word
u\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
let
w=u^{\flat}

and
i=\tau(u)
so that
l(u)>l(w)
. Assuming the assertion for
w
, we first observe

\displaystyle\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{u}\left(x\right)\,=\,\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}\left(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(x)\right)\,\equiv\,\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta\left(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(x)\right)\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\qquad\mod{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)\,.

Applying the relation for
w_{i}
to the
\Delta(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(x))
term, we find

\displaystyle\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{u}\left(x\right)

\displaystyle\,\in\,\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}^{\otimes 2}\left(\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\otimes 2}(\Delta(x))\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}+{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})\right)\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\,+\,{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{17.07164pt}\subseteq\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}^{\otimes 2}(\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w_{i}})\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w\cdot w_{i}}(\Delta(x))\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}^{\otimes 2}(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!w_{i}})\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\,+\,\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}^{\otimes 2}\left({\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})\right)\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\,+\,{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{17.07164pt}\subseteq\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w\cdot w_{i}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w\cdot w_{i}}(\Delta(x))\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w\cdot w_{i}}}\,+\,\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}^{\otimes 2}\left({\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})\right)\,+\,{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{17.07164pt}=\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{u}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{u}(\Delta(x))\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{u}}\,+\,{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(u)\,.

The step from the second to the third line uses (
9.39
) for the first term and the fact
that
\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}^{\otimes 2}\left({\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})\right)
is itself a two-sided ideal for the second term.
The last step uses the iteration of ideals from (
9.41
) and
u=w\cdot w_{i}\,
. Taking the
inclusion modulo
{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(u)
yields the claim.
∎

Recall from the proof of Lemma
9.8
that

\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta(x)=\mathit{\Gamma}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}^{\otimes 2}\bigl(\Delta\bigl(\mathit{\Gamma}_{{s\mkern-1.0mu_{\bullet}}}^{-1}(x)\bigr)\bigr)
for the
twisted coproduct defined in (
9.14
). The relation clearly descends to
U_{\zeta,\ell}
.
Applying, Proposition
9.17
to a reduced word of maximal length now yields the following analog
of Lemma
9.8
.

Corollary 9.18
.

Suppose
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
and
x\in U_{\zeta,\ell}\,
. Then

\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta(x)\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\,\equiv\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\cdot\Delta(x)\qquad\mod{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(z)\,.

The iteration of the coproduct with truncated quasi-
R
-matrices provided in the above proposition allows us
to establish further Hopf ideals. It is immediate from the form in (
9.40
) that

(9.43)

{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(u)\,\subseteq\,{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(u)=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}}\otimes U_{\zeta,\ell}\,+\,U_{\zeta,\ell}\otimes\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}}\,,

which suggests that we first consider these diagonal ideals.

Proposition 9.19
.

For every
u\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
the ideal
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}
is a Hopf ideal in
U_{\zeta,m}\,
.

Proof.

We start by showing that the
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}}
are bi-ideals.
Given their definition, this means verifying that
\Delta(X_{v}),\Delta(Y_{v})\in{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(u)

for all
\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$}\neq v\leq_{R}w\,
. Since
{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(v)\subseteq{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(u)
and
using
\Omega
-symmetry as before, it suffices to check

\Delta(X_{v})\in{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(v)
for any reduced word
v
. Setting
w=v^{\flat}
and
i=\tau(v)

and using (
7.6
) we first observe that

\displaystyle\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}\circ\Delta(X_{i})

\displaystyle=\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}(X_{i}\otimes L_{i}+1\otimes X_{i})=X_{w\cdot w_{i}}\otimes L_{w\cdot w_{i}}+1\otimes X_{w\cdot w_{i}}

\displaystyle=X_{v}\otimes L_{v}+1\otimes X_{v}\;\in\;{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(v)\;.

Using this, Proposition
9.17
, the coproduct from (
7.6
), the fact that

{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(v)
is a two-sided ideal in
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\otimes 2}\,
, and
{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)\subseteq{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(v)

we compute

\displaystyle\Delta(X_{v})

\displaystyle\;=\;\Delta(X_{w\cdot w_{i}})\;=\;\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{w}(X_{i})\;\in\;\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{w}\circ\Delta(X_{i})\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\,+\,{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)

\displaystyle\subseteq\;\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{w}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\left({\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(v)\right)\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\,+\,{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w)\;\subseteq\;{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(v)\,,

so that
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}}
is indeed a bi-ideal.

We now invoke a result of Nichols, which states that any bi-ideal in a pointed Hopf algebra is necessarily a Hopf ideal. See
[
56
, Thm 1(v)]
. By Proposition
3.1
,
U_{q,\mathbb{k}}\cong U_{\zeta,\mathbb{Q}}=U_{\zeta,\ell}\otimes\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)
is pointed for
\mathbb{k}=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)
via the obvious map
\vartheta:\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}\rightarrow\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)\,
.
Since
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\mathbb{Q}$}}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}}\otimes\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)
is a bi-ideal, Nicols’s result
implies that

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\mathbb{Q}$}}
is indeed a Hopf ideal, meaning it is preserved under the antipode
S
.

Finally, by (
6.65
) and (
9.30
), the ideals
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,v)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}
are the
free
\Lambda_{\zeta,m}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
-submodules spanned by a subset of elements of a PBW basis of
U_{\zeta,m}\,
, implying

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,v)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,v)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\mathbb{Q}$}}\cap U_{\zeta,m}\,
. Since the intersection
of a Hopf subalgebra and Hopf ideal is again a Hopf ideal, we arrive at the claim for
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}\,
.
∎

We next seek to extend the observation above to the related families of ideals defined in previous sections.
The two-sided ideals
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{+}
defined in (
6.65
) are not
Hopf ideals since
U_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{+}
is not a bialgebra, nor are they even Hopf subalgebras. We, thus, consider the extension
to the Hopf algebra
U_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
by including the Cartan generators, and defining

(9.44)

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{+}\cdot U_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\qquad\mbox{with \ $\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}$-basis}\qquad\bigl\{b\cdot K^{\nu}\,|\,\nu\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}},\,b\in{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{B}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\iota^{*}([\mathfrak{l},\infty)^{s}),+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-38.43338pt}{\hskip-38.43338pt}{\hskip-24.43651pt}{\hskip-19.09929pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle z\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-24.03674pt}{\hskip-14.74419pt}{\hskip-10.53159pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 36.10007pt}\bigr\}\,.

Here,
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
with
w\leq_{R}z
,
s=\mathscr{r}(w)
, and
\iota:\mkern 0.4mu\boldsymbol{\mathscr{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(s)\hookrightarrow{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\,
. The definition of
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is analogous and the

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,v)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}
are obtained from the
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}},{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
in the same way as in
(
9.30
).

The statement in Item
i)
in Theorem
9.20
already follows,
independently, from
the results in Sections
7
and
8
for the respective
Lie types
\mathsf{A}_{n}
and
\mathsf{B}_{2}
, where the ideals are explicitly identified with vanishing ideals
of Bruhat subgroups.

Word independence, asserted in Item
iii)
,
is already implied by Theorem
6.19
for Lie types different from
\mathsf{G}_{2}
.
The use of Nicols’s result for Hopf ideals in Proposition
9.19
allows
us to extend word independence also to the
\mathsf{G}_{2}
case for the ideals in the full algebras.

Theorem 9.20
.

Suppose

\mathsf{\Phi}

is of any Lie type and
{\mathsf{e}^{*}}\leq m\leq\ell
. Assume further

u,v,u^{\prime},v^{\prime}\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
are reduced words with
s=\mathscr{r}(u)=\mathscr{r}(u^{\prime})
and
t=\mathscr{r}(v)=\mathscr{r}(v^{\prime})
.

i)

The ideals
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
and
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
are Hopf ideals
in
U_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
and
U_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
, respectively.

ii)

The ideal
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,v)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}
is a Hopf ideal in
U_{\zeta,m}
.

iii)

The ideals depend only on the elements represented in
\mathscr{W}
.

That is,
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u^{\prime})$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
,
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u^{\prime})$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
, and
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,v)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}
.

Proof.

The same reasoning as in the proof of Proposition
9.19

applies to show that
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u)$}}^{{}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$m$}}\cap U_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}\,
, by restricting
both the basis elements defined with respect to
u
to those in
(
9.44
)
and reducing the ground ring to
\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}\,
.
As before, since
U_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
is a Hopf subalgebra it follows from
Proposition
9.19
that
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is a Hopf ideal.
The argument for
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\leq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is identical, and the assertion in Item

ii)
is now immediate from the definition in (
9.30
).

The statement in Item
i)
implies, in particular, that for any
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
,

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
is invariant under the antipode. The formulae in (
4.16
)
and the fact that the
\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
Ch}^{\mathsfit h}_{u}
preserves any subspace of
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}
with a

\mathbb{w}
-graded decomposition implies that
\mho
maps
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
to itself. The
decomposition into a positive and Cartan part now implies
\mho(\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{+})=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{+}\,
.

Relation (
6.65
) shows that word independence of
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{+}
is
implied by word independence of

{\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu

\scriptstyle[\mathfrak{l},\infty)^{s},+\hskip-3.01389pt
\scriptstyle w\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}
. To prove the latter we
first oberve that
V^{[s]}=[0,\mathfrak{l})_{s}
is of the split form (
5.65
) with

V_{d}=\{0,1,\ldots,\ell_{d}-1\}\,
. The exponent set
\bar{V}^{]s[}=[\mathfrak{l},\infty)^{s}
is
defined as the complement and thus of the required in the case
ii)

of Corollary
5.15
.

As in the remark following (
6.65
), we have

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})$}}^{+}\,=\,{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle[\mathfrak{l},\infty)^{\bullet},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-26.42697pt}{\hskip-26.42697pt}{\hskip-16.7505pt}{\hskip-12.99767pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}\!=\,{\scalebox{.96}{${\mathfrak{S}}\mkern-1.0mu$}}\mkern 1.5mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\bar{V}^{]ij[},+\hskip-3.01389pt$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-16.43097pt}{\hskip-16.43097pt}{\hskip-12.53777pt}{\hskip-11.89607pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-118.74823pt}{\hskip-72.30884pt}{\hskip-52.2747pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 118.74823pt}
in
{U}_{\ \mkern-9.0mu\zeta}\mkern-1.5mu\raise 0.80002pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle(ij)$}^{+}\,
. By the previous argument we have that
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}})$}}^{+}
is stable under

\mho
so that the second assumption of Corollary
5.15
is also fulfilled.
It follows that that
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w)$}}^{+}
is independent of the choice of
w
. The
respective statements for the other ideals are now immediate from the identities in
(
9.30
) and (
9.44
).
∎

Theorem
9.20
implies, in particular, that the ideals
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.97}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.6mu\raise 0.49164pt\hbox{\scalebox{.7}{$\circ$}}}
,
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\raise 0.49164pt\hbox{\scalebox{.7}{$\circ$}}\mkern-1.6mu\scalebox{.97}{$\bullet$}}
, and
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
defined in (
6.72
) are indeed independent of choices of maximal reduced words as well, including the
\mathsf{G}_{2}
case.

The intertwining relations derived above may also be understood in terms of partial Hopf algebra quotients. For any
s\in\mathscr{W}
and
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
with
s=\mathscr{r}(w)

define

(9.45)

\Delta^{s}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}^{-1}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad U_{\zeta,\ell}^{[s]}=U_{\zeta,\ell}/\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(w,w)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}}\,.

As with any automorphism, the conjugate
\Delta^{s}
defines an alternative Hopf algebra structure
with antipode
S^{\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}}\,
. Theorem
9.20
implies that
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{[s]}
is a Hopf algebra defined independent of the choice of the presentation
w
of
s
.

Proposition 9.21
.

Suppose
t=\mathscr{r}(u)
as above and
t\leq_{R}s
for
s\in\mathscr{W}
. Let
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{u}}=[\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{u}}]
be the image of the partial quasi-
R
-matrix in
(U_{\zeta,\ell}^{[s]})^{\otimes 2}
.
Then
\Delta^{t}
descends to a coproduct
\Delta^{[t]}
on
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{[s]}
,
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{u}}
is invertible, and

\Delta^{[t]}(x)\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{u}}\,=\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{u}}\cdot\Delta(x)\qquad\mbox{for all }x\in U_{\zeta,\ell}^{[s]}\,.

Proof.

Recall first from (
9.41
) and (
9.43
) that

{\mathcal{N}\mkern-5.0mu}_{\circ}(u)\subset{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(u)\subset{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(u)={\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(t)\subseteq{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(s)
. Thus,
equations in Corollary
9.15
and Proposition
9.17
also hold modulo

{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(t)
. The former shows that
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}
is invertible. The latter can be rewritten
as

\Delta^{t}(x)\,\equiv\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{u}}\cdot\Delta(x)\cdot\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!{u}\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 2.0mu\blacktriangleright\mkern 1.0mu$}}}\qquad\mod{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(s).

If
x\in\widehat{\mathcal{K}}\raise 0.7pt\hbox{\scalebox{.82}{$(u,u)$}}_{\scalebox{.62}{$\ell$}}
, Proposition
9.19
implies that

\Delta(x)\in{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(s)
. Thus, the right-hand side and, hence, also
\Delta^{t}(x)
is in
{\mathcal{N}\!}_{*}\mkern-1.0mu(s)
. It follows that
\Delta^{t}
descends to a coproduct
\Delta^{[t]}
on
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{[s]}
for which the claimed identity now clearly holds.
∎

It is important to keep in mind, though, that the automorphisms
\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}
themselves generally do not factor through these Hopf algebra quotients.

9.6.
Quasi-
R
-Matrices for Restricted Quantum Algebras

In this section, we return to the maximal ideal case and collect previous observations for the construction of unique quasi-
R
-matrices for the restricted quantum algebras. The defining relations in tensor products of
U_{\zeta,\ell}
will
generally hold only up to ideals, which we introduce first. For
a\in\mathbb{N}
,
let
{\mathcal{N}}^{\,a}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
be the ideal in
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\otimes a}
generated
by all elements
1^{\otimes(j-1)}\otimes X_{v}\otimes 1^{\otimes(a-j)}
and

1^{\otimes(j-1)}\otimes Y_{v}\otimes 1^{\otimes(a-j)}
for all
\scalebox{.9}{$\emptyset$}\neq v\leq_{R}z
and
j=1,\ldots,a
for some
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
. Theorem
9.20
implies
the word independent presentation

(9.46)

{\mathcal{N}}^{\,a}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}=\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}\otimes U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\otimes(a-1)}+U_{\zeta,\ell}\otimes\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}\otimes U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\otimes(a-2)}+\ldots+U_{\zeta,\ell}^{\otimes(a-1)}\otimes\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}\,,

where
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
is as in (
6.72
). Since, for example,

{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(z)\subseteq{\mathcal{N}}^{\,2}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
, Corollary
9.18
implies

(9.47)

\raise 7.20001pt\hbox{\rule{5.12149pt}{0.76823pt}}\mkern-10.6mu\Delta(x)\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\,\equiv\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\cdot\Delta(x)\qquad\mod{\mathcal{N}}^{\,2}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}\,,

for any
x\in U_{\zeta,\ell}
and
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}
as in (
9.37
). The remainders in these ideals have been explicitly computed
in Appendix
A
. Likewise, the Drinfeld-Tanisaki relations from (
9.2
) hold for the truncated
R
-matrices also only up to remainder terms in these ideals. For example, in the rank one case with

we have

\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}_{12}(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{13})\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{12}\,-\,(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}})=(X\otimes 1\otimes 1)\cdot\mathop{\textnormal{\hbox{\hbox to15.83pt{\vbox to16.44pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 0.0pt\lower-10.00012pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\hbox to0.0pt{{}{}{}{}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@discardpath@clipped{M 0 -13.84 L 0 8.92 L 21.9 8.92 L 21.9 -13.84 Z} {{{}{}{{}}{}

Proposition 9.22
.

For a given maximal reduced word
\,z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}\,
and any Lie type denote
\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}=\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\,
.

Then

\displaystyle(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}})

\displaystyle\equiv\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}_{12}(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{13})\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{12}\quad\mod{\mathcal{N}}^{\,3}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}

and

\displaystyle(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}})

\displaystyle\equiv\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}_{23}(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{13})\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{23}\quad\mod{\mathcal{N}}^{\,3}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}\,.

Proof.

The first identity is straightforwardly verified by juxtaposing the explicit expressions for both sides using the expressions in (
9.38
)
and (
9.23
), all of which specialize to
q\mapsto\zeta
.
