\phi,\psi\in[0,\mathfrak{l})_{\bullet}\end{subarray}}\mathbf{c}_{\phi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(\zeta)$}\mkern 1.6mu^{-1}\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(\zeta)$}\mkern 1.6mu^{-1}\mathbf{m}_{\chi}^{\phi,\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(\zeta)$}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\chi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-3.82988pt}{\hskip-2.24924pt}{\hskip-1.60658pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\otimes K^{-\vec{\psi}}{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\phi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-3.64168pt}{\hskip-2.10294pt}{\hskip-1.50209pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\otimes{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}

Recall here that
\mathbf{c}_{\phi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(\zeta)$}\mkern 1.6mu\neq 0
iff
\phi\in[0,\mathfrak{l})_{\bullet}\,
and observe that
(
9.24
) has a well-defined specialization of
q
to
\zeta
. We infer from this that
for terms for which all three exponents
\chi
,
\phi
, and
\psi
are in
[0,\mathfrak{l})_{\bullet}

the respective coefficients indeed coincide. The difference between the
equations above is, thus, a sum of terms, each of which has at least one exponent in the complement

[\mathfrak{l},\infty)^{\bullet}
. The monomial element associated to this exponent is then, by Corollary
9.13
, in
\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
so that the full tensor term is in

{\mathcal{N}}^{\,3}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
.

This implies the first congruence above. The second identity follows analogously. An alternative argument can be designed by immediately passing to the quotient
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}
from (
9.29
) and observing that the pairing from (
9.25
) factors into a non-degenerate pairing between
the positive and negative parts of
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}
upon the specialization
q\mapsto\zeta
.
The image of

\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}
in
(U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}})^{\otimes 2}
is then the element dual to this form. The duality
relation (
9.27
) also factors into the form on
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}
and is equivalent
to the Tanisaki relation on
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}
.
∎

Indeed, combining Proposition
9.22
and (
9.47
) implies that, for any maximal reduced word

z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
, the triple
\,(U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}},[\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}],\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L})\,
is a pre-triangular Hopf algebra
in the sense of (
9.3
), where
[\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}]
denotes the image of
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}
in

(U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}})^{\otimes 2}\,
. The remaining question is the word independence of

[\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}]
or
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}
modulo
{\mathcal{N}}^{\,2}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}\,
.

At this point, we have the tools to prove this claim in several different ways. One is to reconsider the
pairing from (
9.25
), which is independent of a choice of
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
over

\Lambda_{q,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
and, thus, also over
\Lambda_{\zeta,{\mathsf{e}^{*}}}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.87694pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
as a non-degenerate pairing of the positive and
negative parts of
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}
. Since the element
[\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}]
is dual to this pairing it is also word independent. A second approach is to adapt the uniqueness proof of
[
47
, Thm.4.1.2(a)]

to
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}
and use it directly to show the analog for Corollary
9.9

for
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}
. We offer here a third option that exhibits further symmetries of
the quasi-
R
-matrices.

Lemma 9.23
.

Suppose
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
. Then
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z^{\dagger}}}=\mho\otimes\mho(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}})\equiv\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\mod{\mathcal{N}}^{\,2}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
.

Proof.

Clearly, the automorphisms

L
,
S
, and
\mho
preserve the maximal ideals and are, hence, well-defined on
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}\,
. The Tanisaki relations from Proposition
9.22
, therefore, hold as equalities in the restricted quantum group for the image
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{z}=[\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}]\in(U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}})^{\otimes 2}
. There, we may now repeat the arguments in
(
9.20
) to show that
\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{z}=[\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}]
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{z^{\dagger}}
are both
two-sided inverses of
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{z}
, where
\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}
denotes the truncated version of the element from
(
9.20
).

Setting
{\mathbf{f}}(\mu)=(-1)^{0pt(\mu)}\zeta^{-\frac{1}{2}(\mathchoice{\left(\mu|\mu\right)}{(\mu|\mu)}{(\mu|\mu)}{(\mu|\mu)}-2\mathchoice{\left(\rho|\mu\right)}{(\rho|\mu)}{(\rho|\mu)}{(\rho|\mu)}}
for
\mu\in\mathbb{Z}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
, we may re-express the implied equality
\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{z}=\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}_{z^{\dagger}}

as the following congruence,

\sum_{\psi\in[0,\mathfrak{l})_{\bullet}}{\mathbf{f}}(\vec{\psi})\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(\zeta)$}\mkern 1.6mu^{-1}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\otimes{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z^{\dagger}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-27.53116pt}{\hskip-27.53116pt}{\hskip-17.3714pt}{\hskip-12.99545pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 27.53116pt}=\sum_{\psi\in[0,\mathfrak{l})_{\bullet}}{\mathbf{f}}(\vec{\psi})\mathbf{c}_{\psi}\mkern-0.7mu\scalebox{.83}{$(\zeta)$}\mkern 1.6mu^{-1}\cdot{E}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z^{\dagger}$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-27.53116pt}{\hskip-27.53116pt}{\hskip-17.3714pt}{\hskip-12.99545pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 27.53116pt}\otimes{F}\mkern 1.3mu\raisebox{5.5pt}{$\scriptstyle\psi$}\mkern-2.8mu{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-4.12505pt}{\hskip-2.37517pt}{\hskip-1.69653pt}}\raisebox{-2.7pt}{$\scriptstyle\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}z$}{\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-24.85338pt}{\hskip-15.31584pt}{\hskip-10.9399pt}}{\scriptstyle\hskip 24.85338pt}\quad\mod{\mathcal{N}}^{\,2}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}\,.

Applying to this the map
x\otimes y\mapsto{\mathbf{f}}(\mu)^{-1}x\otimes y
for
\mathbb{w}(x)=\mu
as well
as
\mho\otimes\mathrm{id}
, yields the claimed identity.
∎

Corollary 9.24
.

The element
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}}=[\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}]\in(U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}})^{\otimes 2}
is independent of the choice of
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
.

Proof.

By Matsumoto’s Theorem, it suffices to show
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}\equiv\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}\mod{\mathcal{N}}^{\,2}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
for maximal reduced words of the form
z=a\cdot\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}\cdot b
and
w=a\cdot\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}\cdot b
. Following (
9.39
) we have

\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{a\cdot\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}}^{\otimes 2}(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{b}})\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{a}^{\otimes 2}(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}}})\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{a}}\,,

and the analogous expression for
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}
. By Lemma
9.23
the difference between

\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}}}
and

\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ji|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ji$}}}}=\mho\otimes\mho(\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.39304pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.22911pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-0.90138pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}}})
is sum of terms
of the form
(X_{c}\otimes 1)A
and
(1\otimes Y_{c})B
with
c\leq_{R}\mathchoice{{z}\mkern-1.0mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.8mu\raise-1.69998pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.6}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}\mkern-0.77mu\raise-1.49994pt\hbox{\scalebox{0.46}{$|ij|$}}}{{z}^{\circ}\mkern-7.0mu\raise-1.1pt\hbox{\small$\scriptscriptstyle ij$}}
. Since
for these
a\cdot c
is also reduced, we have
\mathit{\Gamma}_{a}(X_{c})=X_{a\cdot c}
and

\mathit{\Gamma}_{a}(Y_{c})=Y_{a\cdot c}
. It follows from their above decompositions that the difference
of
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{z}}
and
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!\raisebox{0.8pt}{\scalebox{.33}{$\mkern 1.3mu\blacktriangleleft\mkern 3.8mu$}}{w}}
is a sum of terms of the form

(X_{a\cdot c}\otimes 1)A^{\prime}
and
(1\otimes Y_{a\cdot c})B^{\prime}\,
, which is, therefore, in

{\mathcal{N}}^{\,2}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
by word independence of the ideal.
∎

The findings of this section together with Corollary
9.13

can now be summarized as follows.

Theorem 9.25
.

For any Lie type and root of unity
\zeta
of order
\mathscr{k}
as in (
6.1
),
the triple
\bigl(U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}},\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.75}{$\star$}},\mbox{\hskip-11.38109pt
L}\bigr)
is a pre-triangualar Hopf algebra over
\Lambda_{\zeta,\ell}^{\mkern-4.0mu\raisebox{0.9289pt}{\scalebox{.47}{$\blacktriangledown$}}}
, independent of choices of maximal reduced words (or convex orderings) used in its construction.

Moreover, all (anti)automorphisms defined in Section
4.1
, including the Artin group action, factor into well-defined (anti)automorphisms on
U_{\zeta,\ell}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.93}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}{\scalebox{.62}{$\mkern 1.0mu\mathsf{rest}$}}}}
.
The construction is, thus, also independent of chosen directions of multiplications and
independent of whether the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
or
T_{i}
are used in the definition of generators.

The construction of braided tensor categories follows along the same steps as described in Section
9.3
, where

Z

is now allowed to have positive characteristic.

Appendix A
Proof of Lemma
9.16

In this section, we prove Lemma
9.16
. It suffices to show that equation (
9.42
)
holds for each choice of
A_{ij}\in\{2,0,-1,-2,-3\}
. The proof is carried out in a series of computations, with a subsection dedicated to each choice of
A_{ij}
. In most cases, we follow the same sequence of steps.

Proof.

The
A_{ij}=0
case is obvious because
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}
commutes with
\Delta(E_{j})
and since the action
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(E_{j})=E_{j}\,
is trivial.

In the remaining cases, we make use of the fact that the coefficients
a_{s}=\dfrac{\zeta_{i}^{s(s-1)/2}}{[s]!_{i}}(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})^{s}
of
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}=\,\sum_{s=0}^{{\ell_{i}}-1}a_{s}\cdot E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s}
satisfy the
recursion relation

(A.1)

a_{s+1}=\dfrac{\zeta_{i}^{s}(\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1})}{[s+1]_{i}}a_{s}\,.

A.1.
Case
A_{ij}=2

In this case, we write
i=j
.
Using (
4.19
), equation (
9.42
) then reduces to

-K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{-1}-K_{i}^{-2}\otimes K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\equiv\,\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot(-K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\otimes K-1\otimes K_{i}^{-1}F_{i})\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\qquad\mod{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})\,.

We will use the commutation relation

\displaystyle[F_{i},E_{i}^{s}]=-[s]_{i}\dfrac{\zeta_{i}^{s-1}K_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-(s-1)}K_{i}^{-1}}{\zeta_{i}-\zeta_{i}^{-1}}E_{i}^{s-1}\;,

which follows from a straightforward induction. Applying these commutators to each summand
of the
R
-matrix we find the relations

\displaystyle(K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{-1})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}

\displaystyle=\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}(K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{-1})-\sum_{s=0}^{{\ell_{i}}-2}a_{s}(E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s})\left(\left(\zeta_{i}^{2s}-K_{i}^{-2}\right)\otimes K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\right)

\displaystyle=\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}(K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{-1}+K_{i}^{-2}\otimes K_{i}^{-1}F_{i})-\sum_{s=0}^{{\ell_{i}}-2}a_{s}\zeta_{i}^{2s}(E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s})\left(1\otimes K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\right)\,,

\displaystyle(1\otimes K_{i}^{-1}F)\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{i}

\displaystyle=\sum_{s=0}^{{\ell_{i}}-1}a_{s}\zeta_{i}^{2s}(E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s})(1\otimes K_{i}^{-1}F_{i})\,.

Combining terms now yields

\displaystyle(-K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{-1}-1\otimes K_{i}^{-1}F_{i})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{i}

\displaystyle=\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{i}(-K_{i}^{-1}F_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{-1}-K_{i}^{-2}\otimes K_{i}^{-1}F_{i})+a_{{\ell_{i}}-1}q^{2{\ell_{i}}}E_{i}^{\ell-1}K_{i}^{-2}\otimes F_{i}^{\ell}K_{i}^{-1}\;,

which implies the desired equality modulo the ideal
{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})
.

A.2.
Case
A_{ij}=-1

In this case
E_{(ij)}=-E_{j}E_{i}+\zeta^{-1}E_{i}E_{j}
. We use the following relations from
[
46
, Section 5.3]
.

\displaystyle E_{(ij)}E_{i}=\zeta E_{i}E_{(ij)}\,,

\displaystyle[E_{(ij)},F_{i}^{s}]=-\zeta^{1-s}[s]_{i}F_{i}^{s-1}K_{i}E_{j}\,,

with the latter relation obtained by applying
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}\circ\mho
to Lusztig’s equation (c) with
k^{\prime}=1
. These give the following relations between
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}
and terms in
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta(E_{j})
.

\displaystyle(E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}K_{j})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}=

\displaystyle\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}(E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}K_{j})\,,

\displaystyle(1\otimes E_{(ij)})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}=

\displaystyle\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}(1\otimes E_{(ij)})-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})\sum_{s=0}^{{\ell_{i}}-2}a_{s}(E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s})(E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j})\,,

\displaystyle\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta(E_{j})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}=

\displaystyle\,\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}(E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}+1\otimes E_{(ij)})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}

\displaystyle+\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})a_{{\ell_{i}}-1}(E_{i}^{\ell_{i}}\otimes F_{i}^{{\ell_{i}}-1}K_{i}E_{j})

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}\qquad\mod{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})\,.

This expression agrees with the coproduct of
E_{(ij)}
computed below and, therefore, verifies the claim in this case.

\displaystyle\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(E_{j})

\displaystyle=\left\{\begin{matrix}[l]-(E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}+E_{j}\otimes K_{j}E_{i}+E_{i}\otimes E_{j}K_{i}+1\otimes E_{j}E_{i})\\
+\zeta^{-1}(E_{i}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}+E_{j}\otimes E_{i}K_{j}+E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}+1\otimes E_{i}E_{j})\end{matrix}\right.

\displaystyle=E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}\,

A.3.
Case
A_{ij}=-2

The following equations
are obtained from

E_{(ij)}=\zeta^{-2}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}-\zeta^{-1}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}+E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}

as well as the ones listed in
[
46
, Section 5.3]
.

\displaystyle E_{(ij)}E_{i}

\displaystyle=\zeta^{2}E_{i}E_{(ij)}\,

\displaystyle[E_{(ij)},F_{i}^{s}]

\displaystyle=-[s]\zeta^{1-s}F_{i}^{s-1}K_{i}E_{(iji)}+[s][s-1]\zeta^{-2s+4}F_{i}^{s-2}K_{i}^{2}E_{j}

The latter equation is obtained by applying
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}\circ\mho
to Lusztig’s equation (i).
We apply these next to compute the commutator of
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}
with
\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta(E_{j})
.

\displaystyle(E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}=

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}(E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j})\,,

\displaystyle(1\otimes E_{(ij)})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}=

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}(1\otimes E_{(ij)})-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})\sum_{s=0}^{\ell-2}a_{s}(E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s})(E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{(iji)})

\displaystyle+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}\sum_{s=0}^{\ell-3}a_{s}(E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s})(E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j})\,.

We infer from these relations that
\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta(E_{j})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}
equals

\displaystyle E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{(iji)}+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j}

\displaystyle+\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\left(a_{\ell-1}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}^{\ell}\otimes F_{i}^{\ell-1}K_{i}E_{(iji)}-\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}\sum_{s=\ell-2}^{\ell-1}a_{s}E_{i}^{s+2}\otimes F_{i}^{s}K_{i}^{2}E_{j}\right)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{(iji)}+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j}\qquad\mod{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})\,.

Since

\displaystyle\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(E_{j})

\displaystyle=\left\{\begin{matrix}[l]\zeta^{-2}\begin{pmatrix}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}+\zeta E_{i}E_{j}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}K_{j}+E_{j}\otimes E_{i}^{(2)}K_{j}\\
+E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j}+\zeta_{i}E_{i}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}E_{j}+1\otimes E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}\end{pmatrix}\\
\rule[-22.76219pt]{0.0pt}{51.21495pt}-\zeta^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}+E_{i}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}E_{i}+E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}K_{i}+E_{j}E_{i}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}K_{j}\\
+E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}E_{i}+E_{j}\otimes E_{i}K_{j}E_{i}+E_{i}\otimes E_{i}E_{j}K_{i}+1\otimes E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}\end{pmatrix}\\
+\begin{pmatrix}E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{2}+\zeta E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{j}E_{i}K_{i}+E_{j}\otimes K_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\\
+E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes E_{j}K_{i}^{2}+\zeta E_{i}\otimes E_{j}E_{i}K_{i}+1\otimes E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\end{pmatrix}\end{matrix}\right.

\displaystyle=E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{2}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes(K_{i}(\zeta^{-2}E_{i}E_{j}-E_{j}E_{i}))+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j}

\displaystyle=E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{(iji)}+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j}\;,

this proves the case for
A_{ij}=-2
.

A.4.
Case
A_{ij}=-3

In this case,

\displaystyle E_{(ij)}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(E_{j})=\zeta^{-3}E_{i}^{(3)}E_{j}-\zeta^{-2}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}E_{i}+\zeta^{-1}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}-E_{j}E_{i}^{(3)}=(T_{w_{j}w_{i}})^{2}(E_{j})\,.

Below, we refer to Lusztig’s equations (a1) and (a3) in
[
46
, Section 5.4]
.

\displaystyle E_{(ij)}E_{i}

\displaystyle=\zeta^{3}E_{i}E_{(ij)}\,

\displaystyle[E_{(ij)},F_{i}^{s}]

\displaystyle=-[s]\zeta^{1-s}F_{i}^{s-1}K_{i}E_{(iji)}+[s]!\zeta^{4-2n}F_{i}^{(s-2)}K_{i}^{2}E_{(ijiji)}-\zeta^{9-3n}[s]!F_{i}^{(s-3)}K_{i}^{3}E_{j}

These relations yield expressions for conjugation of

\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta(E_{j})=E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}^{3}K_{j}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}
by
\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}
via the following computation.

\displaystyle(E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}^{3}K_{j})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}=

\displaystyle\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}(E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}^{3}K_{j})\,,

\displaystyle(1\otimes E_{(ij)})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}=

\displaystyle\,\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}(1\otimes E_{(ij)})-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})\sum_{s=0}^{\ell-2}a_{s}(E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s})(E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{(iji)})

\displaystyle+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}\sum_{s=0}^{\ell-3}a_{s}(E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s})(E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{(ijiji)})

\displaystyle-\zeta^{3}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{3}\sum_{s=0}^{\ell-4}a_{s}(E_{i}^{s}\otimes F_{i}^{s})(E_{i}^{3}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j})\,,

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{19.91692pt}\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\otimes 2}\circ\Delta(E_{j})\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}=

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}^{3}K_{j}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{(iji)}

\displaystyle+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{(ijiji)}-\zeta^{3}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{3}E_{i}^{3}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}

\displaystyle+\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\left(\begin{matrix}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})a_{\ell-1}E_{i}^{\ell}\otimes F_{i}^{\ell-1}K_{i}E_{(iji)}\\
\rule[-17.07164pt]{0.0pt}{39.83385pt}-\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}\sum_{s=\ell-2}^{\ell-1}a_{s}(E_{i}^{s+2}\otimes F_{i}^{s}K_{i}^{2}E_{(ijiji)})\\
+\zeta^{3}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{3}\sum_{s=\ell-3}^{\ell-1}a_{s}(E_{i}^{s+3}\otimes F_{i}^{s}K_{i}^{3}E_{j})\end{matrix}\right)

\displaystyle\equiv

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{i}^{3}K_{j}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{(iji)}

\displaystyle+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{(ijiji)}-\zeta^{3}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{3}E_{i}^{3}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}\qquad\mod{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})\,.

It remains to verify the coproduct identity

\displaystyle\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(E_{j})=\Delta(E_{(ij)})=

\displaystyle E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{3}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{(iji)}

\displaystyle+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{(ijiji)}-\zeta^{3}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{3}E_{i}^{3}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}\,.

We begin by expanding the coproduct for the divided powers expressions in
\Delta(E_{(ij)})
:

\displaystyle\,\begin{matrix}[l]\zeta^{-3}\begin{pmatrix}E_{i}^{(3)}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}^{3}K_{j}+\zeta^{2}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}^{2}K_{j}+\zeta^{2}E_{i}E_{j}\otimes E_{i}^{(2)}K_{i}K_{j}+E_{j}\otimes E_{i}^{(3)}K_{j}\\
+E_{i}^{(3)}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}+\zeta^{2}E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}^{2}E_{j}+\zeta^{2}E_{i}\otimes E_{i}^{(2)}K_{i}E_{j}+1\otimes E_{i}^{(3)}E_{j}\end{pmatrix}\\
-\begin{pmatrix}\zeta^{-2}\begin{pmatrix}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}+\zeta E_{i}E_{j}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}K_{j}+E_{j}\otimes E_{i}^{(2)}K_{j}\\
+E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j}+\zeta E_{i}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}E_{j}+1\otimes E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}\end{pmatrix}\\
-\dfrac{\zeta^{-1}}{[2]}\begin{pmatrix}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}+E_{i}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}E_{i}+E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}K_{i}+E_{j}E_{i}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}K_{j}\\
+E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}E_{i}+E_{j}\otimes E_{i}K_{j}E_{i}+E_{i}\otimes E_{i}E_{j}K_{i}+1\otimes E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}\end{pmatrix}\\
+\dfrac{1}{[3]}\begin{pmatrix}E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{2}+\zeta E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{j}E_{i}K_{i}+E_{j}\otimes K_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\\
+E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes E_{j}K_{i}^{2}+\zeta E_{i}\otimes E_{j}E_{i}K_{i}+1\otimes E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\end{pmatrix}\end{pmatrix}\Delta(E_{i})\end{matrix}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{3}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}

\displaystyle\begin{matrix}[l]+\zeta^{-3}\begin{pmatrix}\zeta^{2}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}^{2}K_{j}+\zeta^{2}E_{i}E_{j}\otimes E_{i}^{(2)}K_{i}K_{j}+E_{j}\otimes E_{i}^{(3)}K_{j}\\
+E_{i}^{(3)}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}+\zeta^{2}E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}^{2}E_{j}+\zeta^{2}E_{i}\otimes E_{i}^{(2)}K_{i}E_{j}\end{pmatrix}\\
+\begin{pmatrix}-\zeta^{-2}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}E_{i}-\zeta^{-2}E_{i}\otimes E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}K_{i}+\dfrac{\zeta^{-1}}{[2]}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}E_{i}\\
+\dfrac{\zeta^{-1}}{[2]}E_{i}\otimes E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}K_{i}-\dfrac{1}{[3]}E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{2}E_{i}-\dfrac{1}{[3]}E_{i}\otimes E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}K_{i}\end{pmatrix}\\
-\begin{pmatrix}\zeta^{-2}\begin{pmatrix}\zeta E_{i}E_{j}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}K_{j}+E_{j}\otimes E_{i}^{(2)}K_{j}\\
+E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j}+\zeta E_{i}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}E_{j}\end{pmatrix}\\
-\dfrac{\zeta^{-1}}{[2]}\begin{pmatrix}E_{i}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}E_{i}+E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}K_{i}+E_{j}E_{i}\otimes E_{i}K_{i}K_{j}\\
+E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}E_{i}+E_{j}\otimes E_{i}K_{j}E_{i}+E_{i}\otimes E_{i}E_{j}K_{i}\end{pmatrix}\\
+\dfrac{1}{[3]}\begin{pmatrix}\zeta E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{j}E_{i}K_{i}+E_{j}\otimes K_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\\
+E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes E_{j}K_{i}^{2}+\zeta E_{i}\otimes E_{j}E_{i}K_{i}\end{pmatrix}\end{pmatrix}\Delta(E_{i})\end{matrix}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{3}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}

\displaystyle\begin{matrix}[l]+\zeta^{-3}\begin{pmatrix}\zeta E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}E_{i}+\zeta^{4}E_{i}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}+\zeta^{9}E_{j}\otimes K_{j}E_{i}^{(3)}\\
+E_{i}^{(3)}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}+\zeta^{-2}E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{i}E_{j}+\zeta^{-2}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}\end{pmatrix}\\
+\begin{pmatrix}-\zeta^{-2}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}E_{i}-\zeta^{-3}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}+\dfrac{\zeta^{-1}}{[2]}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}E_{i}\\
+\dfrac{\zeta^{-2}}{[2]}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}-\dfrac{1}{[3]}E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{2}E_{i}-\dfrac{\zeta^{-1}}{[3]}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\end{pmatrix}\\
-\begin{pmatrix}\dfrac{\zeta}{[2]}E_{i}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}E_{i}+\dfrac{\zeta^{6}}{[3]}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}^{(2)}+\dfrac{\zeta^{6}-\zeta^{4}-\zeta^{2}+\zeta^{-2}+\zeta^{-4}}{[3]}E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j}\\
+\dfrac{\zeta^{-4}+\zeta^{-2}-1}{[2]}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}E_{j}-\dfrac{\zeta^{2}}{[2][3]}E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}E_{i}+\dfrac{\zeta^{3}-\zeta^{-1}-\zeta^{-3}}{[2][3]}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}E_{i}\end{pmatrix}\Delta(E_{i})\end{matrix}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{3}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-\zeta^{-4}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}

\displaystyle\begin{matrix}[l]+\zeta^{-3}\begin{pmatrix}\zeta^{4}E_{i}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}+\zeta^{9}E_{j}\otimes K_{j}E_{i}^{(3)}\\
+E_{i}^{(3)}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}+\zeta^{-2}E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{i}E_{j}\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}\dfrac{\zeta^{-1}}{[2]}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}E_{i}+\dfrac{\zeta^{-2}}{[2]}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}\\
-\dfrac{1}{[3]}E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{2}E_{i}-\dfrac{\zeta^{-1}}{[3]}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}\end{pmatrix}\\
-\begin{pmatrix}\dfrac{\zeta^{-1}}{[2]}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}E_{i}+\dfrac{\zeta}{[2]}E_{i}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}K_{j}E_{i}^{2}+\dfrac{\zeta^{6}}{[2][3]}E_{j}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}^{3}\\
+\dfrac{\zeta^{9}-\zeta^{7}-\zeta^{5}+\zeta+\zeta^{-1}}{[2][3]}E_{i}^{3}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j}E_{i}+\dfrac{\zeta^{-3}+\zeta^{-1}-\zeta}{[2]}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{i}E_{j}\\
+\dfrac{\zeta^{-4}+\zeta^{-2}-1}{[2]}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}-\dfrac{1}{[2][3]}E_{j}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}K_{j}E_{i}+\dfrac{\zeta^{3}-\zeta^{-1}-\zeta^{-3}}{[2][3]}E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}E_{i}^{2}\end{pmatrix}\end{matrix}

Further collapsing these expressions, we obtain

\displaystyle\Delta(E_{(ij)})=

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{3}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-\zeta^{-4}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)}

\displaystyle+\zeta^{-2}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}-\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{j}E_{i}

\displaystyle-\zeta^{3}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{3}E_{i}^{3}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}-\zeta^{-2}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{i}E_{j}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{19.91692pt}=

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{3}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}(\zeta^{-4}E_{i}^{(2)}E_{j}-\zeta^{-2}E_{i}E_{j}E_{i}+E_{j}E_{i}^{(2)})

\displaystyle+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}(\zeta^{-3}E_{i}E_{j}-E_{j}E_{i})-\zeta^{3}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{3}E_{i}^{3}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{19.91692pt}=

\displaystyle\,E_{(ij)}\otimes K_{j}K_{i}^{3}+1\otimes E_{(ij)}-(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})E_{i}\otimes K_{i}E_{(iji)}

\displaystyle+\zeta(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{2}E_{i}^{2}\otimes K_{i}^{2}E_{(ijiji)}-\zeta^{3}(\zeta-\zeta^{-1})^{3}E_{i}^{3}\otimes K_{i}^{3}E_{j}\,.

This now proves
\Delta\circ\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(E_{j})\,\equiv\,\raise 7.29996pt\hbox{\rule{6.54413pt}{0.79666pt}}\mkern-11.8mu{\mathcal{P}}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\cdot\mathit{\Gamma}^{\otimes 2}_{i}\circ\Delta(E_{j})\cdot\mathcal{P}^{\scalebox{.35}{$\blacklozenge$}}_{\!i}\quad\mod{\mathcal{N}}\mkern-1.0mu(w_{i})
.
∎

Appendix B
Proofs and Computations for Section
8.2

We supply here the computational proofs of
Proposition
8.3
and Lemma
B.3

used in Sections
8.1
and
8.2
.

B.1.
Proof of Proposition
8.3

We begin with a variation of the recursive identity used to define the coefficients
c_{k,t}
in (
8.13
) that applies more directly to the desired proof. To this end we introduce
notation for the coefficients actually appearing in the formula of Proposition
8.3
, namely,

(B.1)

a^{n}_{s,t,k}=q^{-(s+t+k)(n-s-t-k)-(s-t)(2t+k)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
s+t+k\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$s+t+k$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
s-t\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}c_{k,t}\,,

for
s\geq t\geq 0
,
k\geq 0
, and
n\geq s+t+k\,
. We further have
a^{0}_{0,0,0}=1
and use the convention that
a^{n}_{s,t,k}=0
whenever any one of the index bounds is exceeded. That is, whenever

(B.2)

s,t,k<0\,,\qquad s>n\,,\qquad t>\min{(s,n-s)}\,,\quad\mbox{or}\quad k>n-s-t\,.

Lemma B.1
.

With definitions and conventions as above, we have the recursion

a^{n+1}_{s,t,k}=q^{-2(n+1-s+t)}a^{n}_{s-1,t,k}+q^{-3(n+1-s-t-k)}[n+2-s-t-k]a^{n}_{s-1,t-1,k}+q^{-2(n+1-s-t-k)}a^{n}_{s,t,k-1}+a^{n}_{s,t,k}\,.

Proof.

The following straightforward verification makes repeated use of the

q
-binomial formula from (
3.2
). To shorten some formulae, we use
u=s+t+k
.

\displaystyle a^{n+1}_{s,t,k}=

\displaystyle~q^{-u(n+1-u)-(s-t)(2t+k)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n+1$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
u\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$u$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
s-t\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}c_{k,t}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle~q^{-u(n+1-u)-(s-t)(2t+k)}\left(q^{u}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
u\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}+q^{-(n+1-u)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
u-1\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}\right)\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$u$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
s-t\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}c_{k,t}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle~a^{n}_{s,t,k}+q^{-(u+1)(n+1-u)-(s-t)(2t+k)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
u-1\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}\left(q^{s-t}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$u-1$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
s-t\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}+q^{-(2t+k)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$u-1$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
s-1-t\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}\right)c_{k,t}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle~a^{n}_{s,t,k}+q^{-2(n+1-s+t)}a^{n}_{s-1,t,k}

\displaystyle+q^{-(u+1)(n+1-u)-(s-t)(2t+k-1)}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
u-1\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$u-1$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
s-t\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}(c_{k-1,t}+q^{-(2t+k-2)}[2t+k-1]c_{k,t-1})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle~a^{n}_{s,t,k}+q^{-2(n+1-s+t)}a^{n}_{s-1,t,k}+q^{-2(n+1-u)}a^{n}_{s,t,k-1}

\displaystyle+q^{-(u+1)(n+1-u)-(s-t+1)(2t+k-1)+1}[n+2-u]\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
u-2\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$u-2$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
s-t\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}c_{k,t-1}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle a^{n}_{s,t,k}+q^{-2(n+1-s+t)}a^{n}_{s-1,t,k}+q^{-2(n+1-u)}a^{n}_{s,t,k-1}+q^{-3(n+1-u)}[n+2-u]a^{n}_{s-1,t-1,k}\,.

∎

Observe that we may also consider the
a^{n}_{s,t,k}
to be defined via the
recursion in Lemma
B.1
and the mentioned boundary conditions.
The following identity is proved in
[
45
, Lemma 1.6]
for the special case
v=1
.

Lemma B.2
.

Suppose
A,B,D
satisfy

\displaystyle DA=v^{2}AD+B,

\displaystyle BA=q^{-2}v^{2}AB,\qquad\mbox{and}

\displaystyle DB=q^{-2}v^{2}BD\,.

Then
D^{m}A=v^{2m}AD^{m}+(q^{-1}v^{2})^{m-1}[m]BD^{m-1}
and

D^{m}A^{n}=\sum_{i=0}^{\min(m,n)}v^{2mn-i(i+1)}q^{-i(n+m-2i)-i(i-1)/2}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$n$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
i\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\vskip-1.99168pt\raise 2.84526pt\hbox{$m$}\vskip-1.99168pt\\
i\vskip-2.27621pt\end{bmatrix}[i]!A^{n-i}B^{i}D^{m-i}\,,

where quantum numbers and coefficients are with respect to
q\,
.

Proof.

Each of the two claims of the lemma is proved by induction. The base case of the former is the assumption
DA=v^{2}AD+B
. For the induction step, we compute

\displaystyle D^{m+1}A

\displaystyle=D(v^{2m}AD^{m}+(q^{-1}v^{2})^{m-1}[m]BD^{m-1})

\displaystyle=v^{2(m+1)}AD^{m+1}+v^{2m}BD^{m}+(q^{-2}v^{2})(q^{-1}v^{2})^{m-1}[m]BD^{m}

\displaystyle=v^{2(m+1)}AD^{m+1}+(q^{-1}v^{2})^{m}[m+1]BD^{m}\,,

where the last equality uses
1+q^{-(m+1)}[m]=q^{-m}[m+1]\,
. The second statement
is now derived by induction in
n
using the first identity as the base case.
It amounts to repeated use of (
3.2
) and resummations.
∎

Note that the
q
-binomials disappear in the formula of Lemma
B.2
if it is rewritten
in terms of divided power generators
A^{(n)}=\frac{1}{[n]!}A^{n}
. That is, we find instead

D^{(m)}A^{(n)}=\sum_{i=0}^{\min(m,n)}v^{2mn-i(i+1)}q^{i(n+m-2i)+i(i-1)/2}A^{(n-i)}B^{(i)}D^{(m-i)}\,.

With these preparations we proceed to the main goal of this section.

Proof of Proposition
8.3
.

Assume
A
,
B
,
C
, and
D
fulfill the commutation relations stated in the proposition. The assertion is trivial for
n=0
and easily worked
out for
n=1\,
. Assume, thus, that the formula hold for
(A+C+D)^{n}
, with coefficients
a^{n}_{s,t,k}
as in (
B.1
). We compute

\displaystyle(A+C+D)^{n+1}=

\displaystyle~\sum_{s=0}^{n}\sum_{t=0}^{\min(s,n-s)}\sum_{k=0}^{n-s-t}a^{n}_{s,t,k}A^{s-t}B^{t}C^{k}D^{n-s-t-k}(A+C+D)

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{31.29802pt}=

\displaystyle~\sum_{s=0}^{n}\sum_{t=0}^{\min(s,n-s)}\sum_{k=0}^{n-s-t}a^{n}_{s,t,k}q^{-2(n-s+t)}A^{s-t+1}B^{t}C^{k}D^{n-s-t-k}

\displaystyle\qquad+a^{n}_{s,t,k}q^{-3(n-1-s-t-k)}[n-s-t-k]A^{s-t}B^{t+1}C^{k}D^{n-s-t-k-1}

\displaystyle\qquad+a^{n}_{s,t,k}q^{-2(n-s-t-k)}A^{s-t}B^{t}C^{k+1}D^{n-s-t-k}

\displaystyle\qquad+a^{n}_{s,t,k}A^{s-t}B^{t}C^{k}D^{n+1-s-t-k}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{31.29802pt}=

\displaystyle\sum_{s=1}^{n+1}\sum_{t=0}^{\min(s-1,n+1-s)}\sum_{k=0}^{n+1-s-t}a^{n}_{s-1,t,k}q^{-2(n+1-s+t)}A^{s-t}B^{t}C^{k}D^{n+1-s-t-k}

\displaystyle+\sum_{s=1}^{n+1}\sum_{t=1}^{\min(s,n+1-s)}\sum_{k=0}^{n+1-s-t}a^{n}_{s-1,t-1,k}q^{-3(n+1-s-t-k)}[n+2-s-t-k]A^{s-t}B^{t}C^{k}D^{n+1-s-t-k}

\displaystyle+\sum_{s=0}^{n}\sum_{t=0}^{\min(s,n-s)}\sum_{k=1}^{n+1-s-t}a^{n}_{s,t,k-1}q^{-2(n+1-s-t-k)}A^{s-t}B^{t}C^{k}D^{n+1-s-t-k}

\displaystyle+\sum_{s=0}^{n}\sum_{t=0}^{\min(s,n-s)}\sum_{k=0}^{n-s-t}a^{n}_{s,t,k}A^{s-t}B^{t}C^{k}D^{n+1-s-t-k}

\displaystyle\rule{0.0pt}{31.29802pt}=

\displaystyle\sum_{s=0}^{n+1}\sum_{t=0}^{\min(s,n+1-s)}\sum_{k=0}^{n+1-s-t}a^{n+1}_{s,t,k}A^{s-t}B^{t}C^{k}D^{n+1-s-t-k}\,.

In the first step, we employ the original commutation relations as well as Lemma
B.2
.
In the second step, we shift summation indices and make use of the boundary conditions on
the
a^{n}_{s,t,k}\,
. The last equation then results from Lemma
B.1
, completing the induction step.
∎

B.2.
A Summation Identity for the
c^{\prime}_{k,p}

As before, let
c_{k,p}
be the coefficients defined recursively in (
8.13
)
and
c^{\prime}_{k,p}=\mathsf{sq}(c_{k,p})
the element in
\Lambda_{q}
with
q
replaced by
q^{2}
as
explained in Section
8.2
.

Lemma B.3
.

For all
n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}
, the following equality holds in
\Lambda_{q,3}\,
,

\sum_{p=0}^{\lfloor{n/2}\rfloor}\left(-\frac{q-q^{-1}}{q^{2}[2]}\right)^{p}c^{\prime}_{n-2p,p}=q^{-\binom{n}{2}}[2]^{-n}\left\{n\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu2\right\}\,.

Proof.

Recall that
\left\{n\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu2\right\}=\prod_{i=1}^{n}(q^{i}+q^{-i})
under the specialization of
\mathsf{e}=2
in (
3.6
). We prove that both expressions in the proposed equality are sequences in
n
with the same initial values and satisfy the same recursion relation. Denote the sides of the desired equality by

\displaystyle A_{n}

\displaystyle=\sum_{p=0}^{\lfloor{n/2}\rfloor}\phi_{p}c^{\prime}_{n-2p,p}\,,

where
\phi_{p}=\left(-\frac{q-q^{-1}}{q^{2}[2]}\right)^{p}
, and

\displaystyle B_{n}

\displaystyle=q^{-\binom{n}{2}}\psi_{n}\,,

\displaystyle\mbox{where $\psi_{n}=[2]^{-n}\left\{n\mkern-3.0mu:\mkern-3.0mu2\right\}$}\,.

Observe that
A_{0}=B_{0}=A_{1}=B_{1}=1
. The recursion for
A_{n}
is given below. Note that if
n
is even,
c^{\prime}_{n-2(\lfloor{n/2}\rfloor-1),p}=0
and
n/2-1=\lfloor{(n-1)/2}\rfloor
. Whereas if
n
is odd,
\lfloor{n/2}\rfloor=\lfloor{(n-1)/2}\rfloor
and
c^{\prime}_{n-2(\lfloor{n/2}\rfloor-1),p}\neq 0
.

\displaystyle A_{n}

\displaystyle=\sum_{p=0}^{\lfloor{n/2}\rfloor}\phi_{p}c^{\prime}_{n-2p,p}=\sum_{p=0}^{\lfloor{n/2}\rfloor}\phi_{p}(c^{\prime}_{n-2p-1,p}+c^{\prime}_{n-2p,p-1}q^{-2(n-2)}[n-1]_{q^{2}})

\displaystyle=A_{n-1}+q^{-2(n-2)}[n-1]_{q^{2}}\sum_{p=0}^{\lfloor{n/2}\rfloor-1}\phi_{p+1}c^{\prime}_{n-2p-2,p}

\displaystyle=A_{n-1}-q^{-2(n-2)}[n-1]_{q^{2}}\left(\frac{q-q^{-1}}{q^{2}[2]}\right)A_{n-2}

\displaystyle=A_{n-1}-q^{-2(n-1)}[n-1]_{q^{2}}\frac{q-q^{-1}}{[2]}A_{n-2}

Hence
A_{n}-A_{n-1}=-q^{-2(n-1)}[n-1]_{q^{2}}\frac{q-q^{-1}}{[2]}A_{n-2}
. An identical recursion for
B_{n}
is found by computing

\displaystyle B_{n}-B_{n-1}

\displaystyle=\psi_{n-2}[2]^{-1}(q^{n-1}+q^{-(n-1)})\left(q^{-\binom{n}{2}}(q^{n}+q^{-n})[2]^{-1}-q^{-\binom{n-1}{2}}\right)

\displaystyle=\psi_{n-2}[2]^{-1}(q^{n-1}+q^{-(n-1)})q^{-\binom{n-2}{2}}\left(q^{-2n+3}(q^{n}+q^{-n})[2]^{-1}-q^{-n+2}\right)

\displaystyle=B_{n-2}\frac{[n-1]_{q^{2}}}{[2][n-1]}\left((q^{-n+3}+q^{-3n+3})-(q^{-n+3}+q^{-n+1})\right)

\displaystyle=-q^{-2(n-1)}\frac{[n-1]_{q^{2}}}{[2]}(q-q^{-1})B_{n-2}\,.

It follows that
A_{n}=B_{n}
by strong induction, which is the identity claimed in the lemma.
∎

Appendix C
Inexistence of Quantum Weyl Elements and Related Notes

In the finite-dimensional representation theory of classical, simple Lie algebras, Weyl elements
are formal elements that are instrumental in the derivation of various dimension and character formulae. For a simply connected simple Lie group
G
with maximal torus
T\subset G
the geometric Weyl group
\mathscr{W}
, defined as

N(T)/T
, is acting on
\mathfrak{h}
, the Lie algebra of
T
, via conjugation by representatives in the normalizer
N(T)\,
.
The action of a standard generator
s_{i}\in\mathscr{W}
is given by
S_{i}=\mathrm{Ad}(\mathscr{w}_{i})
,
where
\mathscr{w}_{i}=\exp(E_{i})\exp(-F_{i})\exp(E_{i})\in N(T)
. (see, for example,
[
32
]
). The elements
\mathscr{w}_{i}
also appear in the theory of Chevalley groups and Tits systems.

The
\mathscr{W}
-action extends naturally to
\mathfrak{g}
and hence to

U(\mathfrak{g})
. There, the generators
S_{i}
coincide with the
T_{i}
or
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
actions
on
U_{\hbar}(\mathfrak{g})
from Section
4.3
in the specialization
\hbar\rightarrow 0\,
. On finite-dimensional highest weight representations
V
of the corresponding Lie algebra
\mathfrak{g}
the
\mathscr{w}_{i}
, as elements of
\mathrm{End}(V)
, are well-defined since
E_{i}
and
F_{i}
act nilpotently on
V
.

Quantum Weyl elements attempt to define analogs of
\mathscr{w}_{i}
for certain versions of quantum groups, which implement the
T_{i}
or
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
actions in the same manner by conjugation. Constructions of such elements are described in

[
66
,
44
,
42
]
and
[
16
, 8.2]
. In essence, these approaches map a quantum group
U
into a completion of
\bigoplus_{\lambda}\mathrm{End}(V_{\lambda})
, where
\lambda
ranges over dominant highest weights so that
each
V_{\lambda}
naturally carries a
\mathscr{W}
-action. The
\mathscr{w}_{i}

elements are then used to derive various formulae for
R
-matrices and

\mathscr{A}
-actions.

For relevant versions of quantum groups at roots of unity, however, quantum Weyl elements implementing the
T_{i}
-actions
almost never
exist for
U_{\zeta}
and related quantum algebras, even if formulated in a very weak sense. The criteria discussed in this section illustrate that such implementations exist only in very exceptional types of representations.

Consider a representation
\rho:U_{\zeta,\mathbb{Q}}\rightarrow\mathrm{End}(V)
on a vector space
V
over
\mathbb{C}

give an embedding
\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)\subset\mathbb{C}
.
Let

\mathfrak{z}
be the center of
U_{\zeta,\mathbb{Q}}
and
\mathcal{Z}=\mathcal{Z}_{\bullet}\otimes\mathbb{C}
the full subalgebra described in Section
6.3
. With primes indicating commutants, we have inclusions

\,\mathrm{im}(\rho)\subseteq\mathrm{im}(\rho)^{\prime\prime}\subseteq(\rho(\mathfrak{z}))^{\prime}\subseteq(\rho(\mathfrak{z}\cap\mathcal{Z}))^{\prime}=:C_{\rho}\,
of subalgebras of
\mathrm{End}(V)\,
. We say that a representation
(\rho,V)
is
weakly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant
if there exist
invertible operators
\mathsf{M}_{i}\in C_{\rho}
such that
\,\rho(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}(x))=\mathsf{M}_{i}\rho(x)\mathsf{M}_{i}^{-1}\,
for all
i=1,\ldots,n\,
and

x\in U_{\zeta,\mathbb{Q}}\,
. The existence of quantum Weyl elements
\mathscr{w}_{i}\in U_{\zeta,\mathbb{Q}}
would immediately imply this property
for
all
representations
by setting
\mathsf{M}_{i}=\rho(\mathscr{w}_{i})\in\mathrm{im}(\rho)
and is, thus, a far stronger requirement.

For the assertions and counterexamples that follow, assume
\mathscr{k}
is odd and exclude Lie types
\mathsf{B}
and
\mathsf{G}
. Fix a maximal word
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
and denote respective generators by
E_{\alpha}
in the sense of (
5.3
). Similar results hold for other Lie types and even
\mathscr{k}
but are technically more involved.

For a given representation,

(\rho,V)
use the shorthand
\bar{A}=\rho(A)
for
A\in U_{\zeta,\mathbb{Q}}
as well as
F_{\alpha}=E_{-\alpha}

and
Y_{\alpha}=X_{-\alpha}
for
\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\,
. Let also
\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Lambda}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Lambda}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Lambda}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Lambda}$}}}_{\mathscr{k}}=\mathbb{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}}/\mathscr{k}\mathbb{Z}^{{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}}\cong(\mathbb{F}_{\mathscr{k}})^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Delta}$}}}}
be the
weight space mod
\mathscr{k}
, generated by the fundamental weights
\varpi_{i}\,
defined via

\mathchoice{\left(\varpi_{i}|\breve{\alpha}_{j}\right)}{(\varpi_{i}|\breve{\alpha}_{j})}{(\varpi_{i}|\breve{\alpha}_{j})}{(\varpi_{i}|\breve{\alpha}_{j})}=\delta_{ij}\,
. Assuming
(\rho,V)
is weakly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant, denote by
\mathbb{M}
the subgroup of
\mathrm{GL}(V)\cap C_{\rho}
generated by

\mathsf{M}_{i}\,
. Moreover, for a reduced word
w=w_{i_{1}}\ldots w_{i_{k}}\,
, write
\mathsf{M}_{w}=\mathsf{M}_{i_{1}}\cdot\ldots\cdot\mathsf{M}_{i_{k}}\,
. Recall also the augmentation ideals

\mathcal{K}_{\bullet}^{\raisebox{1.0pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\Box$}}
and

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}
as defined in (
6.67
) and (
6.72
) of Section
6.5
.

Proposition C.1
.

Suppose
(\rho,V)
is weakly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant with
\{\mathsf{M}_{i}\}
and
\mathbb{M}
as above,
\mathscr{k}
odd, and the Lie type is neither
\mathsf{B}
nor
\mathsf{G}\,
. Then

i)

We have decompositions
V=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Lambda}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Lambda}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Lambda}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Lambda}$}}}_{\mathscr{k}}}V_{\lambda}\,
, where
\,K_{i}v=\zeta^{\mathchoice{\left(\lambda|\alpha_{i}\right)}{(\lambda|\alpha_{i})}{(\lambda|\alpha_{i})}{(\lambda|\alpha_{i})}}v\,
for
\,v\in V_{\lambda}\,
. Moreover,
\,\bar{E}_{\alpha}(V_{\lambda})\subseteq V_{\lambda+\alpha}\,
and
\,\bar{F}_{\alpha}(V_{\lambda})\subseteq V_{\lambda-\alpha}\,
.

ii)

For any
w\in\mathscr{W}^{*}
we have
\mathsf{M}_{w}(V_{\lambda})=V_{s(\lambda)}
where
s=\gamma(w)
.

iii)

For any pair
\alpha,\beta\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
with
d_{\alpha}=d_{\beta}\,
there exists an
\,\mathsf{M}\in\mathbb{M}\,
such
that
\,\mathsf{M}\bar{E}_{\alpha}\mathsf{M}^{-1}=\bar{E}_{\beta}\,
. Similarly,

\bar{F}_{\alpha}
and
\bar{F}_{\beta}
are conjugate by some element in
\,\mathbb{M}\,
, as are
\bar{F}_{\alpha}
and

-\bar{E}_{\beta}\bar{K}^{\beta}\,
.

iv)

There are operators
\,\bar{Z}_{1},\bar{Z}_{\mathsf{e}}\in\mathbb{M}^{\prime}\cap(\mathrm{im}(\rho))^{\prime}\subset\mathrm{End}(V)\,
such that
\bar{X}_{\alpha}=-\bar{Y}_{\alpha}=\bar{Z}_{1}
for all short roots
\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
(that is,
d_{\alpha}=1
) and
\bar{X}_{\alpha}=-\bar{Y}_{\alpha}=\bar{Z}_{\mathsf{e}}
if
\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}
is a long root (
d_{\alpha}=\mathsf{e}\,
).

v)

Suppose
V
is cyclic with a cyclic vector
\mathbfit v\in V
such that
U_{\zeta,\mathbb{Q}}^{+}\mathbfit v=0
. Then

\widehat{\mathcal{K}}_{\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}\mkern-1.4mu\scalebox{.95}{$\bullet$}}\subseteq\mathrm{ker}(\rho)
so that
(\rho,V)
factors into a representation of a respective small quantum group.

Proof.

Note first that the definition of weak
\mathscr{A}
-equivariance implies that for any
a\in\mathcal{Z}\cap\mathfrak{z}
we have
\rho(\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(a))=\rho(a)\,
. Now, since
\mathscr{k}
is odd we have
\,L_{i}=K_{i}^{\mathscr{k}}\in\mathcal{Z}\cap\mathfrak{z}\,
, which implies with
\mathit{\Gamma}_{j}(L_{i})=L_{i}L_{j}^{-A_{ji}}
that
\,\bar{L}_{j}^{-A_{ji}}=\mathbb{1}\in\mathrm{End}(V)\,
for all
\,i,j=\{1,\ldots,n\}\,
. For Lie types different from
\mathsf{B}
we have
\gcd(A_{j1},\ldots,A_{jn})=1
for any
j
so that, indeed,
\bar{L}_{j}=\bar{K}_{j}^{\mathscr{k}}=\mathbb{1}
for all
j\,
. Over a field containing
\zeta
, this implies a decomposition into common eigenspaces of the
\bar{K}_{j}
with eigenvalues of
\bar{K}_{j}
given by some powers
\zeta^{\lambda_{i}}\,
with
\lambda_{i}\in\mathbb{F}_{\mathscr{k}}\,
. Now, for
\lambda=\sum_{i}\lambda_{i}\varpi_{i}
we have
\lambda_{i}=\mathchoice{\left(\lambda|\breve{\alpha}_{i}\right)}{(\lambda|\breve{\alpha}_{i})}{(\lambda|\breve{\alpha}_{i})}{(\lambda|\breve{\alpha}_{i})}\equiv\mathchoice{\left(\lambda|\alpha_{i}\right)}{(\lambda|\alpha_{i})}{(\lambda|\alpha_{i})}{(\lambda|\alpha_{i})}\mod\mathscr{k}
since
\mathscr{k}
is coprime to all
d_{i}
if the Lie type
\mathsf{G}
is also excluded, proving the decomposition in Item
i)
.
The other claims in Item
i)
as well as Item
ii)
are immediate from commutation relations with the
K_{j}
and the actions of the
\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}
on the
K_{j}
.

For Item
iii)
write
E_{\alpha}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{s}(E_{i})
and
E_{\beta}=\mathit{\Gamma}_{t}(E_{j})
for some

s,t\in\mathscr{W}
and
i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\,
with
d_{i}=d_{j}
. So,
\bar{E}_{\alpha}=\mathsf{M}_{w}\bar{E}_{i}\mathsf{M}_{w}^{-1}
and

\bar{E}_{\beta}=\mathsf{M}_{u}\bar{E}_{j}\mathsf{M}_{u}^{-1}\,
with
s=\mathscr{r}(w)
and
t=\mathscr{r}(u)\,
. Since
\alpha_{i}

and
\alpha_{j}
have the same length, there is some
r\in\mathscr{W}
such that
r(\alpha_{i})=\alpha_{j}\,
. From
Proposition
5.1
we then find that
\mathit{\Gamma}_{r}(E_{i})=E_{j}
and, hence,

\mathsf{M}_{z}\bar{E}_{i}\mathsf{M}_{z}^{-1}=\bar{E}_{j}
where
r=\mathscr{r}(z)\,
. The claim now follows for
\mathsf{M}=\mathsf{M}_{u}\mathsf{M}_{z}\mathsf{M}_{w}^{-1}\in\mathbb{M}\,
. The remaining assertions follow from analogous arguments.

Since all
X_{\alpha},Y_{\alpha}\in\mathcal{Z}\cap\mathfrak{z}
by Proposition
6.12
, we infer that
\bar{X}_{\alpha},\bar{Y}_{\alpha}\in\mathbb{M}^{\prime}\cap(\mathrm{im}(\rho))^{\prime}\,
for all
\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\,
. Item
iii)
now implies that
\bar{X}_{\alpha}=\bar{X}_{\beta}
and

\bar{Y}_{\alpha}=\bar{Y}_{\beta}
whenever
d_{\alpha}=d_{\beta}\,
. Next,
\bar{L}_{i}=\mathbb{1}
and (
6.20
) also imply

\bar{X}_{i}=-\bar{Y}_{i}
for all
i\,
so that also
\bar{X}_{\alpha}=-\bar{Y}_{\beta}

whenever
d_{\alpha}=d_{\beta}\,
, proving the claim in Item
iv)
.

For a cyclic vector
\mathbfit v\in V
as in Item
v)
, note that,
by Item
iv)
, any
\bar{Z}\in\{\bar{Z}_{1},\bar{Z}_{\mathsf{e}}\}
is given as

\bar{Z}=\bar{X}_{i}
for some
i
so that
\bar{Z}\mathbfit v=\bar{X}_{i}\mathbfit v=0\,
. Given that any

\bar{A}\in\mathrm{im}(\rho)\,
commutes with
\bar{Z}
, we also find
\bar{Z}\bar{A}\mathbfit v=\bar{A}\bar{Z}\mathbfit v=0

and hence
\bar{Z}=\bar{0}
by the cyclicity assumption. Item
iv)

now implies that all
\bar{X}_{\alpha}=\bar{Y}_{\alpha}=0\,
. Thus,
X_{\alpha}=E_{\alpha}^{\ell_{\alpha}}
,

Y_{\alpha}=F_{\alpha}^{\ell_{\alpha}}
, and
K_{i}^{\ell_{i}}-1=L_{i}-1
are all in the kernel of
\rho
, which then factors into the small quantum group.
∎

In the remainder of this section, we provide several examples of representations that are not weakly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant using the criteria from the above proposition.

Denote by
V_{\kappa}
the weight space on which each
K_{i}
acts as
\kappa_{i}\mathbb{1}\,
for an
n
-tuple
\kappa=(\kappa_{1},\ldots,\kappa_{n})\in\mathbb{t}=(\mathbb{C}^{\times})^{n}\,
. For any
\kappa\in\mathbb{t}
,
a representation with
V_{\kappa}\neq 0
can be easily constructed, for example, as a highest weight representation with highest weight
\kappa\,
. The latter can also chosen to be finite-dimensional and irreducible by dividing out maximal submodules as usual. The condition in Item
i)
thus restricts the set of possible weights from the infinite group
\mathbb{t}
to the finite subgroup
\mathbb{s}=\{\kappa\in\mathbb{t}:\kappa_{i}^{\mathscr{k}}=1\,\forall i\}
of tuples of roots of unity. In this sense, even the weak
\mathscr{A}
-equivariance condition forces a restriction to a null set.

Requiring
\bar{L}_{i}=\mathbb{1}
still leaves large families of finite-dimensional
representations that are not waekly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant. Assuming that
\mathscr{k}
is odd,
these are readily constructed by choosing

any
ideal
J\subsetneq\mathcal{K}_{\bullet}^{-}\subsetneq\mathcal{Z}^{-}\cong\mathbb{C}[\{Y_{\alpha}:\alpha\in{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\scalebox{1.18}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}{\raisebox{-0.15pt}{\scalebox{0.8}{$\mathsf{\Phi}$}}}^{+}}\}]\,
such that
\mathcal{Z}^{-}/J
is of finite rank
m>1\,
.
Since
\mathcal{Z}
is central, any weight
\kappa\in\mathbb{s}
defines a
one-dimensional representation of
B_{J}=J\cdot U_{\zeta,\mathbb{k}}^{{\mathchoice{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.86}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}{\scalebox{.5}{$\mkern 1.0mu\geq\mkern-4.3mu0$}}}}
with
K_{i}\mathbfit v=\kappa_{i}\mathbfit v
and

E_{i}\mathbfit v=b\mathbfit v=0
for all
i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}
and all
b\in J\,
. The induced
module
U_{\zeta,\mathbb{k}}\otimes_{B_{J}}\mathbfit v
is now finite-dimensional with
\bar{L}_{i}=\mathbb{1}
,
but violates Item
v)
in the proposition above and is, thus, not

\mathscr{A}
-equivariant. There are many choices for
J
for which the
\bar{Y}_{\alpha}
are not zero and may in fact even be invertible.

C.1.
An Example in Rank 1

Even among representations that factor through the small quantum groups, most are still not weakly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant. This can already be seen in the rank 1 case
\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
and
\mathscr{k}=3\,
for which
E^{3}=F^{3}=0
and
K^{3}=1\,
.

Denote by
V_{0}
,
V_{-}
, and
V_{+}
the eigenspaces of
K
for eigenvalues
1,
\zeta^{2}=\zeta^{-1}
, and
\zeta^{-2}=\zeta^{1}
, respectively.
We consider a special family of representations in which
V_{+}
and
V_{-}
are isomorphic as vector spaces
to a common space
V_{*}
so that, after conjugation by respective isomorphisms,
the restrictions
E:V_{-}\rightarrow V_{+}
and
F:V_{+}\rightarrow V_{-}
may be viewed as linear endomorphisms of
V_{*}\,
.
Further specializing our example, we assume that these two endomorphisms are the identity on
V_{*}\,
.
The restrictions of
E
and
F
to other eigenspaces are then denoted as

E_{-},F_{+}:V_{0}\rightarrow V_{*}
and
E_{+},F_{-}:V_{*}\rightarrow V_{0}\,
. They form a representation of the small quantum group iff

(C.1)

\displaystyle E_{+}E_{-}=F_{-}F_{+}=0\quad\mbox{and}\quad E_{+}F_{+}=F_{-}E_{-}\qquad

\displaystyle\mbox{ on }V_{0}

\displaystyle\mbox{and}

\displaystyle E_{-}E_{+}=F_{+}F_{-}=E_{-}F_{-}=F_{+}E_{+}=0\qquad

\displaystyle\mbox{ on }V_{*}\,.

This type of reduction of representations of
U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
to a quiver with relations as in (
C.1
) extends to all roots of
unity as shown, for example, in
[
39
]
. The representation given by
the
E_{\pm}
and
F_{\pm}
as above is
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant if and only if there are isomorphisms
W_{0}\in\mathrm{GL}(V_{0})

and
W_{*}\in\mathrm{GL}(V_{*})
such that

(C.2)

W_{0}E_{+}W_{*}^{-1}=F_{-}\,,\quad W_{*}E_{-}W_{0}^{-1}=-F_{+}\,,\quad W_{*}F_{+}W_{0}^{-1}=E_{-}\,,\quad\mbox{and}\quad W_{0}F_{-}W_{*}^{-1}=-E_{+}

implying, in particular,
\mathrm{rank}(E_{+})=\mathrm{rank}(F_{-})
and
\mathrm{rank}(E_{-})=\mathrm{rank}(F_{+})\,
.

It is not hard to construct maps that fulfill (
C.1
) but violate (
C.2
). For example,
setting
E_{+}=F_{-}=0
automatically solves all equations in (
C.1
) so that any choice of maps

E_{-},F_{+}:V_{0}\rightarrow V_{*}
produces a representation. The residual representation theory is, thus, equivalent to that
of the (2) Kronecker quiver, which is tame and for which the indecomposable modules are classified
[
10
, Theorem 4.3.2]
.

Kronecker’s classification includes a generic family in which
\dim(V_{0})=\dim(V_{*})
and one of the maps can be chosen as the identity matrix and the other an indecomposable rational form. For example, if
\mathbb{k}=\mathbb{C}
the latter implies an indecomposable Jordan block
\,J=\kappa\mathbb{1}+N
, where
N
is maximally nilpotent. It is not hard to check that this representation is weakly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant if and only if
\kappa^{2}=-1\,
, again singling out a finite set from an infinite parameter space.

For the second family in the classification, the dimensions of
V_{0}
and
V_{*}
differ by one and there is exactly one representation for each such choice of dimensions.
Bases
\{v^{0}_{i}\}
of
V_{0}
and
\{v^{*}_{i}\}
of
V_{*}

may be chosen such that
E_{-}v^{0}_{i}=v^{*}_{i}
and
F_{+}v^{0}_{i}=v^{*}_{i+1}
or
F_{+}v^{0}_{i}=v^{*}_{i-1}\,
.
These special cases are indeed weakly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant. The
W_{0}
and
W_{*}
may be chosen as anti-diagonal matrices with alternating
+1
and
-1
entries.

Note that if we require representations to lift to a larger (unrolled) quantum group that contains the element
H
as in (
3.10
), the generic family is excluded unless
\kappa=0\,
(which does not yield a weakly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant module due to the rank condition). In this situation, however, the notion of weak
\mathscr{A}
-equivariance on the larger algebra implies
also
-\bar{H}=\mathsf{M}\bar{H}\mathsf{M}^{-1}
since
\mathit{\Gamma}(H)=-H\,
, implying symmetry of
H
-weights around
0
. The latter is easily broken by shifts
\bar{H}\mapsto\bar{H}+m\mathscr{k}\mathbb{1}
, producing infinite families of lifts of a representation that are not weakly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant.

For irreducible representations arising from sufficiently small
dominant highest weights (in a respective principal affine Weyl alcove)
one may expect weak
\mathscr{A}
-equivariance to apply based on the original
constructions of quantum Weyl elements. In the
U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})

situation above, this corresponds to the trivial solution of
(
C.1
) and (
C.2
) in which all maps are zero.

Finally, we note that the standard projective representation in the special
U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
case is in fact weakly
\mathscr{A}
-equivariant. In terms of the maps
above it is given in a suitable basis by matrices

E_{+}=\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\
1&0\end{bmatrix}\,,\;\;E_{-}=\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\
1&0\end{bmatrix}\,,\;\;F_{+}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\
0&0\end{bmatrix}\,,\;\;\mbox{ and }\;\;F_{-}=\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\
0&1\end{bmatrix}\,.

The conditions (
C.2
) are then solved, for example, by
W_{0}=\mathbb{1}

and

W_{*}=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\
1&0\end{bmatrix}\,
.

Appendix D
Integral Form of Coalgebras

We introduce an additional normalization
\hat{X}_{\alpha}
of the De Concini-Procesi singularized power generators
\breve{X}_{\alpha}\,
, which entails integral coproduct expressions in our formulae for types
\mathsf{A}_{n}
and
\mathsf{B}_{2}
. Notice from (
8.7
) that the singularized generator
\breve{X}_{(iji)}
has a coproduct over the Gauss integers
\mathbb{Z}[\scalebox{.75}{$\sqrt{-1}\,$}]
when
\ell
is even. Thus, the integral coordinate rings arise as Hopf subalgebras of
U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{g})
in these types. These integral forms also support simplified computations in future work.

In type
\mathsf{A}_{n}
, we gave in Lemma
7.9
a formula for the coproduct of generators
X_{i,j}

(D.1)

\Delta(X_{i,j})=\sum_{k=i}^{j}b_{k}X_{i,k}\otimes L_{i,k}X_{k,j}\;,

where
\;b_{k}=(\zeta^{-1}-\zeta)^{\ell}\zeta^{\binom{\ell}{2}}\;
for
i<k<j
and
b_{i}=b_{j}=1\,
. Replacing all instances of
X_{\alpha}
with the singular generator
\breve{X}_{\alpha}
removes the coefficient
(\zeta^{-1}-\zeta)^{\ell}
from
b_{k}
. If we set
\hat{X}_{\alpha}=\zeta^{\binom{\ell}{2}}\breve{X}_{\alpha}=(\zeta^{-1}-\zeta)^{\ell}\zeta^{\binom{\ell}{2}}X_{\alpha}
, then we obtain a coproduct formula in which all nonzero coefficients are
1
.

(D.2)

\Delta(\hat{X}_{i,j})=\sum_{k=i}^{j}\hat{X}_{i,k}\otimes L_{i,k}\hat{X}_{k,j}

More generally, set
\hat{E}_{i}^{k}=\zeta_{i}^{\binom{k}{2}}\breve{E}_{i}^{k}
, then write
\hat{X}_{i}=\hat{E}_{i}^{{\ell_{i}}}
. The coproduct formulae of Proposition
8.1
have simpler presentations using the rescaled singularized generators

(D.3)

\displaystyle\begin{aligned} \mathllap{\Delta(\hat{X}_{(iji)})}&=1\otimes\hat{X}_{(iji)}+\hat{X}_{i}\otimes L_{i}\hat{X}_{j}^{\mathfrak{d}}+\hat{X}_{(iji)}\otimes L_{i}L_{j}^{\mathfrak{d}}\,,\\
&\qquad+\delta_{\mathfrak{d},2}\cdot 2\cdot(-1)^{\ell_{j}}\hat{X}_{(ij)}\otimes L_{i}L_{j}\hat{X}_{j}\end{aligned}

(D.4)

\displaystyle\begin{aligned} \mathllap{\Delta(\hat{X}_{(ij)})}&=1\otimes\hat{X}_{(ij)}+\hat{X}_{i}^{\mathfrak{n}}\otimes L_{i}^{\mathfrak{n}}\hat{X}_{j}+\hat{X}_{(ij)}\otimes L_{i}^{\mathfrak{n}}L_{j}\\
&\qquad+\delta_{\mathfrak{n},2}\cdot 2\cdot\zeta^{\binom{\ell+1}{2}}\hat{X}_{i}\otimes L_{i}\hat{X}_{(iji)}\,.\end{aligned}

These follow from the observations
\hat{X}_{j}^{\mathfrak{d}}=\zeta_{j}^{\binom{\ell}{2}}\breve{X}_{j}^{\mathfrak{d}}=(-1)^{\ell+1}\breve{X}_{j}^{\mathfrak{d}}
and
\hat{X}_{i}^{\mathfrak{n}}=\zeta^{\binom{2{\ell_{j}}}{2}}\breve{X}_{i}^{\mathfrak{n}}
.
Note also that
\delta_{\mathfrak{d},2}\zeta^{\binom{\ell}{2}}=\delta_{\mathfrak{d},2}(-\zeta)^{-{\ell_{j}}}
,

\delta_{\mathfrak{n},2}\zeta^{2\binom{\ell}{2}}=1
,

\delta_{\mathfrak{n},2}\zeta^{\binom{\ell}{2}+{\ell_{j}}}=\delta_{\mathfrak{n},2}\zeta^{\binom{\ell}{2}+\ell}=\delta_{\mathfrak{n},2}\zeta^{\binom{\ell+1}{2}}
are all valued in
\{-1,0,1\}
.

The automorphism
\mho
is given for certain power generators in (
6.52
) and (
6.54
). Here, we regard it as a factor of the antipode, which takes values over the same ring as the coproduct. We deduce integrality for the
\hat{X}_{\alpha}
from the respective equations.

(D.5)

\displaystyle(-1)^{\ell}\hat{X}_{(ji)}

\displaystyle=\,\zeta_{j}^{\ell}\hat{X}_{a_{m-1}}\,+\,(-1)^{\ell}\hat{X}_{j}^{\mathfrak{d}}\hat{X}_{i}\,+\,(1-\delta_{\mathfrak{d},1})\cdot\mathsf{e}\cdot(-1)^{\ell}\cdot T_{1}\vskip 22.76219pt

\displaystyle\mbox{where}

\displaystyle T_{1}=\begin{cases}(-1)^{\ell_{j}+1}\hat{X}_{j}\hat{X}_{(ij)}&\mathsf{e}=2\\
\zeta_{j}^{2\binom{{\ell_{j}}}{2}}\hat{X}_{j}^{2}\hat{X}_{(ij)}\,+\,\hat{X}_{j}\hat{X}_{(ijij)}&\mathsf{e}=3\,,\end{cases}

(D.6)

\displaystyle(-1)^{\mathsf{e}\ell_{j}}\hat{X}_{b_{m-1}}

\displaystyle=\,\zeta_{j}^{\ell_{j}}\hat{X}_{(ij)}\,+\,(-1)^{\mathfrak{n}\cdot\ell}\hat{X}_{j}\hat{X}_{i}^{\mathfrak{n}}\,+\,\delta_{\mathfrak{d},1}\cdot(1-\delta_{\mathsf{e},1})\cdot\mathsf{e}\cdot(-1)^{\ell}\cdot T_{2}\vskip 22.76219pt

\displaystyle\mbox{where}

\displaystyle T_{2}=\begin{cases}\zeta^{\ell}\hat{X}_{(iji)}\hat{X}_{i}&\mathsf{e}=2\\
\hat{X}_{(iji)}\hat{X}_{i}\,+\,(-1)^{\ell+1}\hat{X}_{(ijiji)}\hat{X}_{i}^{2}&\mathsf{e}=3\,.\end{cases}

The integrality of these expressions suggests that the normalized generators above produce integral coproducts for all Lie types and roots of unity.

Conjecture D.1
.

Let
z\in\mathscr{W}^{*}_{\mkern-2.0mu\mathfrak{m}}
. The set of
\hat{X}_{w}
for
w\leq_{R}z
generate a
\mathbb{Z}
-Hopf subalgebra of
U_{\zeta}(\mathfrak{g})
.
